text:
Nombre del paciente: Mateo Alejandro Vásquez Rodríguez
Apodo usado por la familia: Teo
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de agosto de 2021
Edad cronológica en la evaluación: 4;2
Sexo: masculino
Número de expediente: MV-20538
Número de Medicaid: 784215630B
Fechas de la evaluación: 20 de octubre de 2025 y 22 de octubre de 2025
Fecha del informe: 3 de noviembre de 2025
Idioma primario del hogar: español; idioma de exposición secundaria: inglés
Remitido por: Dra. Hannah Nguyen, pediatra
CDSA / Agencia de remisión: Piedmont Regional CDSA
Coordinadora de servicios: Rachel Kim
Clínica: Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC (abreviado CPSLT)
Dirección de la clínica: 482 Birchwood Lane, Suite 200, Apex, NC 27502
Teléfono de la clínica: (919) 555-0148
Correo electrónico de la clínica: athompson@carolinapediatricspeech.com
Sitio web: www.carolinapediatricspeech.com
Terapeuta del habla y lenguaje: Avery Thompson, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingüe español-inglés
Intérprete certificado presente: Diego Fuentes
Centro de cuidado infantil: Little Sprouts Early Learning Center

MOTIVO DE LA REMISIÓN

Mateo fue remitido a Carolina Pediatric Speech por su pediatra, la Dra. Hannah Nguyen, después de una visita de control de los cuatro años en la que la familia expresó preocupación por el lenguaje expresivo y la claridad del habla del niño. Su madre, Lucía Rodríguez Fernández, reportó que Mateo usa oraciones cortas, omite palabras pequeñas y con frecuencia es difícil de entender tanto para la familia como para personas fuera del hogar. Su padre, Hugo Vásquez Ibarra, añadió que Mateo se frustra cuando no logra comunicarse y a veces empuja o llora en lugar de hablar.

La maestra principal de Mateo en Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, la maestra Carmen, también envió una nota de preocupación. Ella observa que Mateo participa poco en el círculo de conversación y que su amigo Ethan a menudo habla por él. La asistente de la clase, Miss Ana, notó que Mateo sigue instrucciones de un solo paso pero se pierde con instrucciones de dos pasos. El especialista en desarrollo motor que visita el centro, Mr. Tom, no reportó preocupaciones de motricidad gruesa ni fina.

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Mateo nació a las 38 semanas de gestación mediante parto vaginal en el WakeMed Cary Hospital. Su peso al nacer fue de 3,200 gramos (7 libras, 1 onza) y sus puntuaciones de Apgar fueron de 8 y 9 al minuto y a los cinco minutos, respectivamente. El embarazo fue descrito por Lucía como sin complicaciones mayores, aunque reportó presión arterial elevada durante el tercer trimestre que fue manejada médicamente sin necesidad de hospitalización adicional.

El historial médico de Mateo incluye tres episodios de otitis media entre los dos y tres años de edad, tratados con antibióticos. No ha requerido tubos de ventilación (miringotomía). Una evaluación auditiva realizada el 12 de junio de 2024 en el consultorio de la Dra. Nguyen mostró audición dentro de límites normales bilateralmente. No hay historial de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones significativas ni cirugías. Mateo toma actualmente un multivitamínico diario y no tiene alergias conocidas a medicamentos.

Mateo comenzó a recibir servicios de intervención temprana a través de Piedmont Regional CDSA en marzo de 2024 después de una evaluación de desarrollo que identificó un retraso leve en el área de comunicación. Su Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) incluye actualmente el Resultado 2, enfocado en el seguimiento de instrucciones de dos pasos, y el Resultado 3, enfocado en el aumento de la longitud de sus enunciados. La coordinadora de servicios, Rachel Kim, ha facilitado la comunicación entre la familia y los proveedores durante este proceso.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo vive con su madre, Lucía Rodríguez Fernández, su padrastro, Marcos Jiménez Soto, y su hermana mayor, Camila Vásquez Rodríguez. Su padre biológico, Hugo Vásquez Ibarra, vive en una residencia separada dentro del mismo condado y tiene contacto regular con Mateo los fines de semana. La familia reside en 1147 Willow Creek Road, Garner, NC 27529, dentro del condado de Wake.

En el hogar se habla principalmente español. Lucía reporta que ella y Marcos usan español con los niños casi todo el tiempo, mientras que Mateo escucha inglés principalmente en el centro de cuidado infantil y a través de programas de televisión. Camila, quien tiene seis años y asiste a kinder, está adquiriendo el inglés con mayor rapidez y ocasionalmente traduce para su hermano menor cuando juegan con vecinos de habla inglesa.

En cuanto al historial de empleo de la familia, Lucía trabaja actualmente como cajera en la tienda de abarrotes Harris Teeter; antes de este empleo trabajó durante dos años en el restaurante El Rancho Mexican Restaurant, donde conoció a varios de los vecinos que ahora cuidan a los niños ocasionalmente. Hugo trabaja en la planta de fabricación de muebles Triad Furniture Manufacturing como operador de maquinaria; previamente trabajó en el servicio de limpieza Sparkle Clean Cleaning Service durante el turno nocturno. Marcos, el padrastro de Mateo, trabaja actualmente en la granja Sunrise Dairy Farm, y antes de mudarse a Carolina del Norte trabajó para la compañía de construcción Ortiz Brothers Construction Company.

Debido a los horarios de trabajo de ambos padres, Mateo y Camila pasan las tardes con una vecina de confianza a quien la familia llama doña Lupe. Ella cocina para los niños, los ayuda con tareas sencillas y, según Lucía, habla con ellos principalmente en español, aunque mezcla algunas palabras en inglés que aprendió trabajando anteriormente en una tienda local. La familia recibe apoyo nutricional a través de WIC y ha participado en talleres para padres ofrecidos por Smart Start de Wake County.

La mascota de la familia es un perro llamado Rocky, al cual Mateo menciona con frecuencia durante las sesiones de juego y a quien usa como motivador para practicar vocabulario de animales y acciones.

No se reportan otros retrasos de lenguaje en la familia inmediata. Hugo menciona que él mismo tuvo dificultades leves de pronunciación de niño en México, pero que se resolvieron sin terapia formal. No hay historial familiar de trastornos del espectro autista, pérdida auditiva genética ni trastornos de aprendizaje diagnosticados.

OBSERVACIÓN CONDUCTUAL

Durante ambas sesiones de evaluación, realizadas en las oficinas de CPSLT en Apex, NC, Mateo se mostró inicialmente tímido pero se adaptó rápidamente al ambiente de juego estructurado. Mantuvo atención conjunta de manera consistente y respondió bien al reforzamiento positivo y a los descansos breves con movimiento. Su nivel de atención fue apropiado para su edad durante tareas de quince a veinte minutos. No se observaron conductas repetitivas, dificultades sensoriales significativas ni problemas de interacción social que sugirieran preocupaciones dentro del espectro autista.

El intérprete, Diego Fuentes, facilitó la comunicación con la familia durante la entrevista inicial y la revisión de resultados, asegurando que Lucía y Hugo comprendieran completamente los procedimientos y pudieran hacer preguntas en su idioma preferido.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas, complementadas con observación clínica, muestra de lenguaje espontáneo y entrevista con los padres:

1. Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition, Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish)
2. Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
3. Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA) — subpruebas de Fonología y Morfosintaxis
4. Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo en español e inglés, analizada con codificación tipo SALT
5. Lista de verificación informal de procesos fonológicos (enfoque de Cycles)

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

PLS-5 Spanish:
Comprensión Auditiva: puntuación estándar de 82, percentil 12, intervalo de confianza del 95% de 76–88
Comunicación Expresiva: puntuación estándar de 76, percentil 5, intervalo de confianza del 95% de 70–82
Puntuación Total del Lenguaje: puntuación estándar de 78, percentil 7
Edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo: 30 meses

GFTA-3 (Sonidos en Palabras):
Puntuación estándar: 73, percentil 4

BESA — Fonología:
Puntuación en español dentro del rango esperado para la edad; se observaron procesos fonológicos persistentes, incluyendo gliding de /r/ y /ɾ/ (producidos como [w]) y simplificación de grupos consonánticos (por ejemplo, "pego" por "pero", y "flol" por "flor")

BESA — Morfosintaxis:
Desempeño por debajo del rango esperado en ambos idiomas; omisión frecuente de artículos y marcadores de plural en español, y omisión de la cópula ("is/are") en inglés

Durante la muestra de lenguaje, Mateo produjo enunciados de una longitud media de aproximadamente 3.2 palabras por enunciado en español. Se codificaron varios errores como palabras con error ([EW]) debido a omisiones de morfemas gramaticales. En inglés, produjo "wion" por "lion" y "wed" por "red", consistente con el patrón de gliding observado en español.

En cuanto a producción de sonidos específicos, Mateo logró producir el fonema /s/ correctamente en posición inicial en 8 de 10 intentos (80%) con clave verbal mínima, pero requirió clave moderada para producir /ɾ/ en palabras como "carro" y "pero". En posición final de palabra, logró /s/ correctamente en 3 de 5 intentos (60%) sin ayuda.

Su madre completó un cuestionario de desarrollo comunicativo que arrojó resultados consistentes con las observaciones clínicas, confirmando que la dificultad de Mateo se presenta en ambos idiomas del hogar y no es exclusiva de un solo idioma, lo cual apoya un diagnóstico de trastorno primario del lenguaje en lugar de una diferencia típica asociada al bilingüismo.

IMPRESIONES DIAGNÓSTICAS

Con base en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, la observación clínica, el análisis de la muestra de lenguaje y la información proporcionada por la familia y el personal educativo, Mateo presenta un trastorno mixto de lenguaje receptivo-expresivo con un componente fonológico significativo, presente en ambos idiomas del hogar. Esto es consistente con ICD-10 F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo) con un diagnóstico secundario de F80.0 (trastorno fonológico).

El perfil de Mateo no es atribuible únicamente a la exposición a dos idiomas; su desempeño está por debajo de lo esperado en ambos idiomas en comparación con normas monolingües y bilingües apropiadas. Su inteligibilidad general se estima en aproximadamente 60% para oyentes familiares y menos del 40% para oyentes no familiares, lo cual representa un impacto funcional significativo en su participación en el centro de cuidado infantil y en el hogar.

Los servicios de evaluación de hoy fueron codificados bajo CPT 92523 (evaluación del habla y de la producción de sonidos del habla con evaluación del lenguaje), y se anticipa que los servicios de tratamiento continuo se codificarán bajo CPT 92507.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda terapia de habla y lenguaje individual dos veces por semana, sesiones de 30 minutos, en modalidad bilingüe (español e inglés), a través de Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC.

2. El plan de tratamiento incorporará el enfoque PROMPT para abordar los patrones de gliding y simplificación de grupos consonánticos, junto con el enfoque de Cycles para el tratamiento de procesos fonológicos múltiples.

3. Para el desarrollo de morfosintaxis y longitud de enunciado, se recomienda incorporar estrategias del método Hanen durante las sesiones y capacitar a Lucía y Marcos en técnicas de expansión y modelado lingüístico dentro del hogar.

4. Se recomienda continuar la colaboración con Piedmont Regional CDSA para actualizar el IFSP, revisando el progreso hacia el Resultado 2 y el Resultado 3 en la próxima reunión de revisión, programada para el 15 de enero de 2026.

5. Se recomienda comunicación continua con la maestra Carmen y Miss Ana en Little Sprouts Early Learning Center para generalizar estrategias de comunicación dentro del aula, incluyendo el uso de instrucciones simplificadas y espera estructurada para dar oportunidad a que Mateo se comunique antes de que su amigo Ethan responda por él.

6. Se recomienda una reevaluación formal del progreso en aproximadamente seis meses, o antes si el equipo clínico lo considera necesario.

7. Se sugiere que la familia continúe fomentando el uso del español en el hogar, ya que el bilingüismo no es la causa del retraso de Mateo y debe mantenerse como un recurso valioso para la familia y el desarrollo a largo plazo del niño.

Cualquier pregunta sobre este informe puede dirigirse a Avery Thompson, M.S., CCC-SLP, a través del correo electrónico athompson@carolinapediatricspeech.com, por teléfono al (919) 555-0148, o visitando www.carolinapediatricspeech.com para más información sobre los servicios de CPSLT.

Agradezco la colaboración de la familia y del personal de Little Sprouts Early Learning Center durante este proceso de evaluación.

Atentamente,

Avery Thompson, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje Bilingüe
Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC

Reason for Referral Evaluation Type: Comprehensive Speech-Language Evaluation Clinic/Program: Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Client Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández Preferred Name: Teo
Date of Birth: August 14, 2022 Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Evaluation Dates: October 3, 2026 and October 6, 2026 Report Date: October 10, 2026
Medicaid ID: MA8821046R Record/Case ID: SLP-2026-1142
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Hernández Morales (mother)  Parent/Guardian: Jorge Cruz Delgado (father)
Home Address: 118 Rosemary Lane, Hope Mills, Cumberland County, NC 28348
Phone: (910) 555-2214 Email: lucia.hernandezm82@gmail.com
Primary Home Language: Spanish Secondary Language: English (emerging, school exposure)
Referral Source: Dr. Anand Patel, pediatrics, Cape Fear Valley Medical Center
School District: Cumberland County Schools School: Mintz Elementary School
Classroom/Teacher: Pre-K, Ms. Patterson  Teaching Assistant: Sra. Noemí Álvarez
Examiner: Marisol Ortega Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP  Bilingual Spanish-English Speech-Language Pathologist
Interpreter: Not applicable; examiner is bilingual and testing was conducted in both languages.

Reason for Referral

Teo is a 4;2-year-old boy referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by his pediatrician, Dr. Patel, following concerns raised at his four-year well-child visit at Cape Fear Valley Medical Center. His mother, Lucía, reports that Teo is difficult to understand even for close family, and that he has started to avoid talking at school since starting Pre-K this fall at Mintz Elementary School. Ms. Patterson, his classroom teacher, referred a note home in September stating that Teo "does not initiate with peers and gets frustrated quickly during circle time." Lucía stated, "En la casa habla bastante, pero en la escuela casi no dice nada." The family was also referred through the Cumberland County Partnership for Children (Smart Start) after a developmental screening flagged possible delays. Teo's case had previously been opened with the Southern Regional CDSA for early intervention services under IFSP Outcome 2 (communication) and Outcome 3 (social-emotional), but services lapsed when the family transitioned out of the Cumberland County Early Head Start program at Kiddie Kampus Early Head Start Center in Fayetteville.

Background Information

Teo lives with both parents and his older brother, Sol, age six, in Hope Mills. The family also receives support through Cumberland County WIC and has an open case with Cumberland County DSS related to housing assistance. Jorge works full time at Builders Supply of Fayetteville, and Lucía works part time cleaning houses. Child care during the day, when Lucía works, is provided by a family friend, Flor Jiménez, who watches Teo along with his cousins Camila and Andrés most afternoons. The family dog, Canela, is frequently mentioned by Teo as a comfort during tantrums; Lucía reported that he "le habla más a la perrita que a la gente."

Birth and Medical History

Teo was born at 39 weeks gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery at Cape Fear Valley Medical Center on August 14, 2022. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz. Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Lucía reported no complications during pregnancy or delivery, and no NICU stay was required. Teo passed his newborn hearing screening prior to discharge. Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media between ages one and three, with four documented episodes treated with antibiotics; tympanostomy tubes were placed at 26 months by Dr. Grace Lindqvist, ENT, with resolution of chronic effusion. A follow-up audiological evaluation in March 2025 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. Teo has no diagnosed syndromes, seizure history, or significant illnesses outside of frequent ear infections. Current diagnostic coding on file from his pediatric visit includes ICD-10 F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and ICD-10 H65.3 (chronic otitis media, resolved), with today's evaluation billed under CPT 92523.

Developmental milestones were reported as mildly delayed for expressive language. Lucía reported that Teo said his first words around 18 months, with "mamá" and "papá" as early productions, but did not combine two words until closer to age three. Gross and fine motor milestones (sitting, walking, self-feeding) were within normal limits per parent report, with independent walking at 13 months.

Family and Language History

Teo's home language environment is primarily Spanish. Jorge was born in Veracruz, Mexico, and Lucía was born in Monterrey, Mexico; both moved to North Carolina before Teo was born. Spanish is spoken approximately 85% of the time at home, with some English mixed in from television, his brother Sol's school vocabulary, and visits with cousins. Sol is in first grade and is described by his parents as "bien hablador en los dos idiomas," serving informally as a language model and occasional interpreter for Teo with English-speaking peers.

Lucía described Teo's communication style at home: "Él me entiende todo lo que le digo, en español y hasta un poco en inglés, pero cuando él quiere decir algo, se le traba y se frustra." She noted that strangers and even some family members, including his paternal grandmother who visits from out of state, have difficulty understanding his speech. His babysitter, Flor, reported that Teo frequently uses gestures and pulls adults by the hand to request things rather than using words, particularly when tired or around unfamiliar people. Flor also shared that Teo plays well one-on-one with his cousin Camila, who is close to him in age, but tends to withdraw in larger groups, including at family gatherings where cousins Andrés and his younger sister are present.

At school, Ms. Patterson reported that Teo is generally well behaved but quiet, and that he has one classmate, Dylan, with whom he sometimes plays during outdoor time, though their interactions are mostly nonverbal (chasing, pointing). Another classmate, Emma W., was described as trying to include Teo in group activities, but he often does not respond verbally. Ms. Patterson stated that during calendar time, when children are asked to say the day and weather aloud, Teo "just shakes his head no and won't try," which she interprets as a mix of language difficulty and shyness.

Educational History

Teo began Pre-K at Mintz Elementary School in August 2026, within Cumberland County Schools. Prior to this, he attended Kiddie Kampus Early Head Start Center from roughly age one through three, where early developmental concerns were first noted by staff and a referral was made to Southern Regional CDSA for an IFSP evaluation around November 2024. Speech-language services through that IFSP were approved but attendance was inconsistent due to transportation barriers; the family reports that the Cumberland County Partnership for Children helped coordinate a bus voucher for a period, but services ultimately ended when the family's address changed and the case was not transferred promptly. No formal services have been received in the past eight months. The current referral is intended to establish updated eligibility, potentially through the local preschool exceptional children's program at Mintz Elementary School, as well as continued private therapy at Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC.

Assessment Procedures and Behavioral Observations

Testing was conducted across two sessions. The first session took place on October 3, 2026 in the clinic office, beginning at 9:15 a.m. and ending at 11:40 a.m., with a short snack break at approximately 10:20 a.m.. The second session was conducted at Mintz Elementary School on October 6, 2026, from 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m., in a quiet room adjacent to Ms. Patterson's classroom, coordinated with the school's exceptional children's coordinator. Both parents were present for portions of the first session; Jorge left around 10:00 a.m. for work, while Lucía remained for the full session and provided informal translation support and background information throughout.

Teo separated from his mother without distress and engaged readily with the examiner using a mix of gestures, single words, and occasional two-word combinations. Rapport was established quickly using toy animals, including a stuffed dog that reminded him of his own dog, Canela, which he mentioned spontaneously ("mi perrita Canela es más grande"). Attention and engagement were adequate throughout both sessions, though Teo showed increased frustration and task refusal during more structured expressive language tasks, particularly toward the end of the first session. He was observed to use jargon and unintelligible strings of sounds when attempting to describe events, for example when trying to tell the examiner about a trip to visit his cousins Camila and Andrés.

Speech was characterized by frequent sound substitutions and omissions that reduced overall intelligibility, estimated at approximately 50% intelligible to an unfamiliar listener in connected speech, and closer to 70% intelligible to familiar listeners such as Lucía and Flor. Examples of speech sound errors included fronting of velars, e.g., Teo produced "tasa" for the target word "taza", and "pato" for the target "plato", indicating cluster reduction. He substituted [w] for the Spanish tap /ɾ/ in several words, producing "paweta" for the target "paleta". In English, he substituted /k/ with /t/ in initial position, producing "tat" for "cat". Stimulability was noted for several sounds with moderate cues, and he was able to approximate the target /ɾ/ in isolation with maximal cues but not in words.

Standardized and Informal Assessment Results

Test Name                              Language   Standard Score   Percentile Rank
Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Auditory Comprehension   Spanish    82              12th percentile
PLS-5, Expressive Communication                                           Spanish    76              5th percentile
PLS-5, Total Language Score                                               Spanish    78              7th percentile
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax                 Bilingual  79              8th percentile
BESA, Semantics                                                           Bilingual  85              16th percentile
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)              English    73              4th percentile
Goodness of Intelligibility rating                                        Both       N/A                 2 of 5

On the PLS-5, administered primarily in Spanish with English probes given his dual-language exposure, Teo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 82 (12th percentile), within the low average to below average range, and an Expressive Communication standard score of 76 (5th percentile), falling below average. His Total Language score of 78 (7th percentile, age equivalent 2;9) indicates a significant gap between his chronological age of 4;2 and his functional expressive language skills.

On the BESA, which accounts for bilingual exposure, Teo scored in the below-average range for Morphosyntax (79, 8th percentile) with frequent omission of grammatical markers in both languages, such as article omission in Spanish ("quiero pelota" instead of "quiero la pelota") and verb tense errors in English ("he go house" for "he went home"). His Semantics score of 85 (16th percentile) was closer to average, suggesting relatively stronger vocabulary knowledge than grammatical or expressive formulation skills.

On the GFTA-3, administered in English, Teo obtained a standard score of 73 (4th percentile), indicating a moderate-to-severe articulation delay relative to same-age peers. Error patterns included cluster reduction, velar fronting, and gliding of liquids, consistent with errors noted in connected speech sampling in Spanish. An informal Spanish phonology screening using single-word naming showed similar patterns, with consistent substitution of /k/ and /g/ for anterior sounds in word-initial position and difficulty with the Spanish tap /ɾ/ and trill /r/ across contexts.

A parent rating scale completed by Lucía and Jorge independently showed consistent concerns regarding expressive vocabulary, sentence length, and intelligibility, with both parents rating social communication (eye contact, turn-taking, responding to name) as a relative strength, consistent with observations during testing. Jorge added during a phone follow-up on October 7, 2026, "En el trabajo a veces lo llevo y juega bien con los hijos de mis compañeros, no es tímido, solo que no le entienden lo que dice."

A brief oral-motor examination revealed structures and function within normal limits, with no evidence of dysarthria or significant oral-motor weakness. Hearing was reported as within normal limits per the most recent audiological evaluation on file, and no concerns were raised regarding hearing status during today's sessions.

Clinical Impressions

Teo presents with a bilingual speech sound disorder and expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a true communication disorder rather than solely second-language acquisition, as deficits are present in his dominant home language (Spanish) as well as English. His receptive language skills, while below age expectations, are relatively stronger than his expressive skills, suggesting a primarily expressive profile with secondary mild receptive involvement. His speech intelligibility deficits, characterized by consistent phonological process use (fronting, cluster reduction, gliding), are significant enough to interfere with communication across both familiar and unfamiliar listeners and likely contribute to the social withdrawal and reduced verbal participation reported by Ms. Patterson at school.

Given his history of chronic otitis media and tympanostomy tube placement, it is possible that early fluctuating hearing loss contributed to delayed phonological development, though current hearing is within normal limits. The combination of speech sound disorder and language delay places Teo at risk for later academic difficulties, including early literacy challenges, if not addressed promptly. His relative social strengths, including appropriate eye contact, turn-taking attempts, and interest in peers such as Dylan and Emma W., are encouraging prognostic indicators.

Diagnoses

1. Speech Sound Disorder, bilingual (Spanish/English), moderate-to-severe, ICD-10 F80.0
2. Expressive Language Disorder, with mild receptive involvement, bilingual, ICD-10 F80.1
3. History of chronic otitis media with effusion, resolved, ICD-10 H65.3

Recommendations

1. Teo qualifies for speech-language therapy services based on standardized testing, clinical observation, and parent and teacher report. It is recommended that he receive individual speech-language therapy two times per week for 30-minute sessions, targeting both Spanish and English, delivered by a bilingual provider when possible.

2. Referral is recommended to the preschool exceptional children's program at Mintz Elementary School within Cumberland County Schools for consideration of school-based services, coordinated with Ms. Patterson and the school's exceptional children's team.

3. Continued coordination with Southern Regional CDSA is recommended to formally close or update Teo's prior IFSP record, given the lapse in services, and to ensure a smooth transition to school-based or private outpatient therapy.

4. The family should continue contact with the Cumberland County Partnership for Children (Smart Start) for possible transportation assistance and family support resources, and may benefit from reconnecting with Cumberland County DSS regarding eligibility for additional services given their current circumstances.

5. Continued support through Cumberland County WIC is recommended to continue, as nutrition and early childhood supports may indirectly benefit overall development.

6. A home program emphasizing a Hanen-based approach is recommended for Lucía and Jorge, to increase language stimulation opportunities and modeling within daily routines, in Spanish primarily, with English modeling incorporated through Sol and preschool exposure.

7. A PROMPT-informed approach to articulation intervention is recommended given the motor-based nature of several of Teo's error patterns, to be used alongside traditional articulation drill work targeting /k/, /g/, and /ɾ/.

8. Re-evaluation of speech and language skills is recommended in approximately six months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan, including repeat administration of the PLS-5 and GFTA-3.

9. Caregivers, including Flor, are encouraged to continue using both languages naturally at home and during child care, expanding on Teo's attempts at communication rather than correcting errors directly, and to narrate daily routines (mealtime, play with Canela, outings with cousins) to increase language input.

This evaluation was conducted and this report was written by the undersigned bilingual speech-language pathologist.

INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE / SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Agency (long):  Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Discapacidades del Piedmont   Agency (short):  CDSA Piedmont
Service Coordination Agency (long):  Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Infantiles del Condado de Alamance   Short form:  ACSICA
Provider/Clinic:  Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC   Clinician:  María Elena Sosa, M.S., CCC-SLP
Child's Name:  Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández   Nickname:  Teo   Child ID:  CDSA-0471839   Medicaid ID:  5847203619A
Date of Birth:  June 14, 2022   Date of Evaluation:  September 29, 2026   Report Date:  October 3, 2026
Address:  118 Candlewood Lane, Mebane, Alamance County, NC  27302
Mother/Madre:  Lucía Fernanda Cruz Ramírez   Cell:  (336) 555-7812
Father/Padre:  Edgar Hernández López   Cell:  336.555.9034
Interpreter:  Juan Pablo Díaz   Service Coordinator:  Yolanda Martínez   SC Phone:  (336) 555-2201 ext. 14

Motivo de la Remisión / Reason for Referral:  Teo was referred by his pediatrician, Dr. Robert Chen of Alamance Pediatric Associates, after concerns about limited intelligibility and expressive delay were raised at his 4-year well-child visit. His mother, Lucía, contacted CDSA Piedmont directly on August 11, 2026, stating "no le entiendo casi nada de lo que dice, y en la guardería tampoco lo entienden." The family was already receiving service coordination through ACSICA for an active IFSP Outcome 2 related to expressive language, and Yolanda Martínez requested this update evaluation to inform the annual review.

Historia del Nacimiento / Birth History:  Teo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Alamance Regional Medical Center in Burlington, NC by vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. No NICU stay was reported. Lucía reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care through WIC, where the family has received nutritional support since Teo's infancy. Mother denied maternal illness, substance use, or complications during pregnancy or delivery.

Historia Médica / Medical History:  Current pediatrician is Dr. Robert Chen. Teo passed his newborn hearing screening and a repeat audiological evaluation on March 2, 2026 at UNC Health Audiology confirmed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. No history of chronic ear infections was reported, though Lucía noted "tuvo como dos infecciones de oído cuando era bebé, pero nada grave." Teo is not currently on any medications. He was seen by occupational therapist Dr. Amanda Lee for a fine motor screening in May 2026; results were within normal limits and OT services were not recommended. Medical diagnosis on file from Dr. Chen includes F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), which supports continued CDSA eligibility.

Historia Familiar y del Lenguaje / Family and Language History:  Teo lives with his mother, Lucía Fernanda Cruz Ramírez; his father, Edgar Hernández López; his older sister, Ximena Hernández, age 7;4; and his baby brother, Santiago Hernández, age 11 months. His paternal grandmother, Carmen López de Hernández, known in the home as "Abuela Carmen," lives in the household and provides primary daytime care three days per week. A maternal aunt, Rosa Cruz, and a family friend who babysits occasionally, Flor Ibarra, also provide child care support. The family reports a pet dog named Luna who Teo frequently talks about during sessions.

The home language environment is bilingual. Lucía reported, "en casa hablamos los dos idiomas, pero más español con los abuelos y más inglés con los maestros." Edgar stated that he speaks primarily Spanish with the children, while Lucía code-switches depending on context. Ximena is reportedly fluent and intelligible in both languages and often serves as an informal interpreter for Teo with peers, which the family and this clinician discussed as a pattern to monitor so that Teo continues developing his own expressive skills rather than relying on his sister.

Lucía works part-time at la tienda Dollar General near their home, with shifts that vary weekly. Edgar works full-time at la planta empacadora de carne Smithfield in Tar Heel, NC, typically on the overnight shift. Abuela Carmen previously worked at el restaurante El Bajío in Mebane but reduced her hours to help with childcare. Rosa Cruz works seasonally at la granja avícola Case Farms outside Burlington. A paternal uncle, referenced by the family but not evaluated, works for la compañía de construcción Ramírez, and a cousin works for el servicio de limpieza Brightway in Graham, NC. In English word order, these would be described as the Dollar General store, Smithfield Packing Plant, El Bajío Restaurant, Case Farms poultry farm, Ramirez Construction Company, and Brightway Cleaning Service, respectively.

Teo attends Little Steps Early Head Start Center in Mebane four days a week, enrolled through the Early Head Start program. His classroom teacher, Ms. Patricia Gómez, reports that Teo is social and affectionate but "struggles to make himself understood, especially with new words or longer sentences." Ms. Gómez noted a classmate, Bryson, often helps Teo during circle time by repeating his requests to the group. The family also receives family support services through Alamance Smart Start Partnership for Children and has an open case with Alamance County Department of Social Services, abbreviated locally as DSS, related to a prior housing assistance application; this is unrelated to any protective concerns.

Observaciones Conductuales / Behavioral Observations:  The evaluation session took place on September 29, 2026 from 9:15 a.m. to 10:45 a.m. at CDSA Piedmont's office located at 204 Westgate Drive, Suite B, Burlington, NC 27215. Lucía and Abuela Carmen were present for the session, along with interpreter Juan Pablo Díaz, who supported communication during portions of the parent interview conducted primarily in Spanish. Teo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and testing materials. He demonstrated a positive affect, frequent eye contact, and turn-taking within play, though his speech was frequently unintelligible to unfamiliar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

Teo used single words and occasional two-to-three-word combinations in both English and Spanish throughout the session. Code-switching was observed and appeared appropriate to context rather than reflecting confusion, for example requesting "more agua" and later independently self-correcting to "more water" when prompted by this clinician in English. He demonstrated phonological error patterns including final consonant deletion (producing "ca" for "cat"), cluster reduction ("poon" for "spoon"), and fronting of velars, substituting /t/ for /k/ in words such as "tar" for "car". Stimulability for /k/ in isolation was present with moderate cues, and he achieved 6/10 accuracy on imitated trials by the end of the session.

Pruebas Administradas y Resultados / Tests Administered and Results:

Test                                              Domain                          Standard Score    Percentile    Age Equivalent
Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5)       Auditory Comprehension          72              3rd          2;9
Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5)       Expressive Communication         65              1st          2;3
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)  Sounds-in-Words           68              2nd          2;11
Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3)  Receptive Language Index   74       4th          --
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA)            Spanish Morphosyntax Index        79              8th          --

On the PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension subtest, administered in English with Spanish supports per bilingual protocol, Teo obtained a standard score of 72 (3rd percentile), falling within the moderately delayed range. On Expressive Communication, he obtained a standard score of 65 (1st percentile), in the severely delayed range, consistent with parent and teacher concerns. His combined Total Language Score was 66, falling at the 1st percentile, with an age equivalent of 2;4.

Administration of the GFTA-3 yielded a raw score of 41 errors, converting to a standard score of 68 (2nd percentile). Percentage of Consonants Correct (PCC) was calculated at 62%, which is below age expectations. Stimulability testing showed that Teo could produce /k/, /g/, and final consonants in CV syllables with maximal cues, but accuracy dropped to 3/10 in connected speech.

The BESA was administered to evaluate Spanish language skills given the family's reported home language use. Teo's Spanish Morphosyntax score fell at the 8th percentile, somewhat stronger than his English scores but still below expectations for bilingual peers, suggesting a true language impairment affecting both languages rather than a language difference secondary to bilingual exposure alone.

Dynamic assessment of narrative retell, completed with support from interpreter Juan Pablo Díaz, showed Teo could sequence two of three events in a simple picture story with moderate cues, achieving 2/3 (approximately 67%) accuracy, below the expected 80% benchmark for his age.

Impresiones / Clinical Impressions:  Results indicate a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both English and Spanish, consistent with the medical diagnosis of F80.2 on file. Teo's phonological system shows multiple active error patterns limiting intelligibility across contexts, as reflected in his GFTA-3 results and consistent with the 62% PCC obtained during connected speech sampling. His bilingual profile shows relative strength in Spanish morphosyntax compared to English, though both languages fall below age expectations, ruling out typical bilingual second-language acquisition as the primary explanation for his difficulties. Teo continues to meet eligibility criteria for ongoing Infant-Toddler Program services through CDSA Piedmont under the category of established condition/developmental delay.

Recomendaciones / Recommendations:

1. Continue individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, billed under CPT 92507 (individual speech-language treatment), targeting expressive vocabulary growth, phonological pattern remediation, and narrative skills in both English and Spanish.

2. Add one monthly group session, billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression), to monitor progress across both languages and update goal targets as needed.

3. Continue bilingual service delivery. This clinician recommends therapy be delivered by a bilingual provider or with consistent interpreter support from Juan Pablo Díaz to ensure accurate progress monitoring in Spanish.

4. Family education: provide Lucía and Edgar with home strategies for modeling target sounds and expanding utterances in whichever language is most comfortable in the moment, honoring the family's natural code-switching rather than restricting to one language.

5. Coordinate with Little Steps Early Head Start Center and Ms. Patricia Gómez regarding classroom supports, including reducing reliance on peer interpretation (for example from Bryson) in favor of structured adult prompting to encourage Teo's independent attempts.

6. Recommend referral for a follow-up audiological recheck given history of early ear infections, to rule out any fluctuating hearing contribution to phonological delay; family may coordinate through Dr. Robert Chen or directly with UNC Health Audiology.

7. This clinician will update Yolanda Martínez at ACSICA with this report prior to the annual IFSP review meeting scheduled for November 18, 2026 at 1:00 p.m.

8. Encourage continued connection with WIC and Alamance Smart Start Partnership for Children family support staff, who can reinforce language-rich routines during home visits.

Plan of Care Review Date:  March 2027
Reevaluation recommended in approximately 6 months or sooner if progress plateaus.

This report was prepared following direct observation, parent interview, and interpreter-supported communication. All test results were interpreted considering Teo's bilingual language exposure, consistent with best practice guidelines for dual-language learners.

Abuela materna, quien ayuda con el cuidado: Carmen Hidalgo Reyes.
La familia tambien recibe ayuda ocasional de una vecina, J. Ortiz, quien cuida a Santi cuando la mama tiene citas medicas.

Nombre: Yesenia Cruz Fuentes
Oficina CDSA: Piedmont CDSA, oficina de Siler City
Telefono: (919) 555-0299
Correo electronico: ycruz@piedmontcdsa.org

TERAPEUTA DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Este reporte fue preparado por Maria Fernanda Lopez Duran, M.S., CCC-SLP, patologa bilingue del habla y lenguaje, empleada de Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC. Numero de proveedor: SLP-0071452. Telefono de la oficina: (919) 555-0400.

FECHA DE LA REUNION DE REVISION DEL IFSP: October 6, 2026
FECHA DEL IFSP ANTERIOR: April 2, 2026
FECHA DE INICIO DE SERVICIOS: May 14, 2026

RAZON PARA LA REVISION

Esta es una revision de rutina de seis meses del IFSP de Santi. La familia, la coordinadora de servicios Cruz Fuentes, y esta terapeuta nos reunimos en la casa de la familia el October 6, 2026 para revisar el progreso de Santi hacia sus resultados y para ajustar las estrategias segun sea necesario.

DIAGNOSTICO Y CODIGOS

Diagnostico: trastorno del desarrollo del habla y el lenguaje, codigo F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo). Servicios facturados bajo los codigos de procedimiento 92507 (tratamiento individual de habla/lenguaje) y 92523 (evaluacion de habla sonido-produccion con evaluacion de lenguaje). Modificador aplicado: GN.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA, EN SUS PROPIAS PALABRAS

La mama, Rosa, comparte: "Santi entiende casi todo lo que le decimos, pero cuando el quiere decir algo, solo usa como diez palabras y el resto son sonidos. A veces se frustra mucho y empieza a gritar o a jalarme de la ropa porque no sabe como decirme lo que quiere. Quiero que el pueda decir frases completas antes de entrar a pre-kinder."

El papa, Eduardo, agrega: "En la guarderia me dicen que el juega bien con los otros ninos pero que casi no habla con ellos. Yo quiero que tenga mas amigos y que pueda jugar y platicar como su hermana Valentina cuando ella tenia su edad."

La abuela, Carmen, tambien participo y dijo: "Yo paso mucho tiempo con el en las tardes y he notado que repite lo que uno dice, como un eco, en vez de contestar la pregunta."

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Santi se despierta a las 6:30 a.m. y desayuna con la familia. Su mama lo lleva a los 8:00 a.m. a un programa de cuidado infantil llamado Las Manitas Creciendo, ubicado en 210 West Raleigh Street, Siler City, NC. Alli pasa el dia con su maestra principal, la Senora Alvarado, y la asistente, Yolanda Perez. Entre sus companeros de clase estan Emiliano y Dulce, con quienes juega mas seguido segun el reporte de la maestra.

Por las tardes, Rosa recoge a Santi a las 4:30 p.m. y la familia a veces va a jugar al parque o visita la Biblioteca Publica del Condado de Chatham, sucursal de Siler City, donde hay un programa semanal de cuentos bilingues los miercoles a las 10:00 a.m.. La familia tambien asiste los domingos a la Iglesia Bautista Hispana Nueva Esperanza, donde Santi participa en la clase de ninos pequenos dirigida por una voluntaria, M.R.

La familia recibe apoyo alimentario de WIC y participa en un programa de Smart Start del Condado de Chatham que les proporciona libros bilingues cada mes.

La hora de la cena es alrededor de las 6:00 p.m. y toda la familia, incluyendo a Carmen, come junta la mayoria de las noches. El bano es a las 7:30 p.m. y Santi se duerme cerca de las 8:30 p.m., generalmente con su peluche, un perrito de felpa que la familia llama "Nino" (no es una mascota real, sino un juguete).

La mascota de la familia es un perro llamado Rocky, quien le gusta mucho a Santi y lo busca cada vez que se siente ansioso.

OTRAS AGENCIAS Y PROVEEDORES INVOLUCRADOS

Santi fue referido originalmente por su pediatra, Dr. Hector Villanueva, de Chatham Pediatric Associates, ubicado en 890 Hospital Road, Siler City, NC. El Dr. Villanueva continua monitoreando el desarrollo general de Santi en visitas de rutina.

La familia tambien ha sido conectada con el Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Chatham (DSS) para asistencia con transporte a las citas. El trabajador de caso asignado es J. Delgado.

No hay otros proveedores de terapia activos en este momento. La familia rechazo anteriormente una referencia a terapia ocupacional porque sentian que no era necesaria.

RESUMEN DEL DESARROLLO Y DESEMPENO ACTUAL

Se administraron las siguientes evaluaciones durante la sesion de revision: Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish y observacion clinica estructurada.

Comprension Auditiva: puntuacion estandar de 76, percentil 5, edad equivalente de 22 meses.
Expresion de Lenguaje: puntuacion estandar de 71, percentil 3, edad equivalente de 20 meses.
Puntuacion Total de Lenguaje: 72, intervalo de confianza del 95% de 65-79.

En la evaluacion de produccion de sonidos del habla, Santi demostro los siguientes patrones: sustituye /k/ por [t] en posicion inicial ("tasa" por "casa"), omite consonantes finales de manera consistente, y simplifica grupos consonanticos (por ejemplo, dice "pato" por "plato"). Se observaron estos patrones en 8 de 10 oportunidades durante la muestra de habla espontanea, lo cual representa aproximadamente el 80% de las palabras de prueba.

Santi actualmente usa un promedio de 12 palabras diferentes de manera espontanea, principalmente sustantivos ("agua", "mas", "Mama", "Rocky" cuando se refiere a su perro). No combina palabras de manera consistente; se observaron solo dos combinaciones de dos palabras durante la sesion ("mas agua" y "no quiero").

Se observo tambien un patron de ecolalia inmediata, consistente con lo reportado por la abuela Carmen: cuando se le preguntaba "¿quieres jugar?", Santi repetia "jugar" en vez de responder con si o no.

RESULTADOS DEL IFSP (ACTUALIZADOS)

Resultado 1: Santi se comunicara sus necesidades y deseos usando frases de dos a tres palabras en al menos tres contextos diferentes (casa, guarderia, comunidad).
Estado: progreso emergente. Actualmente logra esto en 2 de 5 oportunidades observadas con claves moderadas (mod cues).
Estrategias: uso del enfoque de Hanen - It Takes Two to Talk por parte de los padres; modelado de lenguaje expandido; tiempo de espera estructurado.

Resultado 2: Santi producira los sonidos /k/, /g/, y consonantes finales en palabras funcionales con un 70% de precision o mas en contexto estructurado.
Estado: en progreso. Precision actual del 40% con claves minimas a moderadas.
Estrategias: enfoque de terapia de ciclos fonologicos (Cycles); practica de palabras objetivo en el hogar durante las rutinas de bano y comida.

Resultado 3 (nuevo, agregado en esta revision): Santi participara en intercambios sociales reciprocos de al menos dos turnos con companeros en la guarderia, usando gestos o palabras, en 3 de 5 oportunidades observadas.
Estrategias: coordinacion con el personal de Las Manitas Creciendo para estructurar oportunidades de juego con Emiliano y Dulce; introduccion de un sistema de apoyo visual tipo PECS para iniciar interacciones.

SERVICIOS ACTUALES Y FRECUENCIA

Terapia de habla y lenguaje individual: una vez por semana, 30 minutos por sesion, en el hogar de la familia, bajo el codigo 92507.
Evaluacion periodica de produccion de sonidos: segun sea necesario, bajo el codigo 92523, tipicamente cada seis meses coincidiendo con la revision del IFSP.
Coordinacion de servicios: mensual, por parte de Cruz Fuentes.

Proxima evaluacion formal programada para: April 7, 2027
Proxima revision de IFSP programada para: April 7, 2027

PLAN DE TRANSICION

Dado que Santi cumplira tres anos el April 11, 2026 del siguiente ciclo, la coordinadora Cruz Fuentes discutio con la familia el proceso de transicion hacia servicios del sistema escolar publico (Parte B, Preescolar con Necesidades Especiales) bajo Chatham County Schools. Se programara una conferencia de transicion aproximadamente a los 2;6 de edad, aunque dado que Santi ya tiene casi 2;11, esta conferencia se adelantara. Fecha tentativa de la conferencia de transicion: November 18, 2026.

La familia expreso que quiere que Santi continue en Las Manitas Creciendo el mayor tiempo posible antes de cualquier cambio de programa, ya que se siente comodo alli y ha formado relaciones con Senora Alvarado y sus companeros.

RECOMENDACIONES ADICIONALES

Se recomienda que la familia continue llevando a Santi al programa de cuentos bilingues de la Biblioteca Publica del Condado de Chatham para fomentar la exposicion al lenguaje en ambos idiomas en un ambiente estructurado y de bajo estres.

Se recomienda tambien que Eduardo y Rosa participen en al menos dos sesiones de entrenamiento para padres sobre el enfoque Hanen durante el proximo periodo de servicio, para asegurar consistencia entre las sesiones de terapia.

Se discutio brevemente con la familia la posibilidad de una evaluacion auditiva de rutina, dado que no se ha documentado una prueba de audicion reciente en el expediente. Rosa indico que programara esta cita con el Dr. Villanueva en las proximas semanas.

Document Type: Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) — Annual Review
Child's Name: María José Hernández Ramírez
Preferred Name: Majo
Date of Birth: April 9, 2024
Age at Review: 26 months
Child ID: NC-ITP-004871
Medicaid ID: 9384710225B
Primary Language(s) – Child: Spanish, English (bilingual exposure)
Primary Language(s) – Home: Spanish
Mother: Lucía Fernanda Ramírez Torres
Father: Esteban Hernández Vidal
Address: 1148 Willowmere Trail, Burlington, Alamance County, NC 27217
Home Phone: (336) 555-0187
Mother's Cell: (336) 555-0412
Email: lramireztorres24@fakemail.com
CDSA Office: Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios Familiares del Condado de Alamance ("CDSA de Alamance")
Service Coordinator: Yesenia Campos Ruiz, Asociación para el Desarrollo Integral de la Niñez y la Familia ("ADINF")
Interpreter Present: Rosa Delmira Peña, certified medical interpreter (Spanish/English)
Primary Author / SLP: Carmen Alicia Rivas, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC
Referring Pediatrician: Dr. Howard Ingram, Alamance Regional Children's Clinic
Birth Hospital: Cone Health Alamance Regional Medical Center
Initial IFSP Date: June 2, 2025
Current Review Date: October 6, 2026
Next Review Due: April 6, 2027
Eligibility Category: Established Condition — F80.2 (Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder)
Daycare/Preschool: Jack-in-the-Pulpit Preschool, Burlington, NC

FAMILY INFORMATION

Majo lives with her parents, Lucía and Esteban, and her older brother Mateo (age 6) in a single-family home on Willowmere Trail in Burlington. Lucía works part-time as a line supervisor at Elon Precision Manufacturing, and Esteban works full-time in landscaping for a company based in Graham. Majo's maternal grandmother, Ofelia Torres Delgado, lives nearby and provides care three afternoons a week while Lucía is at work; the family refers to her as "Abuela Ofelia." The family also has a dog, Canela, who Majo enjoys feeding treats to in the backyard. The home is Spanish-dominant; Mateo is bilingual and often translates for his sister with extended family members who visit on weekends.

The family's first language is Spanish, and both parents report comfort with spoken English but prefer Spanish for discussing Majo's services in depth. Rosa Delmira Peña interpreted for this meeting at the family's request.

SERVICE COORDINATION

Majo's case is coordinated through the CDSA de Alamance, with service coordination contracted to ADINF. Yesenia Campos Ruiz has served as the family's service coordinator since intake in May 2025 and conducts home visits approximately every 60 days. Yesenia reports that the family has been consistent with appointments and has requested additional information about transition planning as Majo approaches her third birthday.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES (in the family's own words)

Lucía shared: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Majo no puede decirnos lo que necesita. Se frustra mucho y empieza a llorar o a jalarnos la ropa." ("What worries us most is that Majo can't tell us what she needs. She gets very frustrated and starts crying or pulling at our clothes.")

Esteban added: "Queremos que pueda jugar con los otros niños en la escuelita sin que se sienta sola." ("We want her to be able to play with the other kids at the little school without feeling alone.")

Both parents identified the following priorities for this IFSP period:
1. Increase Majo's functional vocabulary in both Spanish and English so she can request preferred items and activities.
2. Reduce frustration-related behaviors (crying, pulling, pushing) during daily routines.
3. Support Majo's participation and peer interaction at Jack-in-the-Pulpit Preschool.
4. Prepare the family for the transition to Part B services before Majo turns three.

DAILY ROUTINES

Majo wakes around 7:00 AM and eats breakfast with the family at 7:20 AM. Esteban drops her at Jack-in-the-Pulpit Preschool by 8:15 AM on his way to work. At preschool, Majo is in the toddler room with lead teacher Ms. Whitfield and assistant teacher Ms. Alvarado. Her classmates include Sofia, Benji, and Priya, with whom she engages in brief parallel play. Snack is at 9:30 AM, outdoor play from 10:00 AM to 10:45 AM, lunch at 11:30 AM, and nap from 12:30 PM to 2:00 PM. Abuela Ofelia picks Majo up at 3:00 PM on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays; Lucía picks her up the other days around 3:30 PM. Evenings include dinner together as a family around 6:00 PM, bath at 7:15 PM, and bedtime routine with books in Spanish beginning at 7:45 PM.

Ms. Whitfield reports that Majo enjoys sensory bins and music time but struggles to request turns with toys, often resorting to grabbing or crying, which has led to two minor peer conflicts with Benji this month.

OTHER AGENCIES AND SUPPORTS

The family currently receives WIC nutritional support through the Alamance County health department and has an open case with Alamance County DSS for a one-time emergency utility assistance request, which Yesenia Campos Ruiz is helping them navigate. The family was referred to Smart Start of Alamance County for a possible scholarship to extend Majo's preschool hours, and that application is pending. Majo also sees occupational therapist Jennifer Pak, OTR/L, through a separate contract with the CDSA de Alamance, for fine motor goals not addressed in this plan.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Receptive Language: On the Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual administration, Majo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 70 (2nd percentile), an age equivalent of 15 months. She follows 1-step directions with contextual support but inconsistently follows directions without gesture cues.

Expressive Language: Majo's Expressive Communication standard score was 65 (1st percentile), age equivalent 13 months. Her expressive vocabulary across both languages totals approximately 35 words, including "mamá," "papá," "agua" (produced as "aba"), "no," and "más." She combines two words rarely and only with moderate cues.

Articulation/Phonology: Informal sampling shows consistent reduction of final consonants and substitution of /k/ for /t/ in word-initial position (e.g., target "taza" produced as "casa"-like approximation). Stimulability for /s/ and /m/ was present with minimal cues.

Social Communication/Pragmatics: Majo uses eye contact and reaching to request but rarely vocalizes to initiate. She shows joint attention for brief periods (15-20 seconds) and tolerates turn-taking in simple routines like "ready-set-go" games with 3 of 5 trials successful.

Hearing/Medical: Hearing screened within normal limits at the September 14, 2026 well-child visit with Dr. Howard Ingram. No current ear infections reported. Birth history unremarkable; Apgar scores were 8 and 9, birth weight 7 lbs 2 oz, gestational age 39 weeks.

OUTCOMES

Outcome 1: Majo will use two-word combinations to request preferred items/activities in Spanish and/or English during daily routines, increasing from current baseline of less than 5% of opportunities to 80% of opportunities across three consecutive data collection sessions, as measured by provider and parent report.
Strategies: Model core vocabulary during meals and play using PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cues; parent coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, specifically OWL (Observe, Wait, Listen) and self-talk/parallel-talk during bath and bedtime routines; introduce a low-tech visual choice board as a backup augmentative strategy if verbal requesting does not progress by the next quarterly check-in.

Outcome 2: Majo will reduce frustration-related behaviors (crying, grabbing, pushing) during transitions and peer play at home and at Jack-in-the-Pulpit Preschool from current baseline of 6-8 episodes/day to 2 or fewer episodes/day, measured by teacher and parent tracking logs.
Strategies: Teach a simple manual sign ("more," "help," "done") paired with spoken approximation; collaborate with Ms. Whitfield on a visual schedule for the toddler room; coach Abuela Ofelia and Esteban on consistent use of the same signs/words at home to support generalization.

Outcome 3: Majo will produce at least 3 of 5 target consonants (/m/, /n/, /p/, /s/, /t/) in word-initial position with minimal cues across structured and semi-structured tasks, as measured by SLP data collection.
Strategies: Cycles approach targeting stimulable sounds in word-initial position; bilingual phonological contrast drills alternating Spanish and English target words; home practice sheet with 10 target words per week, tracked by parents with a simple tally (target: 8/10 accuracy by next review).

Outcome 4: The family will identify and understand at least two Part B transition options and complete the transition conference prior to Majo's third birthday.
Strategies: Yesenia Campos Ruiz will schedule the transition conference for February 2027 and provide bilingual written materials on local preschool special education options; Carmen Alicia Rivas will share a written summary of Majo's communication profile for the transition team.

SERVICE DELIVERY

Speech-Language Therapy: Individual sessions twice weekly, Tuesdays 9:00 AM–9:30 AM and Thursdays 1:15 PM–1:45 PM, delivered in the home and at Jack-in-the-Pulpit Preschool on alternating weeks, billed under CPT 92523 (initial/periodic speech sound and language evaluation, as applicable) and CPT 92507 (individual speech-language treatment), by Carmen Alicia Rivas, M.S., CCC-SLP, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC.

Occupational Therapy: One session weekly, Wednesdays 10:30 AM–11:00 AM, provided by Jennifer Pak, OTR/L, addressed under a separate IFSP page.

Service Coordination: Monthly contact (phone or home visit) by Yesenia Campos Ruiz, ADINF, under contract with the CDSA de Alamance.

Natural Environment Justification: All speech-language services are delivered in the child's home and regular childcare setting, consistent with Part C natural environment requirements. The team determined that the home and Jack-in-the-Pulpit Preschool classroom provide sufficient opportunities to embed strategies into Majo's existing routines, including meals, play with peers Sofia and Priya, and bedtime with Lucía and Esteban.

PROGRESS SINCE LAST REVIEW

Since the initial IFSP on June 2, 2025, Majo has progressed from an estimated 10-word expressive vocabulary to approximately 35 words. Her receptive comprehension standard score improved from 58 at initial evaluation to the current 70, though both remain well below average limits. Parent-reported frustration episodes have decreased slightly from 8-10/day to 6-8/day, which the team agrees warrants continued and intensified focus this coming period. Ms. Whitfield notes improved tolerance for group circle time, from roughly 2 minutes to 5-7 minutes of sustained attention.

TEAM SIGNATURES AND PARTICIPATION

Present at this meeting: Lucía Fernanda Ramírez Torres (mother), Esteban Hernández Vidal (father), Yesenia Campos Ruiz (service coordinator, ADINF), Carmen Alicia Rivas (SLP, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC), Rosa Delmira Peña (interpreter). Ms. Whitfield participated by phone from Jack-in-the-Pulpit Preschool for the portion of the meeting addressing classroom strategies.

text:
PROGRAMA INFANTIL Y DE NIÑOS PEQUEÑOS DE CAROLINA DEL NORTE (NC ITP)
REVISIÓN DEL PLAN INDIVIDUALIZADO DE SERVICIOS PARA LA FAMILIA (IFSP)

CDSA: CDSA del Piedmont Triad
Oficina: 2406 Oakdale Road, Greensboro, NC 27403

Niño: Mateo Alejandro Vásquez Reyes
Fecha de nacimiento: 12 de abril de 2023
Edad cronológica: 2;6
Número de expediente: NC-ITP-004417
Número de Medicaid: 784215639A

Madre: Daniela Reyes Martínez
Teléfono: (336) 555-0148
Correo electrónico: danielareyesm@gmail.com
Padre: Carlos Vásquez Lima
Domicilio familiar: 1420 Holloway Street, Durham, NC 27703

Coordinadora de servicios: Lucía Fernández
Patóloga del habla y lenguaje: Ana Gutiérrez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Fecha de la revisión del IFSP: 3 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del IFSP inicial: 15 de enero de 2026

S:
La mamá, Daniela, reporta en sus propias palabras: "Mateo entiende casi todo lo que le decimos en español e inglés, pero cuando quiere algo solo señala o grita. No usa palabras como antes de los 2 años." Dice que en casa usan español la mayoría del tiempo, sobre todo en la cena y a la hora del baño, pero que la hermana mayor, Sol Vásquez Reyes, de 7 años, le habla mucho en inglés porque así aprendió en la escuela. La mamá agrega: "A veces confundo si no habla porque no entiende o porque no quiere esforzarse." También comenta que a la hora de dormir Mateo se frustra si no logra pedir su manta o su vaso de agua y termina llorando hasta que alguien adivina.

Papá, Carlos, comenta que Mateo imita sonidos de animales y de carros, pero casi no imita palabras completas todavía. Reporta que la rutina diaria incluye: despertar a las 7:00 a.m., desayuno en casa con la familia, y a las 8:30 a.m. lo llevan al centro infantil Mundo de Burbujas en Durham, donde pasa el día con otros niños de su edad hasta las 5:30 p.m.. Por la tarde, dos veces por semana, la familia asiste al programa de cuentos bilingües en la Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Durham, donde Mateo disfruta las canciones con movimiento aunque no canta las palabras. Los domingos van a la Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, donde Mateo participa en la clase de niños pequeños con su tía, Rosa Martínez, quien también lo cuida algunas tardes cuando los padres trabajan hasta tarde.

La familia recibe apoyo de WIC y está inscrita en Smart Start de Durham para servicios de alimentación temprana; también fueron referidos recientemente a Early Head Start de Durham para el próximo año escolar. La mamá trabaja medio tiempo en Lavandería Estrella y el papá trabaja en construcción con Constructora Hermanos Ramos.

La mamá menciona que ella creció en la aldea de El Rosario, Intibucá, Honduras, donde no había mucho acceso a terapias de este tipo, y que le preocupa no saber si el retraso de Mateo es "normal" o si necesita más ayuda de la que ya recibe. Reporta que la familia extendida, incluyendo a la abuela, Herminia Reyes, vive todavía en El Rosario, Intibucá y habla con Mateo por videollamada cada semana, aunque él casi no responde verbalmente y solo se queda mirando la pantalla.

Prioridades de la familia para esta revisión: 1) que Mateo use palabras para pedir comida y juguetes en vez de gritar; 2) que se comunique con su hermana Sol sin frustrarse ni morder; 3) que la maestra en Mundo de Burbujas, Srta. Karina Soto, entienda mejor sus señas y gestos durante el juego.

O:
Se administró el Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale el 28 de septiembre de 2026, con instrucciones dadas en español y apoyo de interpretación informal de la mamá. Mateo obtuvo una edad equivalente de 14 meses en comprensión y 11 meses en expresión, con una puntuación total correspondiente al percentil 2. En el Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, administrado en inglés en el Mundo de Burbujas, obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 62 (IC 90%: 56-68), muy por debajo del promedio esperado para su edad.

Se intentó administrar el Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, pero Mateo no cooperó lo suficiente para obtener un puntaje válido; se observaron únicamente los fonemas /m/, /p/ y /a/ en balbuceo espontáneo, sin aproximaciones consonante-vocal-consonante.

La Bayley-4, administrada por la terapeuta ocupacional Jennifer Liu, OTR/L del Hospital Infantil Duke, mostró un puntaje compuesto de comunicación de 70 (percentil 2), motor grueso 85 (percentil 16), motor fino 88 (percentil 21) y socioemocional 92 (percentil 30), este último dentro de rango esperado.

Durante la sesión directa, Mateo produjo aproximadamente 5 palabras aproximadas: "mamá", "papá", "agua" (producida como "a-a"), y dos aproximaciones no identificables. No produjo la palabra objetivo "sol" de manera espontánea, aunque la imitó con máx cues como "o". Se observó 3/10 intentos de imitación verbal exitosos durante la sesión de 45 minutos. Mateo usó gestos (señalar, jalar la mano) en 8/10 oportunidades comunicativas observadas, y recurrió al grito en 2/10 oportunidades cuando el gesto no fue suficiente.

Se observó a Mateo en el Mundo de Burbujas el 1 de octubre de 2026 junto con dos compañeros, Diego y Valentina. Mateo jugó principalmente en paralelo, con poca iniciación verbal hacia sus compañeros, aunque se acercó físicamente a Diego para pedir un juguete usando gesto y vocalización. La maestra Srta. Karina Soto reportó que Mateo usa principalmente gestos y que a veces muerde cuando está frustrado, sobre todo en la transición del juego libre al almuerzo.

Se revisó el historial médico con el pediatra, Dr. Esteban Morales, de Pediatría Comunitaria de Durham, quien confirmó audición normal según evaluación auditiva del 10 de agosto de 2026 y descartó causas médicas del retraso. Los códigos ICD-10 F80.1 (trastorno del lenguaje expresivo) y F80.2 (trastorno mixto receptivo-expresivo) permanecen activos en el expediente.

A:
Mateo presenta un retraso significativo en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y receptivo en ambos idiomas, consistente con un trastorno mixto receptivo-expresivo del lenguaje más que con una diferencia típica de desarrollo bilingüe. Los resultados del Rossetti y del Peabody son congruentes entre sí y muestran un retraso de aproximadamente 12 a 15 meses respecto a su edad cronológica de 2;6. El bajo número de intentos de imitación verbal exitosa (3/10) y la dependencia de gestos (8/10), junto con episodios de conducta agresiva ante la frustración comunicativa, sugieren que Mateo se beneficiaría de un sistema de comunicación aumentativa temporal mientras se desarrolla el lenguaje verbal en ambos idiomas.

La exposición bilingüe en el hogar no explica la magnitud del retraso observado, ya que el retraso es evidente tanto en español como en inglés. Se recomienda continuar la exposición bilingüe sin reducirla, conforme a la evidencia actual sobre desarrollo bilingüe típico y con trastorno del lenguaje. El desarrollo motor grueso, fino y socioemocional se mantiene dentro o cerca del rango esperado, lo cual apoya un perfil de retraso específico del lenguaje en lugar de un retraso global del desarrollo.

La relación entre Mateo y su hermana Sol parece ser una fuente importante de motivación comunicativa; se recomienda involucrarla de manera estructurada en las estrategias de intervención como modelo de lenguaje entre pares. El contexto familiar, incluyendo el acceso limitado a terapias en El Rosario, Intibucá que la mamá describe de su propia niñez, se reconoce como parte de su preocupación, pero no indica ningún riesgo adicional en el entorno actual de la familia en Durham.

P:
Se continúa el Resultado 1 del IFSP: Mateo usará al menos 10 palabras funcionales de manera espontánea para pedir y comentar, en ambos idiomas, en los próximos 6 meses. Estrategia: uso de PECS modificado con tarjetas bilingües, modelado de lenguaje en rutinas diarias, y práctica de palabras objetivo incluyendo "sol", "agua", "más" con cues mín-mod.

Se continúa el Resultado 2 del IFSP, sin cambios: Mateo participará en rutinas de alimentación con menor resistencia sensorial, bajo seguimiento de Jennifer Liu, OTR/L.

Se agrega el Resultado 3 del IFSP: Mateo iniciará interacciones comunicativas con sus compañeros en el Mundo de Burbujas en al menos 3 de 5 oportunidades observadas, en los próximos 4 meses, sin recurrir a morder. Estrategia: entrenamiento a la maestra Srta. Karina Soto en el uso del modelo Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" durante el juego libre, y refuerzo de señas básicas acordadas entre la familia y el centro.

Servicios: terapia de habla y lenguaje, 2 sesiones de 45 minutos por semana, modalidad individual y en grupo, a partir del 10 de octubre de 2026 hasta la próxima revisión programada para el 10 de abril de 2027. Terapia ocupacional continúa con 1 sesión mensual con Jennifer Liu, OTR/L.

Se coordinará, a través de la coordinadora de servicios Lucía Fernández, una visita conjunta al Mundo de Burbujas antes del 1 de noviembre de 2026 para capacitar al personal en estrategias de comunicación aumentativa y manejo de la frustración.

Se recomienda a la familia continuar asistiendo al programa de cuentos bilingües en la Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Durham y se sugiere inscripción adicional en el programa de habilidades sociales para niños pequeños de la Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, los sábados por la mañana.

Dado que Mateo cumplirá 3 años en abril de 2027, se inicia la planificación de transición hacia servicios de educación especial preescolar del distrito. La coordinadora Lucía Fernández enviará la referencia a Durham Public Schools, Servicios de Intervención Temprana en un plazo no mayor a 90 días antes del tercer cumpleaños.

CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT
Evaluación del Habla y el Lenguaje

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Hernández Cruz (called "Teo" at home)
Date of Birth: March 14, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;8
Date(s) of Evaluation: November 3, 2025 and November 10, 2025
Report Date: November 18, 2025
Medicaid ID: 920481773A
CDSA Case Number: CDSA-WC-2023-00417
Referring Physician: Dr. Alan Whitfield, WakeMed Pediatric Primary Care
Evaluating SLP: Jessica Alvarado, M.S., CCC-SLP (Bilingual Spanish-English)
Practice: Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Phone: (919) 555-0148   Email: jalvarado@carolinabilingualspeech.com

Setting of Evaluation:
[X] Home   [ ] Daycare/Preschool   [ ] Clinic   [ ] School

Informant(s):
[X] Mother   [X] Father   [ ] Grandmother   [ ] Teacher
Informant(s) for this report: Lucía Rodríguez Hernández (madre) and Carlos Hernández Pérez (padre), with portions of the family history provided during a prior home visit by Marisol Castañeda, Service Coordinator, Wake County Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA).

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE LA REFERENCIA

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Wake County CDSA following a developmental screening conducted at Casa Mariposa Preschool, where Teo has attended three days a week since August 2024. His lead teacher, la maestra Carmen, and the classroom assistant, Miss Ana, both reported that Mateo's speech is "muy difícil de entender" (very hard to understand) compared to same-age peers, and that he becomes frustrated when classmates do not understand him during circle time. His parents report similar concerns at home and note that his older sister, Sol Hernández, age 7, and his older brother, Diego Hernández, age 10, frequently "translate" for him with adults outside the immediate family.

Setting(s) where concerns are noted:
[X] Home   [X] Daycare   [ ] Community   [X] With unfamiliar listeners

BACKGROUND INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE ANTECEDENTES

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez Hernández and Carlos Hernández Pérez, along with his siblings Sol Hernández and Diego Hernández, at 412 Sweetgum Lane, Garner, Wake County, 27529. The family also receives regular support from the maternal grandmother, referred to throughout the home as doña Lupe (Guadalupe Torres), who provides afterschool care on Fridays and accompanies the family to medical appointments when Lucía Rodríguez Hernández is working.

Living situation:
[X] Lives with both biological parents   [ ] Single-parent household   [ ] Lives with relative(s)
[X] Extended family involved in caregiving   [ ] Foster/kinship care

Carlos Hernández Pérez works full time at Triangle Fresh Foods, a food distribution warehouse in Garner, and Lucía Rodríguez Hernández works part time at a local grocery store. The family was connected to WIC shortly after Mateo's birth and has continued to receive nutritional support through that program. The family was also enrolled with Smart Start of Wake County during Mateo's infancy for developmental screening and referral support, and Lucía Rodríguez Hernández reports that it was through a Smart Start playgroup that she first learned about Wake County CDSA services.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Lucía Rodríguez Hernández reported no complications during pregnancy or delivery, "todo salió bien, no hubo ningún problema" (everything went well, there wasn't any problem).

Medical history is otherwise unremarkable. Mateo sees Dr. Alan Whitfield for routine pediatric care and has no diagnosed syndromes, seizure history, or significant illnesses. He is not currently taking any medications. Vision was last screened at his four-year well-child visit and was reported as within normal limits.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Language(s) spoken in the home:
[X] Spanish   [X] English   [ ] Other: __________

Lucía Rodríguez Hernández and Carlos Hernández Pérez both report that Spanish is the primary language used in the home, with English introduced gradually through Mateo's older siblings and through daycare exposure. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández stated, "En casa hablamos español casi todo el tiempo, pero los niños ya mezclan mucho el inglés" (At home we speak Spanish almost all the time, but the kids already mix in a lot of English).

English — Sol Hernández and Diego Hernández (mixed), la maestra Carmen at Casa Mariposa Preschool (mixed instruction)

No other family members are reported to have a history of speech, language, or learning difficulties, although Carlos Hernández Pérez noted that his own brother "tardó en hablar de niño" (was late to talk as a child) but ultimately "habla normal ahora" (speaks normally now).

EDUCATIONAL AND CHILD CARE HISTORY / HISTORIA EDUCATIVA Y DE CUIDADO INFANTIL

Prior to enrolling at Casa Mariposa Preschool, Mateo participated in Early Head Start of Wake County from roughly January 2023 through July 2024, where he was seen briefly by a home visitor, Tom Ferris — referred to by the family simply as Mr. Tom — who first suggested a developmental screening due to limited intelligibility.

Mateo is expected to enroll in Pre-Kindergarten next fall through Wake County Public School System, and the family has been told he is zoned for Walnut Creek Elementary School. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández expressed concern that Mateo "no va a poder comunicarse bien" (won't be able to communicate well) once he transitions into a larger English-dominant classroom setting.

The family has also been in contact with Wake County Department of Social Services (DSS) regarding continued eligibility for subsidized child care, and their assigned caseworker has coordinated with Wake County CDSA service coordinator Marisol Castañeda to ensure services are not disrupted during the transition to kindergarten eligibility.

PRIOR SERVICES / SERVICIOS PREVIOS

Mateo has an active Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) through Wake County CDSA, with the most recent IFSP review completed on September 22, 2025. Current IFSP Outcome #2 addresses functional communication across settings, and this evaluation was requested to inform updates to that outcome as well as Outcome #3, which addresses peer interaction.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES / PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

This evaluation was conducted in both English and Spanish across two sessions, one at the family's home and one at the evaluator's office, to capture Mateo's communication across contexts and languages.

Tools administered:

- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) — Morphosyntax and Semantics subtests
- Preschool Language Scale-5 Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish) — Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), administered in English
- Spanish Articulation Measures (SAM) screening items, administered in Spanish
- Spontaneous language sample (English and Spanish), analyzed using SALT conventions
