text:
Patient Name: Mateo Hernández Cruz
Preferred Name: Mateo
Date of Birth: April 3, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Medical Record Number: MR-204871
Medicaid Member ID: 100873542D
Date of Evaluation: June 9, 2026
Date of Report: June 14, 2026
Referral Source: Dr. Anne Castellanos, pediatrician, Sandhills Regional Medical Center
Evaluating Clinician: Grace M. Thornton, MS, CCC-SLP
Clinic: Sandhills Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC
Interpreter: Diana Castillo, certified Spanish-English medical interpreter
Home Address: 214 Birchwood Lane, Fayetteville, NC 28301
County: Cumberland County
Home Phone: (910) 555-2847
Primary Caregiver(s): Lucía Hernández Martínez (mother), Héctor Hernández Pineda (father)
Primary Language(s) in the Home: Spanish and English
Service Coordinator: Patricia Núñez, Cumberland County CDSA
IFSP Review Date: August 1, 2026

**Reason for Referral**

Mateo is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish/English) boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Castellanos due to parental and teacher concern regarding limited intelligibility, reduced expressive vocabulary, and difficulty following multi-step directions in both languages. Mateo currently receives early intervention services through Cumberland County CDSA under IFSP Outcome 2, and this evaluation was requested to inform the August 1, 2026 annual IFSP review.

**Background and Family History**

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Hernández Martínez and Héctor Hernández Pineda, and his older sister, Sol Hernández Martínez (age 7), at 214 Birchwood Lane in Fayetteville. The family also includes Mateo's maternal grandmother, Carmen Martínez Soto, who provides after-school and weekend childcare for both children and lives nearby.

Lucía Hernández Martínez works at Restaurante El Buen Sabor, a family-style Mexican restaurant, where she works evening shifts as a server. Héctor Hernández Pineda is employed by Pinewood Construction Company as a framing crew lead. Both parents describe long and variable work hours, and both report that Mateo spends significant time in his grandmother's care in addition to attending Sunshine Steps Child Development Center on weekdays from 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM.

The family attends services at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida most Sundays, where Mateo also attends the children's program. Mateo and his sister, Sol Hernández Martínez, attend the bilingual story-time program hosted by Manos Unidas Family Resource Center on Thursday evenings, which the family has found helpful for building English vocabulary in a low-pressure setting alongside other bilingual families in the community.

Lucía Hernández Martínez was born and raised in La Esperanza, Honduras, a small village in the western highlands, and moved to the United States in 2015. She reports that Spanish was the only language spoken in her childhood home and that she did not learn English until adulthood. Héctor Hernández Pineda was born in Comayagua, Honduras, and came to Fayetteville in 2017 to join extended family already working in the area. Both parents report feeling comfortable using Spanish with Mateo and prefer that he maintain strong Spanish skills alongside English.

**Birth and Medical History**

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation via vaginal delivery at Sandhills Regional Medical Center. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. There were no complications noted in the neonatal period, and Mateo was discharged home with his mother on day two of life. His mother reports an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with 4 documented episodes between 12 months and 24 months of age, each treated with oral antibiotics. Mateo underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement (CPT 69436) on November 12, 2024, performed by Dr. Samuel Okafor, pediatric otolaryngologist. Tubes extruded spontaneously by approximately 30 months of age, and a follow-up audiogram on March 3, 2025 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally, with no evidence of conductive loss at the time of this evaluation. No other significant medical history, hospitalizations, or surgeries are reported, and Mateo takes no regular medications. Vision screening at his most recent well-child visit was within normal limits.

Diagnostic coding associated with the current referral includes ICD-10 F80.9 (developmental disorder of speech and language, unspecified), with F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (phonological disorder) also under consideration pending the results of this evaluation.

**Family and Language History**

Spanish is the primary language used in the home between Mateo and both parents and his grandmother, Carmen Martínez Soto. English is used increasingly with his sister, Sol Hernández Martínez, who is more English-dominant following two years in the Cumberland County school system, and with peers and staff at Sunshine Steps Child Development Center. Parents estimate Mateo's current exposure as approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English, though this ratio has shifted toward more English exposure over the past year as his sister has entered school.

There is a family history of late talking: Héctor Hernández Pineda reports that he did not combine words until after age 3, and a paternal uncle received speech therapy as a child in Honduras. No other family history of hearing loss, autism, intellectual disability, or genetic syndromes is reported.

**Educational History**

Mateo has attended Sunshine Steps Child Development Center since January 2024. His classroom teacher, Jennifer Lopez, reports that Mateo is social and affectionate with peers but is frequently difficult to understand, relies heavily on gesture, and becomes frustrated when he cannot make himself understood. Ms. Lopez also notes that he follows one-step directions reliably but struggles with two-step directions, particularly in English. His classroom peers, including Isabella Cho and Jayden Brooks, reportedly include him in play but sometimes speak for him when he is not understood, which Ms. Lopez feels may be reducing his opportunities to practice independent communication.

**Behavioral Observations**

Mateo presented as a friendly, cooperative child who separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the examiner and with the interpreter, Diana Castillo. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks lasting approximately 20 minutes before requiring a brief movement break, and transitioned well between activities when given advance warning. Hearing and vision were grossly screened and appeared adequate for testing purposes. Oral-motor examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech production, with adequate range of motion, strength, and coordination of the lips, tongue, and jaw observed during both speech and non-speech tasks.

**Standardized Test Results**

The Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), and the Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA) were administered, along with select subtests of the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Fifth Edition (CELF-5) on a qualitative basis.

| Measure | Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | Standard Score 76 | 5th percentile | 2;9 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | Standard Score 71 | 3rd percentile | 2;6 |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | 73 | 4th percentile | — |
| GFTA-3 | Standard Score 68 | 2nd percentile | — |
| BESA Morphosyntax Index (Spanish) | Standard Score 82 | 12th percentile | — |
| BESA Morphosyntax Index (English) | Standard Score 74 | 4th percentile | — |

CELF-5 was administered on a supplemental, qualitative basis only, given Mateo's age falls below the normed range for several subtests; formal scores are not reported, though observations from administered items are consistent with findings on the PLS-5 and BESA.

**Speech Sound Production**

Mateo's connected speech was estimated to be approximately 40% intelligible to unfamiliar listeners in English and approximately 55% intelligible in Spanish, with context available to the listener. Single-word intelligibility in Spanish was higher, at approximately 8/10 words understood by the examiner without the gloss, compared with roughly 5/10 in English.

Phonological processes observed in Spanish included final consonant deletion, stopping of fricatives, and liquid simplification, including gliding of /ɾ/ to [w] and deletion of /s/ in consonant clusters. On a single-word Spanish articulation probe, Mateo was shown a picture of the sun and asked to name it; his target word was "sol", which he produced as "to", omitting the final liquid consistent with the pattern noted above. The clinician noted that this target happens to be homophonous with the name of Mateo's sister, Sol Hernández Martínez, and confirmed with the family, through the interpreter, Diana Castillo, that Mateo did not appear to confuse the word with his sister's name during testing, nor did he reference her when prompted for the target.

In English, Mateo demonstrated fronting of /k/ and /g/ to [t] and [d] respectively (for example, "cat" produced as "tat"), cluster reduction, and final consonant deletion. He produced /θ/ as [f], consistent with common developmental patterns among English learners of his age. Stimulability testing showed that Mateo could produce /k/ in isolation with moderate cues and /s/ in the initial position with minimal cues, suggesting good candidacy for direct therapy using a Cycles approach targeting phonological patterns across both languages.

**Language Sample**

A spontaneous language sample was collected in both languages during structured play with toy animals and a farm set, with Diana Castillo interpreting for the Spanish portions. In Spanish, Mateo produced primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations (for example, "más agua," "no quiero"), with a mean length of utterance of approximately 1.8 morphemes. In English, his utterances were almost exclusively single words, with a mean length of utterance of approximately 1.2 morphemes. He used gesture and pointing extensively to supplement verbal output in both languages, particularly when frustrated or when a listener did not understand him on the first attempt.

Mateo demonstrated understanding of basic spatial concepts (in, on, under) and several body part names in both languages, but had difficulty with multi-step directions, temporal concepts (before, after), and quantitative concepts (more, less) in formal testing, consistent with teacher report from Ms. Lopez. He initiated communication with the examiner and interpreter spontaneously but relied on single words or short phrases rather than extended utterances, even when given models.

**Impressions**

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English (ICD-10 F80.2), along with a moderate speech sound disorder affecting both languages (ICD-10 F80.0). His difficulties are present across both languages and cannot be attributed solely to the process of bilingual acquisition, supporting a true disorder rather than typical second-language learning differences. Reduced intelligibility, limited expressive vocabulary, and difficulty with multi-step directions are consistent with, and likely contributing to, the concerns raised by his family and by his teacher, Jennifer Lopez.

Mateo's strengths include social engagement, appropriate use of compensatory gesture, and stimulability for several error sounds with cueing, all of which are favorable prognostic indicators for intervention. His history of recurrent otitis media during a key period of early language development is also a relevant contributing factor to consider in the overall clinical picture, though current hearing is within normal limits.

**Recommendations**

1. Mateo is recommended to continue speech-language therapy services under his IFSP, with a change in frequency from once weekly to twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, to address both expressive and receptive language goals and speech sound production goals in both Spanish and English.
2. Therapy should employ a Cycles phonological approach for speech sound goals and incorporate Hanen-based strategies to support parent-implemented language facilitation in the home.
3. The family should continue to use Spanish as the primary home language. Bilingual input supports rather than hinders Mateo's language development, and both languages should be targeted and supported in intervention rather than restricted to one language.
4. Coordination with Ms. Lopez and Sunshine Steps Child Development Center staff is recommended to support carryover of therapy targets in the classroom setting.
5. Referral to Cumberland County CDSA for an IFSP update reflecting these new goals is recommended, with review by service coordinator Patricia Núñez at the August 1, 2026 annual review.
6. A repeat audiological evaluation is recommended within the next 12 months given Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media, to be coordinated through Dr. Samuel Okafor's office.
7. The family may benefit from continued participation in the bilingual story-time program at Manos Unidas Family Resource Center, which supports informal English language exposure for Mateo and Sol Hernández Martínez in a supportive community setting.

This evaluation and these recommendations were discussed with Lucía Hernández Martínez and Héctor Hernández Pineda in Spanish, with interpretation provided by Diana Castillo. Both parents voiced agreement with the plan and expressed interest in strategies they can use at home, during family gatherings, and through the children's program at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, which Mateo also attends on Sunday mornings with his sister.

- Mateo was referred by his pediatrician, Dr. Anand Patel of Alamance Regional Medical Center, after a routine four-year well-child visit raised concerns about limited intelligibility and difficulty following multi-step directions.
- His mother, Lucía Fernández, reports that "en casa lo entendemos casi todo, pero la gente afuera no le entiende nada" — at home the family understands almost everything he says, but people outside the home understand very little.
- The family was also referred by their service coordinator at CDSA of the Piedmont Triad following an Early Intervention screening that flagged speech sound and receptive language delays.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION / ANTECEDENTES
Birth and Medical History
- Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Alamance Regional Medical Center on April 9, 2021, via scheduled cesarean section.
- Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz; Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes.
- Mrs. Fernández reports no prenatal complications, though she notes mild gestational diabetes managed with diet.
- Mateo had recurrent otitis media between 8 months and 22 months of age, with four documented episodes and bilateral tympanostomy tubes placed at 18 months by Dr. Samuel Ruiz, an ENT at Alamance Regional Medical Center.
- Hearing was last screened on August 14, 2025 and results were within normal limits bilaterally, per audiology report shared by Dr. Ruiz's office.
- No history of seizures, head injury, or significant developmental regression. Gross and fine motor milestones were reportedly within normal limits, though Mrs. Fernández noted that Mateo "camino un poquito tarde" — walked a little late, around 15 months.
- Medical history is otherwise unremarkable aside from seasonal allergies treated by Dr. Patel.

Family and Language History / Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje
- Mateo lives at 118 Willow Bend Lane, Burlington, Alamance County, NC 27217, with his mother Lucía Fernández, father Héctor Cruz, and older sister Sol Fernández (age 6;10).
- His maternal grandmother, doña Lupe, lives with the family three days a week and is a primary caregiver during the day while both parents work.
- An aunt, Tía Rosa, also helps with childcare on weekends and reportedly speaks only Spanish to Mateo and Sol.
- Language exposure in the home is estimated at roughly 70% Spanish and 30% English. Mr. Cruz speaks primarily Spanish with some English; Mrs. Fernández code-switches frequently, especially when discussing school-related topics.
- Mrs. Fernández stated, "yo le hablo en los dos, pero su papá casi siempre en español" — she speaks to him in both languages, but his father almost always in Spanish.
- Mateo attended Alamance County Early Head Start from age 18 months to 3 years, where his classroom teacher was Miss Ana.
- Miss Ana reportedly told the family during a home visit that Mateo "se frustra cuando no lo entienden los otros niños" — he gets frustrated when other children do not understand him.
- From ages 3 to 4, Mateo attended Sunshine Bilingual Daycare part-time, two days per week.
- The family previously received nutrition support through the Alamance County WIC Office and continues to receive case management support through Alamance County Department of Social Services (DSS).
- The family was connected to developmental screening resources through Smart Start of Alamance County, which provided an initial referral packet when Mateo was 2;8.
- Mr. Cruz works for Cruz Landscaping and Lawn Care, a small business he co-owns with his brother; Mrs. Fernández works part-time as a receptionist.
- Mateo's sister, Sol, is in first grade and reportedly serves as an informal interpreter for her brother with unfamiliar adults and peers.
- Notably, during articulation testing (see below), the target word "sol" was elicited for /s/ in the word-final position; Mrs. Fernández laughed and noted that this is also Sol's name, which Mateo sometimes substitutes when he cannot retrieve the target word, saying his sister's name instead.

EDUCATIONAL HISTORY
- Mateo is currently enrolled in Pre-K at Grove Park Elementary School, part of Alamance-Burlington School System, in the classroom of Mrs. Debra Collins.
- A classroom paraprofessional, la maestra Carmen, provides additional bilingual support two mornings a week.
- Mrs. Collins reports that Mateo participates eagerly in circle time but is frequently unintelligible to peers and adults outside the family.
- Two classmates, Diego and Emily, are described as patient with Mateo and often repeat his requests to the teacher when others cannot understand him.
- Mateo receives transportation to school via a district bus; the family noted that the driver, Mr. Tom, has learned several of Mateo's favorite phrases and greets him by name each morning, which the family appreciates.
- A prior speech-language screening was conducted at the school on March 3, 2025 by a previous contracted clinician identified in records only by initials, M.R., who recommended a full bilingual evaluation.
- An occupational therapy consultation was also requested; the referring OT, identified in school records as J. Ortiz, noted mild fine motor delays unrelated to the current speech-language concerns.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES
- Review of records, including CDSA referral packet and prior screening notes
- Parent interview (conducted bilingually with Rosa Martínez interpreting as needed)
- Hearing screening results review
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), English and Spanish stimulus items
- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA), Phonology and Morphosyntax subtests
- Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5) Spanish-Bilingual Edition, Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication subtests
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5) and Expressive Vocabulary Test-3 (EVT-3), English forms
- Language sample analysis (English and Spanish, approximately 15 minutes each)
- Oral-motor examination and informal play-based observation

TEST RESULTS

Standardized Test Scores
| Measure | Domain | Standard/Scaled Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GFTA-3 | Articulation (English) | SS 76 | 5th percentile | 3;1 |
| BESA Phonology | Articulation (Spanish) | SS 72 | 3rd percentile | — |
| BESA Morphosyntax | Expressive Grammar (Spanish) | SS 78 | 7th percentile | — |
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | Receptive Language | SS 81 | 10th percentile | — |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | Expressive Language | SS 74 | 4th percentile | — |
| PPVT-5 | Receptive Vocabulary (English) | SS 84 | 14th percentile | — |
| EVT-3 | Expressive Vocabulary (English) | SS 77 | 6th percentile | — |

- Confidence interval for PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension: 95% CI 75-87.
- Confidence interval for PLS-5 Expressive Communication: 95% CI 68-80.

Articulation and Phonology
- In English, Mateo produced 18 of 54 consonants in error across word positions, with consistent patterns affecting /s/, /z/, /r/, and consonant clusters.
- Target word "sol" (sun) was produced as [tol], omitting the target /s/ and substituting [t]; this pattern was consistent across 3 of 3 trials.
- In Spanish, Mateo demonstrated difficulty with the tap /ɾ/, frequently substituting [d], and showed cluster reduction in words such as "flor," produced as [for].
- Stimulability testing showed that Mateo could approximate /s/ in isolation with moderate cues, but not consistently at the word level.
- Intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at approximately 40% for unfamiliar listeners and 75% for familiar listeners, consistent with parent report.

Language Sample
- A spontaneous language sample was collected in English (approximately 15 minutes) during play with blocks and a toy kitchen set.
- Mean length of utterance was 3.1 morphemes, below expected range for chronological age.
- In the Spanish sample, Mateo demonstrated similar syntactic limitations, with frequent omission of articles and inconsistent verb conjugation, e.g., producing "yo come" instead of "yo como."
- Mateo used code-switching within single utterances, such as "quiero el ball," which is developmentally appropriate for bilingual children his age and was not counted as an error.
- Pragmatic skills, including turn-taking, joint attention, and requesting, appeared age-appropriate in both languages.

Oral-Motor and Hearing
- Oral-motor examination revealed adequate structure and function for speech; no dysarthria or apraxia indicators were observed.
- A diadochokinetic task showed mildly reduced rate but adequate accuracy.
- Hearing was reported within normal limits per the August 14, 2025 audiogram reviewed prior to testing.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS
- Mateo presents with a moderate speech sound disorder affecting both English and Spanish, consistent with a true bilingual phonological disorder rather than a language difference, given that error patterns are present and comparable across both languages.
- He also presents with a mild-to-moderate expressive and receptive language delay in both English and Spanish, which cannot be attributed solely to typical second-language acquisition given the cross-linguistic consistency of deficits.
- ICD-10 codes considered: F80.1 (Expressive Language Disorder) and F80.2 (Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder), with F80.0 (Phonological Disorder) also applicable.
- CPT codes for this evaluation: 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).
- Family history of late talking was noted; Mrs. Fernández reports that her brother "tardó mucho en hablar" — took a long time to begin talking — and received speech therapy as a child, though no formal records are available.
- doña Lupe expressed concern that Mateo's difficulties might affect his confidence at school, stating "no quiero que se sienta menos que los otros niños" — she does not want him to feel less than the other children.
- Overall prognosis for improvement with consistent, intensive bilingual intervention is good, given Mateo's strong pragmatic skills, family engagement, and stimulability for target sounds with cueing.

RECOMMENDATIONS
- Mateo qualifies for speech-language therapy services based on standardized scores falling at or below the 10th percentile across multiple domains in both languages.
- Recommend individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, provided bilingually or with consistent interpreter support, targeting:
  - English and Spanish /s/, /z/, /r/, and /ɾ/ production using minimal pairs and cued articulation
  - Expansion of morphosyntax in both languages, including article use and verb conjugation
  - Vocabulary development across both languages using shared-book reading
- Recommend continued coordination with CDSA of the Piedmont Triad service coordinator to update the IFSP, specifically Outcome #3 (communication) and Goal #2 (intelligibility).
- Recommend consultation with Mrs. Collins and la maestra Carmen regarding classroom strategies, including repetition, visual supports, and peer modeling with Diego and Emily.
- Recommend the family continue to use both languages at home; there is no clinical reason to reduce Spanish exposure, and doing so could negatively affect family bonding and cultural identity without improving English outcomes.
- Recommend re-evaluation in 6 months to monitor progress and adjust goals.
- Recommend the family follow up with Dr. Ruiz regarding any recurrence of middle ear infections, given the history of otitis media and its potential impact on auditory processing.
- Provided family with information on sibling support, noting that Sol should not be relied upon as a primary interpreter for formal services, though her support at school is appropriate and kind.
- Discussed available resources through Smart Start of Alamance County and Alamance County Department of Social Services (DSS) for continued family support services.
- Written report and recommendations provided to the family in Spanish and English; interpreter Rosa Martínez confirmed family understanding of all recommendations during the October 6, 2025 session.

This report reflects Mateo's speech-language skills as observed on the dates of testing and is intended for use in planning educational and therapeutic services. Please contact Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services at (336) 555-0148 with any questions.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
License #SLP-NC-11287

Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) — Annual Review
North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program

Lead Agency: CDSA of the Triangle, a Children's Developmental Services Agency office located at 4200 Westgate Park Drive, Suite 230, Raleigh, NC 27617 (Wake County).

Child: Mateo Ruiz Ramírez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: January 14, 2024
CDSA Record #: CDSA-2024-01837
NC Medicaid ID: 987654321B

Review Meeting Date: October 2, 2026, 10:00 AM–11:30 AM
Initial IFSP Date: March 20, 2024
Most Recent Prior Review: April 8, 2026
Next Annual Review Due: October 2, 2027

Parents: Lucía Ramírez (mother), Carlos Ruiz (father)
Home Address: 142 Willow Creek Lane, Durham, NC 27703 (Durham County)
Home Phone: (919) 555-0173
Service Coordinator: Monica Chen, MSW, CDSA of the Triangle
SC Phone / Email: (919) 555-0142 / mchen@cdsatriangle.org
Interpreter Present: Elena Gutiérrez, certified Spanish medical interpreter, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC

FAMILY BACKGROUND AND HISTORY

Mateo was born at 28 weeks gestation at UNC Health Rex — UNC Rex Women's and Children's, Raleigh Campus, with a birth weight of 2 lb 9 oz (1,163 g) and Apgar scores of 4 and 7. He spent 9 weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit there before discharge on March 25, 2024. Following discharge, he was followed for pediatric care at UNC Children's Primary Care at Southpoint and for audiology at UNC Health Hearing and Balance Center, Chapel Hill Campus, where he passed his most recent hearing screening on August 14, 2026. He was referred to the NC Infant-Toddler Program at 4 months adjusted age due to prematurity and feeding concerns.

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Ramírez and Carlos Ruiz, and his older sister Sol Ruiz Ramírez, age 6. His maternal grandmother, Rosa Ramírez, provides afternoon childcare three days a week while Lucía works. The family speaks Spanish at home and is building English skills together; Mateo attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center at 890 Chapel Hill Road, Durham, NC 27707 two mornings a week. Carlos works at Triangle Concrete & Masonry in Morrisville, and the family receives support from WIC, Durham County Department of Social Services, and Durham Smart Start for enrollment navigation.

FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES (in the family's words, via interpreter)

Lucía shared: "Nos preocupa que Teo no hable tanto como su hermana Sol a su edad. Queremos que pueda decirnos lo que necesita sin frustrarse." Translated: "We're worried that Teo doesn't talk as much as his sister Sol did at his age. We want him to be able to tell us what he needs without getting frustrated."

Carlos added that he wants Mateo to be understood by his grandmother Rosa and by staff at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, since right now only Lucía can reliably understand his words. The family's priorities for this year are: (1) increase spoken vocabulary in both languages, (2) improve speech sound clarity so unfamiliar listeners can understand him, and (3) support turn-taking play with his sister Sol and peers at daycare.

DAILY ROUTINES

Mornings: Mateo wakes around 7:00 AM, eats breakfast with Sol and Lucía, and is dropped at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center by 8:30 AM on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Afternoons: Rosa picks him up and they often walk to a nearby park before nap. Evenings: the family eats dinner together around 6:00 PM, and Mateo and Sol play with blocks and a shared picture book routine before bedtime at 8:00 PM. Carlos participates in bath and bedtime routines on evenings he is not working.

OTHER AGENCIES AND SERVICES INVOLVED

- WIC — nutrition support, recertification appointment scheduled November 12, 2026
- Durham County Department of Social Services — Medicaid case management
- Durham Smart Start — childcare subsidy coordination
- UNC Health Hearing and Balance Center, Chapel Hill Campus — annual audiology monitoring
- UNC Children's Primary Care at Southpoint — primary care, physician Dr. Angela Whitfield

EVALUATION SUMMARY

Mateo was reassessed on September 18, 2026 by Jennifer Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Licensed Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist with Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC (referred to below as Carolina Bilingual Therapy, or "CBTP"), using Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition, Spanish-English Bilingual Edition (PLS-5 Spanish-English) and informal bilingual sampling. Chronological age at testing: 2;8.

Score Table (PLS-5 Spanish-English, administered bilingually)

Subtest	Standard Score	95% Confidence Interval	Percentile	Age Equivalent
Auditory Comprehension	79	73–85	8th	1;11
Expressive Communication	72	66–78	3rd	1;7
Total Language Score	73	68–78	4th	1;9

Speech sound production was assessed informally across English and Spanish targets. Mateo produced 8/20 consonants correctly in word-initial position and showed consistent final consonant deletion. For the Spanish target word "sol," he produced [so], omitting the final /l/. For the target word "pelota," he produced [peˈota], deleting the medial /l/. In English, the target word "cup" was produced as [kʌ], and "dog" as [dɔ], both showing final consonant deletion. With moderate verbal cues, he imitated 3 of 5 two-syllable words correctly; with maximal cues, accuracy rose to 70% across trials.

Oral mechanism exam was within normal limits. Hearing was confirmed within normal limits per the August 14, 2026 screening. Relevant diagnostic code: ICD-10 F80.2 (Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder). Billed service code for the evaluation session: CPT 92523.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Mateo communicates primarily through gestures, a small set of single words in Spanish and English, and vocal protests when frustrated. He understands simple directions in both languages when paired with gesture (e.g., "dame el perro" / "give me the dog"). He imitates environmental sounds and some animal sounds. He engages in brief parallel play with Sol but does not yet initiate turn-taking games independently. Family and daycare report he is social, affectionate, and motivated to communicate, but his limited intelligibility (estimated 30% intelligible to unfamiliar listeners) causes frustration several times daily.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 2-word combinations in Spanish and/or English to request, comment, and protest across home and daycare settings, as measured by caregiver log and clinician observation, by April 2, 2027.
Strategies: Caregivers will model bilingual 2-word combinations during daily routines using Hanen It Takes Two to Talk strategies; Jennifer Alvarez will coach Lucía and Rosa during home visits; daycare staff will use a shared communication log.

Outcome 2: Mateo will produce final consonants in single words with no more than min cues in 8 of 10 opportunities across both languages, by April 2, 2027.
Strategies: Direct therapy using PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing targeting final /l/, /k/, and /t/; home practice with target words including "sol," "pan," and "cat."

Outcome 3: Mateo will engage in a shared turn-taking routine with Sol or a peer for at least 5 minutes with no more than mod cues, by July 2, 2027.
Strategies: Structured turn-taking games during family play time; daycare staff will facilitate paired play during center time; Jennifer Alvarez will model prompting hierarchy for caregivers and, as needed, introduce core vocabulary boards consistent with PECS principles for high-frustration moments.

The team discussed transition planning for Mateo's third birthday on January 14, 2027, including a referral packet to Durham Public Schools Exceptional Children's Division, to be initiated by October 14, 2026, six months prior to transition per state timelines.

This IFSP review was completed on 3 de marzo de 2025 at the family's home, with a second meeting on el martes 4 de marzo de 2025 at 10:00 a.m. to finish the outcomes section with both parents present.

2. SERVICE COORDINATOR AND CDSA OFFICE

Service Coordinator: María Gutiérrez, Piedmont Regional CDSA
CDSA Office Address: 210 Wicker Street, Sanford, NC 27330
Office Phone: (919) 718-2200
Service Coordinator Email: mgutierrez@piedmontcdsa.nc.gov

Evaluating and Treating Speech-Language Pathologist: Jenny Tran, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish), Carolina Bilingual Therapy Associates, PLLC
Physical Therapist: Mr. Tom Baker, PT, DPT
Interpreter present at intake: Sara Kim
Referring Pediatrician: Dr. Patel, Central Carolina Pediatrics

3. FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES

In the family's own words, recorded with interpretation support:

"Teo solo dice como diez palabras y se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos. Queremos que hable más, en español y en inglés, para que pueda decirle a su maestra lo que necesita." (Mother, Lucía Ramírez Gómez)

"At daycare they tell us he points instead of talking. We want him to use words before he starts school. We also worry because his sister Valentina talked so much earlier." (Father, Hugo Flores Martínez)

"Yo lo cuido todo el día y entiendo lo que quiere con señas, pero me preocupa que la maestra no lo entienda igual." (doña Lupe)

The family's priorities, in order, are: (1) increased spoken vocabulary in both languages, (2) reduced frustration behaviors (hitting, dropping to the floor) when Teo is not understood, (3) Teo following two-step directions at home and at daycare, and (4) building a shared set of words that doña Lupe, Miss Ana, and la maestra Carmen can all use consistently.

Family strengths noted: a close extended family, consistent routines led by doña Lupe, and strong motivation from both parents to carry over strategies around their work shifts.

4. DAILY ROUTINES

Teo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and has breakfast with doña Lupe while his parents leave for work. His mother, Lucía, trabaja en la planta empacadora de pollo del condado de Lee (the Lee County poultry processing plant), on the morning shift, 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.. His father, Hugo, trabaja para la compañía de construcción Triana (the Triana Construction Company), and leaves most days by 6:45 a.m., sometimes earlier when a job site is far from Sanford.

Teo attends Sunshine Beginnings Daycare from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. His teacher there, Miss Ana, reports that he plays well with peers, including his friend Josué and classmate Emily, but rarely initiates speech and instead pulls an adult's hand toward what he wants.

In the evenings the family eats together around 6:00 p.m., often with Diego helping set the table, and Teo bathes around 7:30 p.m. before a bedtime routine of books and songs with Valentina, usually finishing by 8:15 p.m..

On Sundays the family attends Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, where Teo goes to the toddler class taught by la maestra Carmen, and on Saturday mornings they sometimes visit relatives before Hugo's afternoon shift.

5. COMMUNITY RESOURCES AND OTHER AGENCIES

The family receives support from WIC and has an open case with Lee County Department of Social Services (DSS) for food assistance. The family was referred to Smart Start of Lee County for a childcare subsidy, which currently helps cover tuition at Sunshine Beginnings Daycare.

The family also attends the bilingual story time program at the Sanford Public Library most Wednesdays at 11:00 a.m., where Teo enjoys songs more than sitting for stories, and occasionally visits Hope Street Community Outreach, a local nonprofit food pantry, on the first Saturday of the month.

Teo's pediatrician, Dr. Patel, at Central Carolina Pediatrics, last saw him on 02/18/2025 for a well-child visit and referred the family back to this program for a hearing re-check, which is pending at UNC Lee County Hospital audiology.

6. PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

6.1 Communication

On February 10, 2025, Teo was administered the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale and the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish and English forms. He obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), with an age equivalent of 16 months. His expressive vocabulary across both languages was estimated at 14 words. He produced single words such as "agua," "mamá," and "up," with the target word "más" emerging only with moderate cues. No two-word combinations were observed in either language.

Oral-motor and phonological screening showed emerging production of /m/, /p/, and /b/, with /k/ and /s/ still absent from his repertoire; he reduced "agua" to "[awa]."

Birth history is significant for a 37-week gestational age and a birth weight of 5 lbs 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9. A hearing screening at birth was within normal limits.

6.2 Motor and Adaptive

Mr. Tom Baker administered the Battelle Developmental Inventory, Third Edition motor domain on 02/10/2025; Teo scored within the average range, standard score 94, and ambulates independently with no gait concerns.

7. IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Teo will use two-word combinations in Spanish and English to request and comment, in 8 of 10 opportunities, across home and daycare, by September 3, 2025.
Strategies: Model target words at the family's eye level using PROMPT cueing at a moderate cue level; doña Lupe and Miss Ana will narrate routines in short phrases; introduce a core-word board with PECS-style icons for snack and play requests.

Outcome 2: Teo will follow two-step directions without gestural cues in 3 of 5 trials at home, daycare, and church class by September 3, 2025.
Strategies: Pair verbal directions with a consistent visual schedule; la maestra Carmen will use the same picture schedule during the toddler class; use min to mod cues and fade support over time.

Outcome 3: The family will report a decrease in frustration behaviors from daily to 2–3 times per week by September 3, 2025, as Teo's expressive language increases.
Strategies: Teach the family simple sign cues (more, done, help) alongside spoken words; Jenny Tran will coach Lucía and Hugo during alternating evening visits so both parents receive direct coaching around their work schedules.

Outcome 4: Teo will imitate and later approximate the phonemes /k/ and /s/ in single words, achieving 60% accuracy in structured play, by September 3, 2025.
Strategies: Use a Hanen-based "It Takes Two to Talk" framework during family play; practice target words bilingually (casa/house, sopa/soup) with visual and tactile cues.

8. EARLY INTERVENTION SERVICES AND SCHEDULE

Speech-Language Therapy: 2x weekly, 45-minute sessions, provided by Jenny Tran under Carolina Bilingual Therapy Associates, PLLC. Sessions are held Mondays at 9:00 a.m.–9:45 a.m. at Sunshine Beginnings Daycare, and Thursdays at 5:00 p.m.–5:45 p.m. at the family's home, to fit around Lucía's and Hugo's shifts.

Physical Therapy consultation: monthly, 30 minutes, provided by Mr. Tom Baker, first session el martes 4 de junio de 2025 at 2:30 p.m., held at the CDSA office at 210 Wicker Street.

Service Coordination: contact at minimum every 6 months, and as needed by phone, with the next in-home visit tentatively set for July 2025.

Next full IFSP review scheduled for September 3, 2025.

Transportation: Not needed; family provides own transportation.

9. REVIEW AND SIGNATURES

# INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE
## Speech-Language Evaluation Report

**Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates** — Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates
Bilingual Early Intervention & School-Age Services

---

**1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION / Información de Identificación**

Client / Niño: Mateo Alejandro Fuentes Ríos ("Teo")
Date of Birth: April 18, 2021 — Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;6
Evaluation Dates: October 1, 2026 and October 3, 2026
Report Date: October 9, 2026
Evaluator: Katherine Bell, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Interpreter Present: Tom Alvarez, Spanish Medical/Educational Interpreter
Referral Source: Dr. Angela Ruiz, Pediatrician, WakeMed Children's Primary Care — Garner, NC
Service Coordinator: Monica Hayes, Wake County CDSA

Medicaid ID: 784213659M
Insurance Member ID (NC Health Choice Supplemental): HC-0094417
NC ITP Child ID: ITP-27529-0183
Record/Authorization Number: AUTH-2026-10452

Home Address: 412 Palomino Court, Garner, NC 27529 (Wake County)
Parent Contact: (919) 555-2487 (mother, Lucía Fuentes Vega); (919) 555-8360 (father, Daniel Ríos Martínez)
Email: lfuentesvega26@gmail.com

---

**2. REASON FOR REFERRAL / Motivo de la Referencia**

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech and language evaluation by Dr. Angela Ruiz following concerns raised at his 4;6 well-child visit on September 22, 2026 regarding limited intelligibility and reduced sentence length in both English and Spanish. His mother, Lucía, reports, "A veces se frustra porque no lo entendemos, y empieza a llorar o se va solo a su cuarto." His teacher, la maestra Carmen, at El Nido de Sueños Early Learning noted similar concerns during a parent conference on September 10, 2026, stating that Mateo often points or gestures rather than using words to request items during circle time.

Mateo's maternal grandmother, doña Lupe, who provides after-school care three afternoons per week, also expressed concern, telling the evaluator through the interpreter, "Yo le hablo despacito, pero él no me contesta con oraciones, solo palabras sueltas." This evaluation was requested to determine eligibility for continued early intervention services and to guide programming as Mateo transitions toward kindergarten.

---

**3. BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / Historia del Nacimiento y Médica**

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestational age via scheduled cesarean section at WakeMed Cary Hospital on April 18, 2021. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Per maternal report, pregnancy was unremarkable aside from mild gestational hypertension managed with medication during the third trimester.

Mateo experienced recurrent otitis media between 8 months and 26 months of age, with four documented episodes treated with antibiotics. Bilateral myringotomy tubes were placed on March 14, 2023 by Dr. Samuel Oyelaran, Pediatric ENT, with resolution of recurrent infections afterward. A hearing screening conducted on March 14, 2023 at the time of tube placement showed results within normal limits bilaterally. No additional audiological concerns have been reported since.

Mateo is otherwise in good general health. His pediatrician, Dr. Angela Ruiz, confirms no current diagnoses of autism spectrum disorder, though a developmental screening referral is pending given language and social communication concerns. Family medical history is significant for a maternal uncle with a reported history of late talking that resolved by early elementary school, per Lucía's report.

---

**4. FAMILY, DEVELOPMENTAL, AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje**

Mateo lives at home with his mother, Lucía Fuentes Vega; his father, Daniel Ríos Martínez; his older brother, Santiago "Santi" Ríos (age 7); and his infant sister, Camila Ríos (age 1). The family's dog, Rex, is also described as "part of the family" and is frequently mentioned in Mateo's spontaneous speech samples ("Rex comió," "Rex está afuera").

Lucía works second shift as a sorter at Blue Ridge Linens, a commercial laundry facility, and Daniel is employed with Carolina Turf Masters, a landscaping company based in Garner. Because of their work schedules, doña Lupe (maternal grandmother) and occasionally Tía Rosa (maternal aunt) provide childcare in the late afternoons and some weekends.

Language exposure in the home is primarily Spanish. Lucía reports that she and Daniel speak almost exclusively Spanish to Mateo at home, while Santi frequently code-switches with his brother, mixing English learned at school with Spanish. doña Lupe speaks only Spanish. Lucía described Mateo's early language milestones as follows: "Dijo 'mamá' y 'papá' como al año, pero después no agarró más palabras hasta casi los dos años y medio." First words in Spanish were reported around 12 months; however, vocabulary growth was notably slow, with parents estimating fewer than 20 words by 24 months. Two-word combinations did not emerge consistently until approximately 36 months.

The family attends Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza most Sundays, where Mateo participates in a children's Sunday school class led by Miss Ana, who has also commented that Mateo "sigue instrucciones sencillas pero no habla mucho con los otros niños." The family also regularly attends a bilingual story-time program, "Cuentos y Cantos," through Wake County Public Libraries, and Lucía has connected with El Puente Hispanic Family Center for parenting workshops and English classes. Lucía stated that staff at El Puente Hispanic Family Center first suggested she ask the pediatrician about a speech evaluation.

---

**5. EDUCATIONAL HISTORY / Historia Educativa**

Mateo has attended El Nido de Sueños Early Learning since August 2023, currently enrolled in the four-year-old classroom four days per week. His primary teacher, Carmen Pérez (referred to by the family as la maestra Carmen), reports that Mateo is social and affectionate with peers but relies heavily on gesture and single words to communicate needs. His classroom assistant, Ana Gómez (known to the family as Miss Ana — note this is a different Miss Ana than the one at church, per clarification from Lucía), echoed similar concerns, noting that Mateo becomes easily frustrated during transitions when he cannot verbally express what he wants.

Mateo has one close friend in his classroom, Jayden, with whom he reportedly plays well during outdoor time, and a classmate named Valentina who Mateo often imitates during group songs. la maestra Carmen noted, "Con Jayden se ríe mucho, pero casi no le dice frases completas — más bien lo jala de la mano."

Mateo received early intervention services beginning at 30 months through Wake County CDSA, including monthly developmental therapy and a speech-language consultation. His current IFSP (reviewed June 15, 2026) includes Outcome #2, targeting expressive vocabulary growth in both languages, and Outcome #3, targeting two-word combinations across contexts.

---

**6. OTHER SERVICES AND PROVIDERS / Otros Proveedores**

Mateo receives occupational therapy twice monthly with Jennifer Shaw, OTR/L, addressing mild fine motor delays affecting pencil grasp and self-feeding. He also receives physical therapy consultation as needed with Mark Delgado, PT, DPT, related to toe-walking observed in toddlerhood, which has since resolved. Both providers are based out of Wake County CDSA's contracted provider network.

Mateo's pediatric care continues with Dr. Angela Ruiz at WakeMed Children's Primary Care. The family also participates in the WIC nutrition program and has previously received home-visiting support through Smart Start of Wake County during Mateo's infancy.

---

**7. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS / Procedimientos y Observaciones**

Evaluation sessions were conducted bilingually in the clinic playroom at Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates with Tom Alvarez interpreting parent interview content and supporting rapport-building in Spanish. Standardized assessments were administered in both English and Spanish where dual-language norms were available; informal language sampling was conducted in both languages separately to assess each language system independently, consistent with best practice for bilingual assessment.

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and books. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of approximately 15-20 minutes before requiring a break. Rapport was established quickly; Mateo smiled and made eye contact consistently, and he enjoyed turn-taking games such as rolling a ball and stacking blocks. During less structured play, he vocalized frequently but relied on single words and gestures ("más," pointing to a snack; "arriba," reaching to be picked up) more than age expectations would predict.

Hearing was screened informally through parent and teacher report; no concerns were raised, and formal audiological results from March 14, 2023 were within normal limits. Oral-motor structures and function appeared within normal limits for speech production. Behavior throughout testing was cooperative, and results are considered a valid representation of Mateo's current skills in both languages.

---

**8. TEST RESULTS / Resultados de las Pruebas**

| Measure | Language | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) — Auditory Comprehension | English | 78 | 7th percentile | 3;1 | ±6 |
| PLS-5 — Expressive Communication | English | 71 | 3rd percentile | 2;9 | ±5 |
| Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition — Spanish — Comprensión Auditiva | Spanish | 82 | 12th percentile | 3;4 | ±6 |
| PLS-5 Spanish — Comunicación Expresiva | Spanish | 75 | 5th percentile | 2;11 | ±5 |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) | English | 73 | 4th percentile | — | ±7 |
| Contextual Probes of Articulation Competence — Spanish (CPAC-S) | Spanish | — | Informal — see narrative | — | — |

Informal conversational language sample (English, 50 utterances): mean length of utterance of 2.1 morphemes; intelligibility estimated at 60% to unfamiliar listeners, 80% to familiar listeners.

Informal conversational language sample (Spanish, 50 utterances): mean length of utterance of 2.4 morphemes; intelligibility estimated at 65% to unfamiliar listeners, 85% to familiar listeners.

**Articulation/Phonology Observations:**
Mateo demonstrated fronting of velar sounds in both languages, producing [t] for /k/ (e.g., "tasa" for target "casa") and [d] for /g/ (e.g., "dato" for target "gato"). Final consonant deletion was also noted in English productions, such as "ca" for target "cat" and "do" for target "dog." The Spanish tap /ɾ/ was produced inconsistently, often omitted in medial position (e.g., "paa" for target "para"). These patterns are consistent with a phonological process disorder rather than an isolated articulation delay, and notably affect both of Mateo's languages, supporting a true language-based difficulty rather than a second-language-acquisition pattern alone.

Mateo required moderate cues to imitate multisyllabic words accurately and achieved correct productions on 4 of 10 trials (40%) with min-mod cues during structured probes.

---

**9. CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS / Impresiones Clínicas**

Results of this bilingual evaluation indicate that Mateo presents with a **mixed receptive-expressive language disorder** affecting both English and Spanish, alongside a co-occurring **phonological process disorder**. Because deficits are present across both of Mateo's languages at comparable severity, these findings reflect a true language disorder rather than a typical pattern of sequential bilingual acquisition or a language difference attributable to reduced exposure.

Per ICD-10 code F80.2 (Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder) and F80.0 (Phonological Disorder), Mateo demonstrates significant delays in expressive vocabulary, grammatical morphology, sentence formulation, and speech sound production relative to same-age peers in both languages. As Lucía summarized during the feedback session, "Entonces no es que esté confundido por los dos idiomas — de verdad necesita ayuda." This is an accurate characterization: bilingualism is not the cause of Mateo's difficulties, and continued exposure to both English and Spanish at home should be strongly encouraged.

Mateo's social communication, play skills, and nonverbal engagement are notable strengths and support a positive prognosis with intervention. His family's engagement with community supports — including Wake County CDSA, El Puente Hispanic Family Center, and the Wake County Public Libraries story-time program — provides a strong foundation for carryover of therapy strategies into daily routines.

---

**10. RECOMMENDATIONS / Recomendaciones**

1. Mateo qualifies for continued early intervention services and should transition to a speech-language therapy plan addressing both languages, with services provided in Spanish, English, or both as appropriate, ideally by a bilingual provider or with consistent interpreter support (e.g., continued collaboration with Tom Alvarez).

2. Individual speech-language therapy is recommended at a frequency of **two sessions per week, 30 minutes each**, targeting:
   - Expressive vocabulary growth in both languages
   - Two- and three-word combinations and basic grammatical morphemes (plurals, present progressive -ing, Spanish verb conjugations)
   - Phonological awareness and velar sound production (/k/, /g/) and the Spanish tap /ɾ/
   - Functional communication strategies to reduce frustration-related behaviors

3. A Cycles approach to phonological intervention is recommended given the pattern of multiple affected processes across both languages.

4. Continue bilingual language exposure at home. Parents and doña Lupe should continue speaking their strongest, most comfortable language (Spanish) with Mateo, as this supports — rather than hinders — overall language development.

5. Coordinate with la maestra Carmen and Miss Ana at El Nido de Sueños Early Learning to implement classroom strategies, including modeling expanded utterances and offering structured choices to reduce reliance on gesture alone.

6. Continue coordination with Jennifer Shaw (OT) and Mark Delgado (PT) regarding any overlapping sensorimotor goals, and maintain communication with Dr. Angela Ruiz regarding developmental screening follow-up.

7. Re-evaluate in **6 months**, or sooner if progress plateaus, to monitor growth in both languages and reassess the need for continued services as Mateo approaches kindergarten entry.

8. Family is encouraged to continue participation in community language-rich activities, including Cuentos y Cantos story time and programming through El Puente Hispanic Family Center, both of which provide valuable bilingual language modeling opportunities outside of therapy.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Mateo. Please contact our office with any questions regarding this report or the recommendations above.

Respectfully submitted,

Katherine Bell, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates

Email: kbell@carolinapedstherapy.com

Programa de Intervención Temprana para Bebés y Niños Pequeños de Carolina del Norte — Revisión del Plan de Servicios Individualizado para la Familia (IFSP)

El 12 de agosto de 2026 se reunió el equipo del IFSP en las oficinas del CDSA del Piedmont Triad para realizar la revisión semestral de los servicios de Emiliano Castillo Reyes, a quien su familia llama cariñosamente "Emi". Emiliano nació el 3 de enero de 2024 y actualmente tiene 2;7 años de edad (31 meses). Su número de Medicaid es 785213469A y el número de caso del CDSA es CDSA-2025-04821. La coordinadora de servicios, Keisha Thompson, abrió la sesión y repasó el historial del expediente junto con la madre, Daniela Castillo Mendoza, y el padre, Jorge Reyes Lima, quienes asistieron en persona. Yo, Ana Beltrán, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe de Terapia Pediátrica Carolina del Piedmont, PLLC (conocida también como Terapia Pediátrica Carolina, o simplemente TPCP), serví como intérprete clínica y como proveedora principal de los servicios de lenguaje durante esta reunión.

La familia vive en 482 Calle Roble, en Mebane, en el condado de Alamance, código postal 27302. En casa conviven Emi, su hermana mayor Sol Castillo Reyes, de cinco años, y en ocasiones su abuela materna, Rosa Mendoza, quien llega varias tardes por semana para ayudar con la recogida en el programa preescolar y con la cena. La familia también tiene un perro llamado Max, que Emi disfruta mucho y que a veces se usa como motivador durante las sesiones de juego.

Durante la reunión, la madre expresó sus inquietudes en sus propias palabras: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Emi todavía no usa palabras para pedir lo que quiere; solo señala o llora, y a veces se frustra mucho." El padre añadió: "A nosotros nos gustaría que pudiera decirle a su maestra en la escuela qué le duele o qué necesita, porque en la casa medio lo entendemos pero en el salón no lo entienden tan fácil." La madre también comentó: "Quiero que aprenda a jugar con los otros niños, no solo al lado de ellos." Estas prioridades guiaron la revisión de los resultados del IFSP.

La rutina diaria de Emi comienza alrededor de las 6:30 a.m., cuando se despierta y desayuna con su hermana Sol. A las 8:00 a.m., la madre lo lleva al Programa Preescolar Caracolitos Felices, donde pasa la mayor parte del día en el salón de los "exploradores", junto a su amigo Diego y bajo el cuidado de la maestra principal, a quien el personal identifica en las notas de clase simplemente como "M.R.". Emi regresa a casa alrededor de las 4:30 p.m., generalmente recogido por su abuela Rosa Mendoza cuando la madre todavía está en el trabajo. La madre labora en Avance Manufacturing y suele llegar a casa cerca de las 5:45 p.m.. La cena familiar ocurre alrededor de las 6:15 p.m., seguida del baño y la rutina de cuentos antes de dormir, que comienza cerca de las 7:30 p.m.

El historial de desarrollo de Emi incluye un nacimiento a las 38 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 3,200 gramos y puntuaciones de Apgar de 8 y 9. No hubo complicaciones neonatales significativas. El pediatra de la familia, en la Clínica Pediátrica Valle Verde, refirió a Emi al programa de intervención temprana tras notar un retraso notable en el lenguaje expresivo durante la visita de los 18 meses. Una evaluación audiológica reciente en el Hospital Regional de Alamance descartó pérdida auditiva.

En la evaluación actualizada administrada con el Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), Emi obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 78 en el área de Comprensión Auditiva, ubicándolo en el percentil 7, y una puntuación estándar de 82 en Comunicación Expresiva, en el percentil 12. Su edad equivalente expresiva se estimó en 20 meses, con un intervalo de confianza del 95%. En la observación clínica, Emi combina en ocasiones dos palabras ("más upa", "no jugo") pero su inventario fonético es limitado; omite consistentemente los sonidos finales y sustituye /k/ y /g/ por [w] en posición inicial. Durante una actividad de juego con figuras del sol y la luna, se trabajó la palabra meta "sol", que resulta especialmente significativa para la familia porque es también el nombre de la hermana mayor, Sol; Emi logró aproximar la palabra como "to" con claves moderadas (mod cues), acercándose en 3 de 5 ensayos. Respondió a su nombre y mantuvo atención conjunta en 8 de 10 oportunidades estructuradas, un avance notable comparado con la evaluación inicial.

Con base en estos hallazgos y en las prioridades expresadas por la familia, el equipo revisó y actualizó tres resultados del IFSP. El Resultado 1 establece que Emi usará al menos quince palabras o aproximaciones consistentes para pedir objetos y acciones preferidas durante las rutinas diarias en casa y en el programa preescolar. Las estrategias incluyen el uso del enfoque Hanen para que los adultos amplíen los enunciados del niño, la incorporación de claves gestuales y visuales durante la merienda y el juego, y la práctica de palabras meta funcionales como "más", "agua" y "sol" en contextos naturales. El Resultado 2 se enfoca en que Emi inicie interacciones sociales con sus compañeros, como su amigo Diego, al menos tres veces durante el tiempo de juego libre, usando gestos, sonidos o palabras aproximadas; la estrategia principal es el modelado paralelo por parte de la maestra M.R. y el refuerzo de intentos comunicativos espontáneos. El Resultado 3 busca mejorar la inteligibilidad de Emi mediante el uso de un enfoque motor del habla; se recomendó introducir principios del método PROMPT para apoyar la producción de secuencias de sonidos consonante-vocal, con metas específicas en los fonemas /k/ y /g/ en posición inicial de palabra.

Los servicios de patología del habla y lenguaje continuarán con una frecuencia de dos sesiones semanales de 45 minutos cada una, en el modelo de rutina natural, proporcionadas por mí, Ana Beltrán, en representación de TPCP. Las sesiones se llevarán a cabo los martes y jueves, en el hogar de la familia, de 10:00 a.m. a 10:45 a.m., y una sesión adicional mensual de consulta con el personal del Programa Preescolar Caracolitos Felices se realizará los miércoles de 2:00 p.m. a 2:30 p.m. para apoyar la generalización de estrategias en el salón de clase. Estos servicios comenzaron el 20 de febrero de 2025 y continuarán hasta la próxima revisión programada, salvo que el equipo determine lo contrario.

Además de los servicios de lenguaje, la familia recibe apoyo de otras agencias. La familia está inscrita en el programa de WIC del condado para suplementos nutricionales, y Emi asiste part-time al programa de Early Head Start de Alamance dos mañanas por semana, de 9:00 a.m. a 12:00 p.m., como complemento al preescolar privado. La familia también coordina con una terapeuta ocupacional del CDSA, identificada en el expediente por sus iniciales, J. Ortiz, quien trabaja con Emi en regulación sensorial y en el seguimiento de instrucciones de un paso, con sesiones quincenales los lunes de 1:00 p.m. a 1:30 p.m. en el hogar.

Para contactar al equipo, la coordinadora de servicios Keisha Thompson puede ser localizada al (336) 555-0148, y las consultas sobre los servicios de lenguaje pueden dirigirse a Terapia Pediátrica Carolina al (336) 555-0193 o al correo intake@carolinapedspeech.example. La familia confirmó que prefiere recibir recordatorios de citas por mensaje de texto al número de la madre, (336) 555-0271.

Al cierre de la reunión, los padres firmaron el consentimiento para continuar los servicios según lo descrito. La madre reiteró: "Estamos muy agradecidos porque ya lo vemos intentar hablar más, antes casi no lo intentaba." El padre agregó que planea asistir a las sesiones los jueves cuando su horario de trabajo se lo permita. El equipo acordó que la próxima revisión del IFSP se realizará antes del 12 de febrero de 2027, o antes si surge algún cambio significativo en las necesidades de Emiliano. Se entregó a la familia una copia impresa del plan actualizado, junto con materiales visuales en español para apoyar las rutinas de comunicación en el hogar, incluyendo tarjetas con las palabras meta trabajadas en sesión y sugerencias para ampliar el vocabulario durante el baño, la hora de comer y el juego con Max.

Como nota adicional para el expediente, se documentó que durante la sesión del 15 de julio de 2026, Emi produjo de forma espontánea la aproximación [EW] al intentar decir "agua" mientras jugaba con su hermana Sol en el jardín trasero de la casa, lo cual fue reportado por la madre como un momento significativo de progreso. Este dato se incorporó al resumen narrativo de la evaluación y será monitoreado en las próximas sesiones como indicador de la emergencia de combinaciones consonánticas.

Firmado y revisado por el equipo interdisciplinario del CDSA del Piedmont Triad, con la participación de la familia Castillo Mendoza-Reyes Lima, la coordinadora de servicios Keisha Thompson, y la patóloga del habla y lenguaje Ana Beltrán de Terapia Pediátrica Carolina del Piedmont, PLLC.
