text:
+ Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fuentes
+ CA: 4;2
+ DOB: August 14, 2021
+ Date of Evaluation: October 2, 2025
+ Evaluator: Jennifer Marsh, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist, Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Associates
+ Interpreter: Rosa Fernández, Certified Medical Interpreter (Spanish)
+ Referral Source: Dr. Anil Patel, Pediatrician
+ Service Coordinator: James Alvarez, Mecklenburg County CDSA
+ Context: Clinic-based bilingual speech-language evaluation conducted at Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Associates, 4820 Monroe Road, Suite 210, Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, NC 28205. Session length: 90 minutes, 9:00 a.m. to 10:30 a.m.. Mother present throughout; interpreter present for all parent interview portions.
+ Medicaid ID: 803214567B
+ Case/Record #: LD-2025-00412
+ Clinic Phone: (704) 555-0148
+ Service Coordinator Email: jalvarez@mecklenburgcdsa.org

SUMMARY

Mateo is a 4;2-year-old bilingual Spanish/English-speaking boy referred by Dr. Patel for a comprehensive speech and language evaluation due to parent and teacher concerns regarding delayed expressive language, reduced speech intelligibility, and difficulty following multi-step directions in both languages. Mateo currently attends The Caterpillar Clubhouse three days per week and receives Early Head Start home-visiting services. He is enrolled with the Mecklenburg County CDSA under an active IFSP, with James Alvarez serving as service coordinator. Results of this evaluation indicate moderate delays in expressive language in both English and Spanish, mild-moderate delays in receptive language, and a moderate speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility, particularly in connected speech. Recommendations include continued speech-language therapy twice weekly, continuation of IFSP services, and a repeat audiological evaluation.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez, his father, Carlos Cruz, and his older sister, Sofía (age 7), at 482 Willow Bend Lane, Charlotte, NC 28208. Lucía reported that Mrs. Rodríguez's mother, whom the family calls doña Lupe, helps care for Mateo several afternoons a week while Lucía works. Lucía works nights at Palmetto Linen Services as a shift supervisor, typically 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., and Carlos works days at Ferreira Construction Group as a site foreman. Because of the parents' schedules, Mateo's primary daytime caregivers during the week are his teacher at The Caterpillar Clubhouse, known to the family as Miss Ana, and the center's Spanish-language instructional aide, whom the children call la maestra Carmen. Mateo's movement and gross-motor group at the center is led by Mr. Tom, who has also noted that Mateo has difficulty following multi-step verbal instructions during circle time.

The family was referred to Mecklenburg County DSS for a home visitation check approximately one year ago following a report of inadequate heating in the family's prior residence; that case was closed with no further concerns. The family also receives nutritional support through the Mecklenburg WIC Program and has participated in parenting workshops offered through Smart Start of Mecklenburg County. Mateo was enrolled in Early Head Start of Charlotte home-visiting services at 18 months of age following a developmental screening that flagged expressive language concerns; home visits are currently conducted twice monthly.

Mateo's IFSP was initiated on March 11, 2023 and most recently reviewed on September 9, 2025, with the next annual review scheduled for March 11, 2026. James Alvarez has coordinated services since intake and can be reached at the number listed above or at jalvarez@mecklenburgcdsa.org.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Lucía reported an uncomplicated pregnancy until 34 weeks gestation, when she was admitted for preterm labor. Mateo was born at 35 weeks gestational age at Blue Ridge Children's Hospital – Uptown Campus on August 14, 2021, with a birth weight of 4 pounds, 11 ounces and Apgar scores of 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. He required a 9-day stay in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Blue Ridge Children's Hospital – Uptown Campus for respiratory support and feeding difficulties, and was followed by the hospital's NICU follow-up clinic until approximately 14 months of age.

Mateo had recurrent ear infections between 8 months and 2;6, with bilateral tympanostomy tubes placed at 18 months of age. He is followed by Piedmont Crossing ENT & Audiology – SouthPark Office, where his most recent audiogram, completed by Dr. Helen Nguyen, audiologist, on June 3, 2025, showed normal hearing sensitivity bilaterally with normal tympanometry. No current ear infections are reported. Lucía denied any history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness. Mateo takes no current medications. Vision was reported as normal per the most recent well-child visit with Dr. Patel.

Developmental milestones were reported as mildly delayed: Mateo sat independently at 7 months, walked at 15 months, and said his first words around 20 months, notably later than his sister, Sofía, who spoke in short sentences by 18 months. Lucía reported that she raised her concerns about Mateo's language with Dr. Patel at the 18-month well-child visit, which prompted the Early Head Start referral.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo is being raised bilingually. Lucía speaks primarily Spanish with Mateo at home, while Carlos uses a mix of Spanish and English. Sofía speaks mostly English with Mateo and reportedly often "translates" for him with peers and adults outside the home, which Lucía described as a source of some frustration for Mateo. doña Lupe speaks only Spanish with Mateo during their time together. At The Caterpillar Clubhouse, instruction is primarily in English with some Spanish support provided by la maestra Carmen.

Lucía reported that extended family, including Mateo's grandmother abuela Rosa, who lives in the household part-time, are concerned that Mateo is "behind" both his sister and his cousins of the same age. Lucía denied any family history of autism but reported that Carlos's brother had a speech delay as a child and received therapy through elementary school. No other family history of hearing loss, learning disability, or genetic syndromes was reported.

At The Caterpillar Clubhouse, Miss Ana reported that Mateo plays well with peers but is sometimes difficult to understand, particularly by classmates such as Liam and Ethan, who often ask him to repeat himself or look to an adult to interpret. Miss Ana also noted that Mateo follows one-step directions reliably but frequently needs directions repeated or simplified when given in a sequence, such as during cleanup time.

At home, the family has a dog named Max, whom Mateo reportedly talks to frequently and whose name was one of Mateo's earliest clear words.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND RESULTS

Mateo was evaluated using standardized and informal measures in both English and Spanish, with interpreter support from Rosa Fernández for parent interview. Mateo separated easily from his mother, engaged readily with novel toys and the evaluator, and demonstrated age-appropriate attention for structured tasks with occasional redirection needed for longer verbal tasks.

Receptive and Expressive Language (Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish-Bilingual editions administered in each language; higher of composite scores used per bilingual scoring guidelines):

| Domain | Standard Score | Percentile | Confidence Interval | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 78 | 7th percentile | 95% CI: 71–85 | Mild-moderate delay |
| Expressive Communication | 70 | 2nd percentile | 95% CI: 63–77 | Moderate delay |
| Total Language Score | 73 | 4th percentile | 95% CI: 67–79 | Moderate delay |

Supplemental testing with the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Fifth Edition (CELF-5) Preschool subtests yielded the following:

| Subtest | Scaled Score | Percentile |
|---|---|---|
| Sentence Structure | 5 | 5th percentile |
| Word Structure | 6 | 9th percentile |
| Expressive Vocabulary | 6 | 9th percentile |

Mateo's performance was notably more consistent across languages than is typical for bilingual children at this stage, suggesting that his expressive language delay is a true delay rather than solely an artifact of dual-language exposure. In both English and Spanish, Mateo used primarily two- to three-word utterances ("more juice," "quiero eso," "dog go bye") with limited use of grammatical morphemes such as plurals, past tense markers, and possessives. Mean length of utterance in a 50-utterance spontaneous language sample was 2.3 morphemes, consistent with expectations for a child closer to 2;6–3;0.

Articulation and Phonology:

Using the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), Mateo obtained a standard score of 72 (3rd percentile). Speech intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at approximately 60% for familiar listeners and 30–40% for unfamiliar listeners. Phonological process analysis identified the following patterns:

- Final consonant deletion (e.g., "cat" produced as [kæ], occurring in 7 of 10 trials)
- Cluster reduction (e.g., "star" produced as [tɑɹ])
- Fronting of velars (e.g., /k/ and /g/ produced as [t] and [d], respectively)
- Gliding of liquids, with /ɾ/ in Spanish frequently produced as [l] (e.g., "para" produced as "pala")

With moderate cueing, Mateo was able to self-correct final consonant deletion in approximately 4 of 10 trials, suggesting stimulability for this pattern. He required maximal cues to approximate target production of /k/ in isolation and was not yet stimulable for the Spanish tap /ɾ/.

Oral-Motor and Feeding:

Oral-motor examination was within normal limits for structure and function at rest and during speech tasks. No feeding concerns were reported by Lucía or noted by this evaluator; Mateo eats a full range of age-appropriate textures.

Social Communication and Play:

Mateo demonstrated age-appropriate joint attention, eye contact, and symbolic play skills during the session, including extended pretend play sequences with toy animals. No concerns regarding social communication or restricted/repetitive behaviors were noted by this evaluator, Miss Ana, or Lucía, and Mateo does not currently carry an autism diagnosis.

IMPRESSIONS

Mateo presents with a moderate mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, more pronounced in expressive language, affecting both English and Spanish, consistent with a true language delay rather than typical bilingual second-language acquisition patterns. He additionally presents with a moderate speech sound disorder characterized by multiple phonological processes affecting intelligibility in both languages, with reduced stimulability for several target sounds. Given his history of recurrent otitis media and NICU stay, hearing status should continue to be monitored closely despite the most recent normal audiogram from Piedmont Crossing ENT & Audiology – SouthPark Office. Mateo's social communication and play skills are age-appropriate and are a relative strength to build on in intervention.

Relevant diagnostic coding for this encounter includes ICD-10 F80.2 (Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and ICD-10 F80.0 (Phonological disorder), billed under CPT 92523 (Evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) and CPT 92597 (not applicable, removed) — correction: billed under CPT 92523 only, with modifier GN applied per clinic policy for speech-language pathology services.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo should continue to qualify for Part C early intervention services and should be referred for continued speech-language therapy services under his existing IFSP with the Mecklenburg County CDSA, targeting IFSP Outcome 2 (expressive communication) and IFSP Outcome 3 (speech sound production).
2. Direct speech-language therapy is recommended twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, in a bilingual service delivery model, focusing on expanding utterance length, grammatical morphology, and phonological patterns in both English and Spanish.
3. A hybrid treatment approach combining principles of PROMPT for motor-based articulation goals and a modified Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" coaching model for caregiver language facilitation is recommended, given Lucía's and Carlos's strong interest in home carryover strategies.
4. Continued close coordination with Early Head Start of Charlotte home visitors and The Caterpillar Clubhouse staff, including Miss Ana and la maestra Carmen, is recommended to support generalization of targets across environments, including simplifying multi-step directions and pairing verbal cues with visual supports during transitions.
5. Repeat audiological monitoring is recommended at Piedmont Crossing ENT & Audiology – SouthPark Office within the next 6 months given Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media, to be coordinated by Dr. Nguyen in consultation with Dr. Patel.
6. The family should continue contact with James Alvarez at Mecklenburg County CDSA regarding the upcoming annual IFSP review on March 11, 2026, and may continue to access supports through Smart Start of Mecklenburg County and the Mecklenburg WIC Program as needed.
7. Reassessment of Mateo's speech and language skills is recommended in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and adjust IFSP goals accordingly.

This evaluator is available to discuss these findings further with the family, James Alvarez, or The Caterpillar Clubhouse staff as needed to support coordinated planning across settings. Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Mateo. Please contact Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Associates at (704) 555-0148 with any questions regarding this report.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Marsh, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Associates
Report Date: October 6, 2025

Coordinadora de servicios (SC): Diana Martínez, del CDSA del Suroeste de Carolina del Norte, Oficina de Fayetteville. Línea directa de la SC: (910) 555-2290.

SLP bilingüe que redacta esta nota: Yolanda Pérez, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Pequeños Pasos Terapia Pediátrica, PLLC (en adelante Pequeños Pasos o PPTP).

ANTECEDENTES: Mateo nació a las 37 semanas de gestación en Hospital WakeMed Cary, c/ Apgar de 8/9 y peso al nacer de 2,890 gramos. Referido al programa b/c retraso en lenguaje expresivo notado por pediatra Dr. Esteban Ruiz en visita de 24 meses. Eval. inicial completada 20 de mayo de 2025 por Yolanda Pérez, M.S., CCC-SLP; pt calificó p/ servicios b/c retraso significativo en comunicación expresiva.

Hermana mayor: Sol Hernández Cruz, de 7 años, asiste a la Escuela Primaria Oakview en Dunn. Mamá reporta que Sol "le habla a Mateo en inglés y español, y a veces hace de traductora en la casa, pero le decimos que Mateo tiene que intentar hablar primero."

Abuela materna: Carmen Reyes cuida a Mateo 2 días/sem mientras CG trabajan. Mamá Lucía trabaja en Supermercado La Economía en turnos variables; papá Carlos trabaja en construcción c/ horario irregular, a veces fuera del condado.

Mateo asiste al programa preescolar El Rinconcito de las Estrellas en Dunn, de lunes a viernes, 7:30 a.m. a 4:00 p.m.. Su maestra, Ana Gómez, reporta que Mateo juega paralelo c/ su compañero Bryan y c/ su compañera Daniela, pero rara vez inicia interacción verbal; prefiere señalar o jalar la ropa de la maestra p/ pedir ayuda.

PREOCUPACIONES/PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (palabras textuales):
"Yo quiero que Mateo pueda decirme qué necesita sin llorar. A veces se frustra mucho porque no lo entendemos." — Lucía Hernández Cruz
"Mi esposo y yo queremos que aprenda a jugar con su hermana Sol y que la escuela nos diga cómo ayudarlo en casa." — reportado en reunión del 8 de octubre de 2026.
Papá Carlos Cruz Medina agregó: "Quiero que hable más, aunque sea en español primero, no me importa el idioma. Lo importante es que se comunique."
Abuela Carmen Reyes comentó: "Cuando está conmigo, usa más señas que palabras. Yo le hablo despacio pero no sé si lo hago bien."

RUTINAS DIARIAS:
AM: despierta approx 6:45 a.m., desayuno c/ familia; CG lo viste c/ mod cues p/ seguir instrucciones de 1 paso ("dame el pie", "levanta el brazo"). Sale p/ El Rinconcito de las Estrellas approx 7:15 a.m..
Mediodía: siesta en daycare 12:30 p.m.–2:00 p.m.; come bien pero prefiere textura blanda; rechaza alimentos mixtos (ej. sopas c/ trozos).
PM: recogido por abuela Carmen Reyes approx 4:15 p.m.; tiempo de juego c/ Sol hasta cena approx 6:30 p.m..
Fines de semana: familia visita parque cercano en Dunn los sábados approx 10:00 a.m.; Mateo disfruta columpio y repite "más" c/ apoyo.
Noche: rutina de baño y cuento antes de dormir approx 8:00 p.m.; mamá reporta que señala objetos en el cuento pero usa pocas palabras espontáneas.

OTRAS AGENCIAS/APOYOS INVOLUCRADOS:
- WIC, oficina del Condado de Harnett — apoyo nutricional, revisión cada 3 meses.
- Smart Start de Harnett — subsidio parcial de cuidado infantil, renovación pendiente.
- DSS del Condado de Harnett — caso cerrado; sin servicios activos actualmente.
- Terapia ocupacional (OT) a domicilio por Marisol Alvarado, OTR/L, tb de Pequeños Pasos Terapia Pediátrica, PLLC, 1x/sem; nota de OT indica hipersensibilidad táctil leve.

EVALUACIÓN/PROGRESO (resumen desde última revisión):
Administrado PLS-5 Spanish 1 de octubre de 2026: Comprensión Auditiva puntaje estándar 78 (percentil 7); Expresión Verbal puntaje estándar 72 (percentil 3); Total de Lenguaje puntaje estándar 74; edad equivalente approx 18 meses. Intervalo de confianza 90%: 68-80.
Produce approx 35 palabras espontáneas en español, 8 en inglés. Combina 2 palabras en 2 de 10 oportunidades observadas. Fonológicamente omite consonantes finales; ej. dice "pato" → [pa], meta /t/ final ausente. Tb omite sílaba inicial en palabras de 3 sílabas.
En sesión de hoy produjo "upa" p/ "súbeme" c/ mod cues (modelo + espera estructurada), 7/10 ensayos correctos. Imitó /p/ y /m/ iniciales c/ min cues, 90% de precisión. Produjo "mamá", "agua", "más" espontáneamente durante merienda, 3 veces c/u.

RESULTADOS/OUTCOMES DEL PSFI:

Resultado 1: Mateo usará palabras o aproximaciones p/ pedir objetos/acciones deseadas en vez de llorar, en casa y en El Rinconcito de las Estrellas.
Estrategias: CG y maestra Ana Gómez usarán espera estructurada (3-5 seg) antes de dar el objeto; modelar frase de 1-2 palabras; reforzar cualquier aproximación verbal. Enfoque tipo Hanen (It Takes Two to Talk) revisado c/ CG el 8 de octubre de 2026.
Progreso: emergente; de 2/10 a 7/10 intentos verbales en sesión de hoy.

Resultado 2: Mateo combinará 2 palabras p/ comentar o pedir en rutinas diarias (comida, juego, baño) en el 75% de oportunidades observadas por CG en casa.
Estrategias: expansión de enunciados (CG repite + agrega 1 palabra); lectura compartida c/ vocabulario de rutina; práctica durante baño usando frases cortas modeladas por mamá y abuela Carmen Reyes.
Progreso: inicial; línea base 2/10, meta 75%, aún no alcanzada.

Resultado 3: Familia identificará 2 estrategias p/ apoyar el desarrollo bilingüe de Mateo y las usará consistentemente en rutinas c/ Sol y abuela.
Estrategias: uso flexible de "un hablante, un idioma" según comodidad familiar; traducción cruzada por Sol permitida pero no exclusiva; SLP proveerá lista de vocabulario bilingüe p/ rutinas de comida y baño.
Progreso: en curso; CG reporta mayor consistencia desde última revisión.

Resultado 4: Mateo aceptará ampliar variedad de texturas de alimento en daycare y casa, c/ apoyo de OT, p/ reducir selectividad alimentaria.
Estrategias: exposición gradual (programa tipo SOS modificado) c/ 1 textura nueva/sem; coordinación entre SLP y Marisol Alvarado, OTR/L; maestra Ana Gómez reportará aceptación en almuerzo escolar.
Progreso: recién iniciado; línea base 1 textura tolerada.

PLAN DE SERVICIOS Y HORARIOS:
SLP individual, en el hogar, 2x/sem, 30 min c/u. Próxima sesión 15 de octubre de 2026, 10:00 a.m.–10:30 a.m.; sesión siguiente 17 de octubre de 2026, 1:00 p.m.–1:30 p.m..
OT, 1x/sem, 45 min, jueves approx 9:00 a.m..
Coordinación de servicios por SC Diana Martínez, contacto mensual; próxima llamada approx 5 de noviembre de 2026.
Consulta en daycare c/ maestra Ana Gómez 1x/mes p/ generalizar estrategias; próxima visita 22 de octubre de 2026 approx 11:00 a.m..

TRANSICIÓN: familia fue informada verbalmente sobre el proceso de transición a Parte B (preescolar), que inicia approx a los 2;6–3;0 años. SC Diana Martínez enviará paquete escrito antes de 1 de enero de 2027. Se discutió posible evaluación de las escuelas públicas del condado si Mateo continúa calificando.

OBSERVACIONES ADICIONALES: mamá expresó preocupación de que algunas abreviaturas del expediente estén solo en inglés; SC acordó solicitar resumen en español p/ próxima reunión. Abuela Carmen Reyes confirmó disponibilidad p/ asistir a próxima visita de OT si CG no pueden.

text:
IFSP REVIEW — NC Infant-Toddler Program

Child: María José Fuentes Ramírez ("Majo")
DOB: January 14, 2024   CA: 2;9
CDSA Case ID: CDSA-2024-01837
Medicaid ID: 987654321A
Home address: 412 Willowbrook Lane, High Point, Guilford County, NC 27260
IFSP Review Date: October 9, 2026
Last IFSP: April 3, 2026
Session Time: 9:00 AM–9:50 AM, home visit

Team present: mother Lucía Ramírez Torres; father Carlos Fuentes Díaz (by phone); Service Coordinator Jennifer Walsh, Piedmont CDSA; Developmental Therapist Kayla Simmons; author/SLP Maria Hernández, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services. No interpreter needed; author bilingual Spanish/English.

Background: term birth at 38 weeks gestation, Apgar 8/9, birth weight 6 lbs 14 oz. No NICU stay. Referred to Piedmont CDSA at 19 months by pediatrician Dr. Angela Soto, Cone Health Pediatrics, for limited expressive vocab. Initial eligibility eval March 20, 2026. Older full sibling Diego Fuentes Ramírez (CA 5), no hx of speech/lang concerns, attends Fairview Elementary kindergarten.

S:
Mother Lucía Ramírez Torres reports gains since last IFSP but remains concerned re: intelligibility. Mother states "ya dice como quince palabras, pero todavía no junta dos palabras" ("she says about fifteen words now but still doesn't combine two words"). Family's top priority, in mother's words: "queremos que hable más para que la entiendan en la guardería" ("we want her to talk more so she's understood at daycare"). Father Carlos Fuentes Díaz, joining by phone from work, adds: "se frustra mucho en las tardes cuando no la entendemos" ("she gets very frustrated in the evenings when we don't understand her"), reports tantrums nightly around bathtime when Majo cannot get her point across.

Daily routine per mother: Majo wakes approx. 6:30 AM, breakfast with brother Diego Fuentes Ramírez before he leaves for school by 7:40 AM. Mother drops Majo at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center by 8:00 AM; pickup by 4:00 PM M–W–F, grandmother Rosa Torres Vega ("Abuela Rosa") picks up Tu/Th when mother works a later shift at the plant (through 6:00 PM). Abuela Rosa lives two streets over and provides backup care most weekends. Evening routine: dinner by 6:30 PM, bath 7:15 PM, bed by 8:00 PM; mother reports tantrums cluster around bath transition.

At Little Sprouts, lead teacher Monica Alvarez reports Majo plays well alongside peers, esp. classmate Isabella, and has begun imitating single words from Isabella during pretend play, but staff frequently cannot understand requests and redirect to pointing. Ms. Alvarez asked for written strategies given family's stated priority re: daycare communication.

Agencies/community supports in use: family receives food assistance through Guilford County DSS, caseworker Denise Patterson; enrolled with Guilford County WIC office on Elm Street for nutrition support; childcare subsidy coordinated through Smart Start of Guilford County, subsidy coordinator Rachel Kim, currently covering a portion of Little Sprouts tuition. Family attends a bilingual parent-child playgroup Tuesdays at 10:00 AM hosted at Our Lady of Guadalupe Catholic Church hall, and Saturday mornings attends the "Cuentos y Cantos" bilingual story-time program at the High Point Public Library. Mother reports both are helpful for Majo's exposure to peers and books in both languages.

Mother denies new medical concerns. Majo last seen by Dr. Soto at Cone Health Pediatrics on September 2, 2026; hearing screen within normal limits, no new diagnoses, growth tracking WFL. No current meds. Mother reports no feeding concerns; family eats mixed Mexican/American diet at home, no restrictions.

O:
Standardized testing readministered today: Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale. Receptive language age-equivalent 21 months (CA 33 months), delay of 9 months (63% of CA, below 90% cutoff). Expressive language age-equivalent 16 months, delay of 17 months (48% of CA). Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 attempted; limited stimulability for imitation items, Sounds-in-Words standard score 62 (CI 90%: 58-66), 1st percentile.

Prior comprehensive eval March 20, 2026 used Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4: Cognitive composite 88 (21st percentile); Language composite 70 (2nd percentile), with Receptive scaled score 7 and Expressive scaled score 4; Motor composite 97 (42nd percentile). Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test not administered at that visit due to age limit; informal expressive vocabulary checklist today documents approx. 18 single words used consistently across contexts, 0/10 spontaneous two-word combinations observed in 40-min session.

Spontaneous speech sample, home play with mother and SLP: 3/10 single-word utterances intelligible to unfamiliar listener (SLP, first exposure). Sample productions, target in quotes: "ba" for "ball", "'nana" for "banana", "ca" for "cat", "do" for "dog". Phonological patterns: final consonant deletion (consistent), stopping of fricatives, substitution of /b/ for /p/ word-initial. Vowel inventory within functional limits. No jargon, no echolalia noted. SALT-style transcript excerpt: [EW] marked on 2 unintelligible attempts during ball-rolling routine.

Trialed PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing for bilabial closure on /b/ and /p/ targets; Majo required mod cues to approximate target placement, improved to min cues by end of 10-min block for "ba" imitation, 4/6 trials correct with support. Joint attention within functional limits; responded to name 4/5 trials. Followed 1-step directions without gesture 3/5 trials; with added gesture cue, 4/5 trials (80%), compared to 40% at last review.

Oral mechanism exam within normal limits; no structural or functional feeding concerns observed, consistent w/ parent report. Symbolic play age-appropriate: fed doll with spoon, pretended to talk on toy phone, brief 2-step pretend sequences without prompting. No repetitive or restrictive behaviors noted during session.

Billing: CPT 92523 (speech/language eval) and CPT 92507 (individual tx) documented for today's combined review/treatment visit. Working diagnoses: ICD-10 F80.1 (expressive language disorder), F80.0 (phonological disorder).

A:
Majo continues to present with a moderate-to-severe expressive language delay that exceeds her receptive delay, consistent across the Bayley-4 administered in March 2026 and today's Rossetti findings. Phonological pattern of final consonant deletion and stopping is within range for typical bilingual Spanish/English development, but the magnitude of delay across both standardized measures and classroom report from Monica Alvarez exceeds what would be expected from bilingual exposure alone. Majo continues to meet NC Infant-Toddler Program eligibility criteria under the established expressive delay criterion.

Family's stated priorities, daycare intelligibility and reduction of evening frustration behaviors, align closely with current functional outcomes and should remain central to goal-writing. Progress toward Outcome #1 (word combinations) has not yet been met: mother reports zero spontaneous two-word combinations at home, and none were elicited in today's 40-minute sample despite structured opportunities. Outcome #2 (following routine directions) is substantially met, improving from 40% to 80% with gesture support since last review; recommend narrowing criterion toward directions without gesture cue going forward.

Response to PROMPT tactile cueing today (improvement from mod to min cues within a single 10-minute block) suggests Majo is a good candidate for continued motor-based articulation intervention alongside language-facilitation strategies. Family engagement is strong; both parents attended or called in for today's review, and mother has been consistently implementing home strategies discussed at last visit. Developmental Therapist Kayla Simmons concurs with continuing direct SLP services at current frequency and recommends joint home visit next quarter to coordinate play-based cognitive and communication targets.

Recommend continued direct SLP services 1x/week, addition of monthly consult contact with Little Sprouts staff given family's identification of daycare communication as the top concern, and introduction of a visual support tool to address evening frustration behaviors reported by father.

P:
1. Outcome #1 (continue, revised criterion): Majo will combine 2 words (noun+verb or noun+noun, in English or Spanish) in 4/5 opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions, per SLP data collection and parent log.
Strategy: expansion and parallel-talk modeling during daily play routines; mother to model 2-word combinations during bathtime and mealtime using Hanen "More Than Words" self-talk and parallel-talk strategies reviewed today; SLP to send a short home video example by next visit.

2. Outcome #2 (continue, narrowed criterion): Majo will follow 1-step directions without a gesture cue in 4/5 trials across home and daycare settings.
Strategy: Little Sprouts staff to pair verbal directions with a brief gesture and fade gesture support over 4 weeks; SLP to provide a bilingual (English/Spanish) written strategy sheet to family and Monica Alvarez by next visit.

3. Outcome #3 (continue): Majo will imitate bilabial sound targets (/b/, /p/) in single words with no more than min cues in 4/6 trials across 2 consecutive sessions.
Strategy: continue PROMPT-based tactile cueing during direct sessions; model target words during snack and ball-play routines at home; mother to practice "ba," "pa" word-initial targets 5 min daily during routine play.

4. New Outcome #4: family will report a reduction in frustration-related tantrums from nightly to 3 times per week or fewer by next review, measured via parent log, through consistent use of a visual choice board.
Strategy: SLP to construct a 4-picture choice board (more, help, all done, book) at next home visit for use during bath and transition times; Little Sprouts to use a matching board during daycare transitions; SC Jennifer Walsh to coordinate with Smart Start of Guilford County coordinator Rachel Kim to confirm continued subsidy funding so consistency of daycare attendance, and therefore strategy carryover, is maintained.

Services continuing: direct SLP, 1x/week, 45 minutes, home-based, delivered in English and Spanish per family preference, next session scheduled October 16, 2026 at 9:00 AM. Developmental Therapy continuing at current frequency per Kayla Simmons; joint SLP/DT home visit tentatively planned for January 2027 quarter.

Care coordination: SC Jennifer Walsh to follow up with Guilford County DSS caseworker Denise Patterson regarding renewal of the food assistance case, paperwork due November 1, 2026, and to confirm Guilford County WIC enrollment renewal prior to its expiration. SC to also share updated outcomes with Monica Alvarez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center for classroom carryover.

Next IFSP review scheduled April 9, 2027; annual comprehensive evaluation to include repeat Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale and a full-battery attempt of the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 once stimulability improves, plus consideration of the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test once Majo reaches the minimum age for administration.

Contacts: SC Jennifer Walsh, Piedmont CDSA, (336) 555-0148, jwalsh@piedmontcdsa.org. SLP Maria Hernández, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services, (336) 555-0291. Medicaid ID on file: 987654321A.

Signed: Maria Hernández, M.S., CCC-SLP
October 9, 2026

+ Name: Mateo Fernández
+ CA: 4;2
+ Context: Sesión de terapia de habla-lenguaje a domicilio, 482 Hollyhock Court, Fayetteville, 28314, el 8 de octubre de 2026 a las 3:30 p.m.

RESUMEN

S: La mamá, Lucía Fernández, reporta que Mateo asistió bien esta semana a Mundo de Estrellitas, su preescolar, donde la maestra, Srta. Carmen Osorio, indicó que Mateo jugó con su compañero Josué durante el círculo de cuentos. La familia también participa cada sábado en el programa de cuentos de la Biblioteca Regional de Cumberland, y asiste los domingos a la Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza, donde Mateo canta con el grupo infantil. Lucía comparte que la abuela, Rosa Fernández, ha estado cuidando a Mateo por las tardes mientras ella trabaja en Vance Textiles.

O: Se revisaron los resultados preliminares de la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale y el Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, administrados por Dana Whitfield, MS, CCC-SLP el 1 de octubre de 2026. Mateo obtuvo un puntaje estándar de 78 en comprensión auditiva y un 65% de inteligibilidad en conversación espontánea. Durante la sesión de hoy se trabajaron los sonidos /s/ y /l/ en el contexto de la palabra meta "sol", escogida en parte porque es también el nombre de su hermana, Sol Fernández. text:
NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM — INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) REVIEW

Child's Name:  Mateo Alejandro Fuentes Rodríguez  ("Teo")
Date of Birth:  08/14/2022        Chronological Age at Review:  3;1
NC ITP Child ID:  NC-ITP-448217        Medicaid ID:  800452913
Insurance Member ID:  BCB847162935        Prior Authorization #:  PA-2025-33847
CDSA Office:  Foothills Regional CDSA        County:  Alamance County
Service Coordinator:  Patricia Alvarado, M.Ed.        Phone:  (336) 555-2047
Family Address:  210 Persimmon Grove Road, Mebane, NC 27302
Mother:  Lucía Rodríguez Peña        Father:  Diego Fuentes Castillo
Home Language:  Spanish/English        Interpreter Needed:  No (bilingual provider)
Initial IFSP Date:  15 de noviembre de 2023        This Review Date:  30 de septiembre de 2025
Next Review Due:  30 de marzo de 2026        Annual IFSP Due:  11/15/2026
Report Written By:  Jennifer Soto-Hill, M.S., CCC-SLP        Employer:  Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC

BACKGROUND / HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO

Teo is the younger of two children born to Lucía Rodríguez Peña and Diego Fuentes Castillo. He was born at 38 weeks gestation with an Apgar score of 8/9 and a birth weight of 6 lbs 11 oz. His older sister, Camila, is in first grade and has no developmental concerns. Teo was referred to the Infant-Toddler Program by his pediatrician after his abuela Rosa Fuentes, who provides daytime care three days a week, reported that he was not combining words by 24 months. Diagnostic code on file: F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder). Billing for ongoing individual sessions uses CPT 92507; the initial evaluation was billed under CPT 92523.

RESUMEN DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY SUMMARY

La mamá, Lucía, trabaja de noche en Blue Ridge Poultry Processing en la línea de empaque, de lunes a viernes. ("Mom works nights at Blue Ridge Poultry Processing on the packing line, so my mother-in-law, Rosa, stays with the kids until I get home around 7 a.m.") El papá, Diego, trabaja con una cuadrilla de jardinería en Green Valley Landscaping & Lawn Care, y a veces llega tarde cuando hay mucho trabajo en el verano. La familia vive con la abuela Rosa Fuentes en la misma casa en Mebane.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

During the review meeting, Lucía shared, in her own words: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos. Grita, tira las cosas, y a veces se pega en la cabeza. Yo sé que él tiene cosas que decir pero no le salen las palabras." She also noted, "En la casa hablamos los dos idiomas, español con la abuela y un poquito de inglés porque mi esposo trabaja con americanos. Yo quiero que Teo hable los dos, pero primero quiero que pueda comunicarse, no importa en cuál idioma."

Diego added, "I just want him to be able to tell his sister what he wants without hitting her. Camila gets upset porque dice que su hermanito nunca la deja jugar bien porque no entiende las reglas."

Family priorities identified for this review:
1. Teo will use more words at home so his grandmother and parents understand his needs without guessing.
2. Teo will reduce hitting and head-banging when frustrated.
3. The family wants strategies that work in both Spanish and English, since Rosa speaks only Spanish and Diego mixes both at home.
4. Lucía would like help explaining Teo's needs to the staff at Casita de Sueños Early Learning Center, where he attends three mornings a week while Diego works.

RUTINAS DIARIAS / DAILY ROUTINES

Teo wakes around 7:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Rosa while Lucía is finishing her shift. On Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays, Rosa drops him at Casita de Sueños Early Learning Center on Chestnut Ridge Road by 9:00 a.m.. His teacher there, Miss Brenda, reports that he plays well in the sensory bin but has trouble with turn-taking during circle time; his favorite classmate, Kevin, often tries to pull him into pretend play that Teo does not yet follow. Bath time is around 6:00 p.m., and the family dog, Max, usually sits outside the bathroom door during this routine, which Teo enjoys and uses as motivation ("¿Dónde está Max?").

On Saturdays the family attends Iglesia Pentecostal Monte de Sion, where Teo goes to the nursery room during the second service; the nursery volunteers have asked Lucía for simple sign strategies because he becomes overwhelmed by the noise. Sundays are often spent at Alamance County Public Library for the "Bebés y Libros" story-time program, which Lucía says is "lo único gratis que podemos hacer todos juntos los cuatro." The family also receives support through WIC at the Mebane office and recently enrolled in a parenting class through Alamance Smart Start.

OTHER AGENCIES / OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

- Foothills Regional CDSA: service coordination, ongoing eligibility
- Alamance Smart Start: parent education class, Tuesdays 6:00 p.m.
- WIC: nutrition support, recertification due el martes 4 de noviembre
- Iglesia Pentecostal Monte de Sion: nursery accommodations, informal family support
- Alamance County Public Library: "Bebés y Libros" bilingual story-time program
- Pediatrician: Dr. Rebecca Osei, UNC Children's Primary Care at Mebane

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT / NIVELES ACTUALES DE DESARROLLO

Communication: Administration of the PLS-5 (Spanish and English forms, composite scoring) on 09/22/2025 yielded an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 72 (3rd percentile), with a 95% confidence interval of 68-80 for the Total Language score. Age equivalent for expressive language fell at 18 months. On the CELF Preschool-3 Spanish supplement, Teo produced a mean length of utterance of 1.4 morphemes; sample utterances included "más agua," "no quiero," and "ayuda mamá." SALT-coded transcript notes flagged frequent [EW] (exclamatory word) tags during moments of frustration.

Speech sound production: Teo substitutes /t/ for /k/ and /d/ for /g/ in word-initial position (e.g., "tat" for target "cat," "dato" for target "gato"). He produces final consonant deletion in both languages, e.g., "pa" for "pan." With moderate cues he self-corrected to approximate [k] in two of ten trials (2/10). Stimulability for /g/ was present with minimal cues (8/10).

Social-emotional: Teo bangs his head against the floor or furniture an average of 3 times per session when a request is not immediately understood, decreasing to 1 time per session when a visual choice board is offered.

Gross/fine motor: Within normal limits; no concerns noted by the occupational therapy consultant, Marcus Whitfield, OTR/L.

STRATEGIES / ESTRATEGIAS

The team, including Jennifer Soto-Hill, Patricia Alvarado, and the family, discussed strategies grounded in Hanen It Takes Two to Talk principles for the home and daycare settings, combined with PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing for speech sound targets during direct sessions. A picture exchange system modeled loosely on PECS will be introduced at Casita de Sueños Early Learning Center to reduce frustration during transitions, with Miss Brenda trained to use it consistently.

Lucía noted during planning, "Si le damos las fotos para escoger, a lo mejor no se enoja tanto. En la casa yo puedo hacer lo mismo con las fotos de la comida."

IFSP OUTCOMES

Outcome 1: Teo will use two-word combinations in Spanish and/or English to request desired items or activities, in 4 of 5 opportunities across home, daycare, and therapy settings, as measured by provider observation and parent report.
Strategy: Model expansion ("quiero agua" for "agua"); use the picture board at Casita de Sueños Early Learning Center and at home; Rosa and Diego will be coached on bilingual modeling during weekly home visits.

Outcome 2: Teo will reduce self-injurious behavior (head-banging) to 0-1 episode per day by using a visual choice board or gesture to communicate wants/needs, as measured by a home behavior log kept by Lucía and reviewed biweekly.
Strategy: Introduce a core visual board with 12 high-frequency items in both languages; reinforce immediately when Teo points or vocalizes instead of hitting.

Outcome 3: Teo will produce initial /k/ and /g/ in single words with no more than minimal cues in 8 of 10 trials across three consecutive sessions.
Strategy: PROMPT cueing for tongue-back placement; practice in both "gato/cat" and "casa/house" word sets to support bilingual carryover.

Outcome 4: The family will identify and use one calming strategy consistently across the three caregiving settings (home with Lucía and Diego, home with Rosa, and Casita de Sueños Early Learning Center) within 8 weeks.
Strategy: Team will coordinate a shared one-page visual script, translated into Spanish, for use by Rosa and Miss Brenda.

SERVICE DELIVERY

Speech-Language Therapy:  30 minutes, 1x/week, home-based        Provider:  Jennifer Soto-Hill, M.S., CCC-SLP
Service Coordination:  monthly contact, home or phone        Provider:  Patricia Alvarado, M.Ed.
Developmental Consultation (OT, as needed):  quarterly        Provider:  Marcus Whitfield, OTR/L
Location of Services:  210 Persimmon Grove Road, Mebane, and Casita de Sueños Early Learning Center on Chestnut Ridge Road
Start Date of Services:  11/15/2023        Anticipated Duration:  through 03/30/2026 review

NEXT STEPS / PRÓXIMOS PASOS

1. Jennifer Soto-Hill will deliver the translated visual script to Rosa and Miss Brenda by el martes 4 de noviembre.
2. Patricia Alvarado will follow up with Alamance Smart Start regarding the parenting class schedule change for 3 de marzo de 2025 cohort closing and re-enrollment for the spring session.
3. Family will bring behavior log data to the next contact on 30 de octubre de 2025.
4. Annual IFSP meeting scheduled for 11/15/2026; six-month review scheduled for 30 de marzo de 2026.
5. Team will request updated WIC recertification documentation after the el martes 4 de noviembre appointment and share with the CDSA record file under authorization PA-2025-33847.

PARENT SIGNATURE: _________________________ Lucía Rodríguez Peña        DATE: 30 de septiembre de 2025
PARENT SIGNATURE: _________________________ Diego Fuentes Castillo        DATE: 30 de septiembre de 2025
SERVICE COORDINATOR SIGNATURE: _________________________ Patricia Alvarado        DATE: 30 de septiembre de 2025
SLP SIGNATURE: _________________________ Jennifer Soto-Hill, M.S., CCC-SLP        DATE: 30 de septiembre de 2025

CONTACT INFORMATION ON FILE

Family Phone (Lucía):  (336) 555-8812        Family Phone (Diego):  (336) 555-9034
Service Coordinator Email:  patricia.alvarado@foothillscdsa.org
SLP Email:  j.sotohill@carolinabilingualtherapy.com
Record/Case File #:  FRC-2023-01187

NOTAS ADICIONALES / ADDITIONAL NOTES

Lucía mentioned that she worries Teo will be "behind" when he starts pre-k next year, since most of the other children at Casita de Sueños Early Learning Center, including Kevin and Sofía, already speak in full sentences. The team reassured the family that bilingual exposure is not the cause of the delay and that continued intervention in both languages is appropriate and recommended. Diego asked whether the family could request a Saturday session occasionally when his landscaping schedule is lighter in winter; the team agreed to revisit scheduling flexibility at the 30 de marzo de 2026 review. Rosa was present for part of the meeting and expressed relief that strategies would be available in Spanish: "Yo quiero ayudar pero a veces no sé qué hacer cuando él se frustra tanto."

End of IFSP Review Document.

Se administraron partes de la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale y de la Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) como parte del monitoreo trimestral. Mateo obtuvo un puntaje estándar de 78 en el área receptiva y 72 en el área expresiva, ubicándolo en el percentil 9. En la subprueba de articulación, produjo correctamente 8 de 10 palabras objetivo, con dificultad persistente en los fonemas /s/ y /ɾ/. Al pedirle que repitiera la palabra objetivo "pato", produjo "paɾo", mejorando a "pato" con claves moderadas. También se revisaron resultados previos de la Bayley Scales of Infant Development-4 (Bayley-4) y de la Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5), administradas en agosto de 2026 por el equipo del CDSA del Piedmont.

ANÁLISIS:
Mateo continúa mostrando progreso lento pero constante hacia el objetivo 2 del IFSP, relacionado con el aumento del vocabulario expresivo y la inteligibilidad. Se nota mayor interacción social con Ethan y Camila en comparación con sesiones anteriores, lo cual favorece la generalización de los sonidos trabajados. La familia reporta que la abuela, Rosa Cruz, también refuerza el lenguaje en casa durante las tardes mientras Lucía trabaja. Se recomendó a Lucía contactar al pediatra, Dr. Esteban Ramírez, para una revisión auditiva de seguimiento antes de la próxima reunión del IFSP.

PLAN:
Se coordinará con Ana Gómez de ACCSTA para programar la revisión del IFSP el 15 de diciembre de 2026 a las 2:30 p.m. en las oficinas del CDSA del Piedmont. La próxima sesión de terapia será el 16 de octubre de 2026 a las 10:00 a.m. en Escuela Primaria Oak Hill. Se continuará utilizando el enfoque PROMPT y el programa Hanen para apoyar la comunicación funcional en el hogar y en el salón de clases. Cualquier pregunta puede dirigirse a Laura Martínez al (336) 555-0199 o por correo a lmartinez@terapiaspedcarolina.com.

text:
CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

- Child: Mateo Alejandro Flores Díaz (called Teo at home)
- Date of birth: April 11, 2023
- Chronological age at evaluation: 2;6
- Evaluation dates: October 2, 2026 and October 6, 2026
- Report date: October 9, 2026
- Parents/Guardians: Lucía Rodríguez Flores (mother), Carlos Flores Méndez (father)
- Home address: 418 Esperanza Lane, Durham, Durham County, NC 27703
- Home phone: (919) 555-0148
- Mother's cell: (919) 555-0177
- Email: lucia.rodriguez0411@gmail.com
- Primary languages: Spanish (home), English (emerging)
- Referral source: Dr. Michael Chen, pediatrician
- Examiner: Jennifer Caldwell, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish)
- Clinic: Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
- Clinic phone: (919) 555-0199
- Service coordinator: Gabriela Santos
- Service coordination agency: Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Infantiles y Familiares del Condado de Durham (short form: ACSIF)
- CDSA office: Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Piamonte (short form: CDSA del Piamonte)
- CDSA case number: CDSA-04471-PB
- Medicaid ID: 987654321A
- Child ID: LDS-22890

BACKGROUND AND REASON FOR REFERRAL

- Mateo was referred to CDSA del Piamonte by Dr. Michael Chen at his 24-month well-child visit on April 18, 2025, due to limited expressive vocabulary and reduced intelligibility noted by both the pediatrician and the family.
- His mother, Lucía Rodríguez Flores, reports that Mateo uses fewer than ten consistent words across both languages and relies heavily on pointing and pulling adults toward what he wants.
- The family was connected to CDSA del Piamonte through Durham Early Head Start, where Mateo attends part-time.
- Carlos Flores Méndez, Mateo's father, reports similar concerns and notes that Mateo's older sister, Sol, was talking in short sentences by this same age.
- The family's service coordinator, Gabriela Santos of ACSIF, requested this evaluation to inform eligibility determination and IFSP outcome development.
- This evaluation was conducted in the family's home and at the clinic, with portions of history-taking and parent interview conducted in Spanish by the bilingual examiner, Jennifer Caldwell.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

- Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Duke University Hospital via uncomplicated vaginal delivery.
- Birth weight was 6 lbs 14 oz; Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes.
- There were no complications during the pregnancy, delivery, or newborn period, per maternal report.
- Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening bilaterally and has had no documented ear infections or episodes of otitis media.
- A tympanometry screening completed at September 28, 2026 by David Kim, audiologist, showed Type A tympanograms bilaterally, consistent with normal middle ear function.
- Medical history is otherwise unremarkable: no history of seizures, head injury, or hospitalization beyond birth.
- Mateo is up to date on immunizations and sees Dr. Michael Chen at Duke Regional Medical Center pediatric clinic for routine care.
- Gross and fine motor milestones were reported as age-appropriate: Mateo walked independently at 13 months and currently climbs stairs with alternating feet.
- No prior speech-language services have been provided.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

- Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Carlos Flores Méndez, his older sister, Sol, age four, and his maternal grandmother, Esperanza Díaz, who provides childcare several days a week.
- The family's primary home language is Spanish. Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Esperanza Díaz speak almost exclusively Spanish to Mateo, while Carlos Flores Méndez uses a mix of Spanish and English.
- Sol is described as bilingual, switching easily between languages, and often serves as an informal interpreter for Mateo with English-speaking visitors.
- Lucía Rodríguez Flores works part-time as a housekeeping aide at Duke Regional Medical Center; Carlos Flores Méndez works full-time at the Perdue Farms processing plant in Garner.
- The family attends services weekly at Iglesia Bautista Monte Sion, where Mateo participates in a toddler nursery program alongside other young children from the congregation.
- The family also regularly attends a Spanish-language storytime program at the Durham County Public Library South Branch, which Lucía Rodríguez Flores credits with helping Sol's early English exposure.
- The family receives nutrition support through WIC and has previously worked with Smart Start of Durham County for a parenting education series.
- The family has an open case with Durham County Department of Social Services related to housing assistance; this is unrelated to any child welfare concern.
- The family's pet, a small dog named Rex, is frequently mentioned by Sol and is a favored topic during play-based assessment.
- No other languages are spoken in the home. The family denies any family history of speech, language, or hearing disorders, though Carlos Flores Méndez reports that his own brother was "a late talker" who later caught up without services.

DAYCARE AND EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

- Mateo attends Durham Early Head Start three mornings per week, where his lead teacher is Amanda Lopez.
- Amanda Lopez reports that Mateo is social and affectionate with peers but frequently frustrated when he cannot communicate his wants, sometimes resulting in pushing or crying.
- A classmate, Emma, is described as Mateo's preferred play partner; the two frequently engage in parallel play with blocks and cars.
- On days the family needs additional care, Mateo attends Sunshine Christian Daycare near the family home, supervised by staff familiar with his limited verbal communication.
- Amanda Lopez completed a classroom communication checklist on September 22, 2026 indicating that Mateo follows simple one-step directions in English approximately 6 of 10 trials but rarely initiates verbal requests.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

- Mateo presented as a friendly, curious toddler who separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and the examiner.
- Eye contact and joint attention were age-appropriate; Mateo consistently followed the examiner's point and gaze.
- Play skills included functional and emerging symbolic play, such as feeding a stuffed animal and pushing a toy car while making an engine sound.
- Mateo used frequent gestures, including pointing, reaching, and pulling adults by the hand, to communicate across both assessment sessions.
- Attention and engagement were adequate for standardized testing with brief redirection needed approximately every 8-10 minutes.
- No concerns were noted regarding oral motor structure or function; the oral mechanism exam was within normal limits for symmetry, strength, and range of motion.

ASSESSMENT INSTRUMENTS ADMINISTERED

- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (parent interview and direct observation, administered in Spanish and English)
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4), Language and Cognitive subtests
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) (English, screening administration)
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5) (English, screening administration, scores interpreted with caution given bilingual status)
- Spanish single-word articulation and vocabulary screening using examiner-developed informal probes
- Hearing screening results reviewed from David Kim
- Oral mechanism examination
- Language sample collected during structured and unstructured play, analyzed with SALT conventions

TEST RESULTS

RECEPTIVE AND EXPRESSIVE LANGUAGE

| Measure | Domain | Raw Score | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Interaction-Attachment | 22 | — | — | 22 months |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Pragmatics | 18 | — | — | 19 months |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Gesture | 25 | — | — | 24 months |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Play | 20 | — | — | 21 months |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Language Comprehension | 16 | — | — | 17 months |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Language Expression | 11 | — | — | 14 months |
| Bayley-4 | Receptive Communication | 7 scaled | 70 | 2nd | 16 months |
| Bayley-4 | Expressive Communication | 5 scaled | 55 | <1st | 13 months |
| Bayley-4 | Cognitive | 9 scaled | 95 | 37th | 30 months |
| PPVT-5 (English) | Receptive Vocabulary | 12 | 78 | 7th | 20 months |

- On the Bayley-4, Mateo's Expressive Communication scaled score of 5 falls more than 2 standard deviations below the mean, within the range considered significantly delayed.
- His Receptive Communication scaled score of 7 falls approximately 1.5 standard deviations below the mean.
- Cognitive scores were within the average range, suggesting that nonverbal problem-solving and play skills are developing commensurate with age, in contrast to significantly depressed verbal scores.
- Informal Spanish vocabulary probes, administered by Jennifer Caldwell, identified approximately 15 consistent Spanish words and 4 consistent English words, for a combined expressive vocabulary of approximately 18 unique words (accounting for overlap).
- This combined vocabulary size is notably below expectations for a child at 2;6, regardless of bilingual status, and meets criteria for expressive language delay in both languages.

ARTICULATION AND PHONOLOGY

- On the GFTA-3 screening, Mateo's limited expressive vocabulary restricted the number of scoreable items; a standard score was not calculated due to insufficient verbal output, consistent with GFTA-3 administration guidelines.
- Available productions showed consistent patterns, including final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for "cat"), fronting of velars (e.g., "tat" for "cat"), and reduction of consonant clusters.
- In Spanish, informal probes elicited the target word "pelota", produced as "peota", and the target word "agua", produced as "awa", both consistent with developmentally typical simplifications but limited by overall low verbal output.
- Phonetic inventory across both languages was notably restricted, with primary reliance on the phonemes /m/, /p/, /b/, /a/, and /o/.
- No productions of /k/, /g/, /s/, or consonant clusters were observed in either language during this evaluation.
- Given the limited sample size, formal phonological process analysis was deferred pending vocabulary growth.

LANGUAGE SAMPLE ANALYSIS

- A 20-minute play-based language sample was collected across both home and clinic settings and coded using SALT conventions.
- Mateo produced 9 intelligible utterances during the sample, of which 7 were single words and 2 were two-word combinations ("más agua" and "no no").
- Mean length of utterance could not be reliably calculated given the small, restricted sample, consistent with significant expressive delay.
- Communicative functions observed included requesting (most frequent), protesting, and labeling; commenting and questioning were not observed.
- Code-switching within utterances was not observed; Mateo used Spanish words with family members and attempted English words inconsistently with Amanda Lopez and Emma at Durham Early Head Start.
- Utterances were coded with [EW] markers for word-final omissions and [EU] for unintelligible segments per standard SALT coding.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

- Results of this bilingual speech-language evaluation indicate a significant expressive language delay and a moderate receptive language delay across both Spanish and English, consistent with a diagnosis of Developmental Language Disorder.
- Mateo's delay is evident in both languages and cannot be attributed solely to typical bilingual acquisition patterns; combined vocabulary across languages remains well below age expectations.
- Cognitive and play skills are age-appropriate, supporting a primary speech-language diagnosis rather than a broader developmental concern at this time.
- Limited phonetic inventory and reliance on early-developing sounds in both languages suggest an associated speech sound delay, though formal articulation scoring was not possible due to restricted verbal output.
- Hearing has been appropriately screened and ruled out as a contributing factor.
- Mateo meets eligibility criteria for Early Intervention services under North Carolina's Infant-Toddler Program based on a 33% delay in the communication domain, as calculated from standardized assessment results above.
- Family engagement, home language support, and participation in community programs including Iglesia Bautista Monte Sion and Durham Early Head Start are notable strengths that will support intervention.

RECOMMENDATIONS

- Mateo is recommended for ongoing speech-language therapy services through the Early Intervention system, with a recommended frequency of two sessions per week, 30 minutes each, in a bilingual service delivery model.
- Treatment should address both Spanish and English expressive vocabulary growth, early phonological patterns, and functional communication strategies such as requesting and protesting using words rather than gestures alone.
- A total communication approach, including modeling of core vocabulary and incorporation of a few basic signs, is recommended to reduce frustration while verbal output develops.
- The family should continue to use Spanish as the primary home language; there is no evidence that bilingual exposure is contributing to Mateo's delay, and continued dual-language input is supported.
- Coordination with Amanda Lopez at Durham Early Head Start is recommended to ensure consistent communication strategies across home and classroom settings.
- Reassessment of articulation and phonology is recommended in approximately six months, once expressive vocabulary has increased sufficiently to allow formal scoring on the GFTA-3 or a parallel Spanish measure.
- Continued audiological monitoring is recommended given the speech-language delay, even though current screening results were normal.
- The family may benefit from continued participation in library-based bilingual literacy programs, such as the Spanish storytime at the Durham County Public Library South Branch, to support language-rich exposure outside of therapy.
- Referral to a bilingual parent coaching resource through Smart Start of Durham County is suggested to reinforce home-based language strategies.

SERVICE COORDINATION AND IFSP INFORMATION

- This report will be shared with the family's service coordinator, Gabriela Santos of ACSIF, to support development of the Individualized Family Service Plan.
- Proposed IFSP outcome 1: Mateo will use 25 new words across English and Spanish combined to request desired items and actions within 6 months.
- Proposed IFSP outcome 2: Mateo will combine two words to form simple phrases in his home language with 80% accuracy across three consecutive sessions within 9 months.
- The family's IFSP review meeting is scheduled for January 15, 2027 at 10:00 AM at the CDSA del Piamonte office.
- CDSA del Piamonte case records should be updated to reflect findings from this report, referencing case number CDSA-04471-PB.
- Questions regarding this report may be directed to Jennifer Caldwell at jcaldwell@carolinapedislp.com or by phone at (919) 555-0199.

This evaluation was conducted and this report prepared by Jennifer Caldwell, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist, Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC, on October 9, 2026.

Mom reports, in her own words (translated from Spanish by Teresa Gómez): "Él entiende todo, pero casi no habla. Dice 'mamá' y 'agua' pero nada más. Me preocupa que no hable con los otros niños en la guardería." ("He understands everything but barely talks. He says 'mama' and 'water' but nothing else. I worry he doesn't talk with the other kids at daycare.")

Grandmother adds, in English: "He points to what he wants. He gets frustrated and cries if we don't get it fast enough. At my house he does the same thing with Rocky's food bowl — points, grunts."

Family priorities per mom (unchanged from initial IFSP, reaffirmed today): 1) Mateo use words so family and daycare staff understand him; 2) Mateo play alongside cousin Diego Ramírez and other kids w/o tantrums; 3) family receive more home strategies in Spanish.

Daily routine per mom: wakes 6:30 AM, breakfast w/ sister Valentina de la Cruz before she leaves for school; Mateo attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center M–F 8:00 AM–4:30 PM; picked up by grandmother Rosa Méndez 3x/wk, by mom 2x/wk; dinner as family; bath; bed by 8:00 PM. Other agencies/providers involved: Wake County Smart Start provided home-visiting support January 2026–March 2026, case closed per mom request (scheduling conflict w/ work). Family also receiving WIC through Wake County Division of Social Services. Pediatrician Dr. Omar Hassan at WakeMed Cary Hospital pediatric clinic last seen September 2, 2026 for well-check; no new medical concerns per mom, referred back to ITP for speech follow-up. Birth history per mom: born 38 weeks gestation at WakeMed Cary Hospital, birth weight 6 lbs 11 oz, Apgar 8/9, no NICU stay.

Mom denies new feeding concerns. Reports Mateo eats table foods, occasional pocketing of bread noted but not consistent. No hearing concerns; newborn screen passed per mom report, audiology not yet repeated since initial IFSP — SC Brenda Walsh to follow up re: referral.

O:
Mateo alert, active, easily separated from mom to engage w/ clinician. Play skills: functional and symbolic play observed w/ farm set and shape sorter; engaged in reciprocal ball rolling 4/5 trials w/o cue. Joint attention: established and maintained w/ pointing + eye gaze to shared object 6/8 opportunities.

Communication sample (20 min, structured + unstructured play):
- Expressive: 3 consistent words noted ("mama," "agua," "más"); several vocal approximations not yet consistent. Produced "uh-oh" 2x spontaneously during block tower fall. Attempted "perro" (dog) when shown photo of Rocky, approximated as [pe], mod verbal cue given, improved to [peo] w/ mod cues.
- Gesture use: pointing, reaching, pulling adult by hand observed; no conventional gestures (waving, nodding) observed today despite elicitation attempts.
- Receptive: followed 1-step directions w/o gesture 4/6 trials ("give me the cup," "find the dog"); followed 2-step directions 0/3 w/o repetition.
- Oral mech: structure WNL; no overt feeding red flags observed during snack (crackers, applesauce). Mild drooling noted during focused play, intermittent.

Standardized measures administered this visit:
PLS-5 (Spanish/English bilingual administration, Preschool Language Scale–5):
- Auditory Comprehension: standard score 76, 5th percentile
- Expressive Communication: standard score 68, 2nd percentile
- Total Language Score: 70, 2nd percentile, age equivalent 15 months

MacArthur-Bates CDI (parent report, Spanish form, completed by mom w/ interpreter support): expressive vocabulary checklist 12 words reported across both languages combined.

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale informal observations consistent w/ above; attention, gesture, and play subdomains at/near age expectations; receptive and expressive language subdomains significantly below age expectations.

Classroom observation conducted October 1, 2026 at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, toddler room, teacher Ms. Katherine Lopez. Mateo observed during free play and snack w/ classmates Ethan Brooks and Sofia Castillo. Ms. Lopez reports Mateo "mostly plays alone or next to" peers, occasional parallel play w/ Sofia Castillo over shared toys; grabs items from Ethan Brooks w/o requesting, resulting in peer conflict 2–3x/day per teacher log. Ms. Lopez notes she has begun using visual choice boards per prior consult but inconsistently due to staff turnover. Referral documentation on file notes previous teacher Mr. Jordan Blake, who left Little Sprouts August 2026; Ms. Lopez took over room August 18, 2026.

A:
Mateo presents w/ significant expressive and receptive language delay relative to age, consistent w/ initial eligibility determination April 2026 under ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and DC:0-5 criteria reviewed at intake. Scores obtained today represent minimal change from initial IFSP evaluation 6 mo ago (PLS-5 Total Language Score 68 at intake vs 70 today) — progress noted but remains well below age expectations (<3rd percentile). Family's priority re: functional communication at home and daycare remains appropriate and unmet; continued ITP services and intensity warranted.

Bilingual presentation: language delay evident across both Spanish and English per combined CDI and direct assessment; not attributable to typical bilingual language acquisition pattern — true delay confirmed by convergent measures in both languages, consistent w/ ASHA bilingual assessment guidelines reviewed w/ family.

Social communication concerns (limited gesture repertoire, peer conflict at daycare, frustration-driven behavior) warrant continued collaboration w/ classroom staff and incorporation of PECS-style visual supports already partially introduced; family open to continued home coaching in Spanish, per mom's stated priority #3.

Risk factors: inconsistent audiology follow-up since birth screen; recommend SC Brenda Walsh confirm referral status w/ Dr. Omar Hassan's office prior to next review. Feeding: pocketing noted but insufficient for separate feeding eval referral at this time; monitor.

P:
IFSP outcomes reviewed and updated as follows:

Strategies: model + expand ("agua" → "más agua"); offer choices w/ 2 items + label; mom and grandmother Rosa Méndez coached today in self-talk/parallel talk technique in Spanish; written strategy sheet provided in Spanish via interpreter Teresa Gómez.

Outcome 2 (continued): Mateo will use a gesture or visual icon to request desired item in place of grabbing/crying, across home and daycare settings, 4/5 observed opportunities.

Outcome 3 (new, added per family priority #2): Mateo will engage in parallel or interactive play with a peer or cousin for 5 min w/o adult-mediated conflict, across 3 observed occasions.
Strategies: structured turn-taking games introduced during playdates w/ cousin Diego Ramírez; visual timer for turn-taking; coaching provided to mom and to Ms. Katherine Lopez re: redirecting grabbing behavior w/ classmates Ethan Brooks and Sofia Castillo.
