text:
CAROLINA BILINGUAL THERAPY PARTNERS, PLLC
SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Hernández Rodríguez (called "Teo" at home and at school)
Date of Birth: March 3, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 5;3
Record/Case ID: REC-55219
Medicaid ID: NC9284716B
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Guadalupe Rodríguez Pérez (mother); Jesús Hernández Morales, called "Chuy" by family (father)
Home Address: 2214 Willowbrook Lane, Greensboro, NC 27410
Home Phone: (336) 555-0148
Parent Email: lucia.rodriguez84@fastmail.com
Evaluation Date: el martes 4 de junio de 2026
Report Date: 06/09/2026
Referral Source: Dr. Angela Whitfield, pediatrician, Blue Ridge Women's Hospital Pediatric Clinic
Service Coordinator: Monica Tran, Piedmont Regional CDSA
Interpreter Present: Gabriela Soto, certified Spanish medical/educational interpreter
Evaluating Clinician: Patricia Noemí Delgado, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Spanish-English SLP Credential (NC), Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC

2. REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Whitfield following concerns raised by Lucía Rodríguez Pérez and classroom staff at Mariposa Azul Early Learning Village regarding limited intelligibility, reduced sentence length, and inconsistent response to directions in both English and Spanish. Chuy Hernández reported that strangers often cannot understand Teo's speech, while family members "fill in the gaps" based on context. The family requested the evaluation be conducted bilingually, with results interpreted for eligibility for Early Intervention services through Piedmont Regional CDSA and for an updated Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP).

3. BACKGROUND INFORMATION

3.1 Family Composition and Language History

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Pérez; his father, Jesús "Chuy" Hernández Morales; his older sister, Isabella Hernández Rodríguez, called "Lupita" (age 8;9); and his younger brother, José Hernández Rodríguez, called "Pepe" (age 2;1). The family resides in Greensboro, NC 27410, within Guilford County.

Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home. Lucía reported that approximately 80% of input to Teo is in Spanish, with the remainder in English, largely from Lupita, who attends Hamilton Elementary School and models English frequently at home. Chuy speaks primarily Spanish with occasional English phrases learned at work. The maternal grandmother, Rosa Pérez Núñez, lives nearby and provides childcare three days per week; she speaks only Spanish with Teo and his siblings.

Lucía reported that Teo's receptive and expressive language, in both languages, lags behind that of Lupita and most of his peers at Mariposa Azul Early Learning Village. She denied any period of true bilingual fluency followed by regression, and confirmed that Teo has been exposed to both languages since birth (simultaneous bilingual exposure).

3.2 Parent Occupations and Household Schedule

Lucía Rodríguez Pérez works at the Fresh Mart grocery store on Battleground Avenue, typically from 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.; la señora Rodríguez trabaja en la tienda Fresh Mart de lunes a viernes. Jesús Hernández Morales works at the Caldwell Valley Poultry Plant on the second shift; el señor Hernández trabaja en la planta avícola Caldwell Valley, de 3:00 p.m. a 11:00 p.m.

The paternal grandfather, Manuel Hernández Castillo, works at Green Valley Farms outside of Sedalia; don Manuel trabaja en la finca Green Valley durante la temporada de cosecha. The paternal uncle, Ramón Hernández Morales, works for Thompson Construction Company; el tío Ramón trabaja para la compañía de construcción Thompson y a veces recoge a los niños de la escuela. The maternal aunt, Carmen Rodríguez Pérez, works for Sparkle Clean Cleaning Service; la tía Carmen trabaja para el servicio de limpieza Sparkle Clean y ayuda con los niños los fines de semana.

Because of the parents' rotating and overlapping schedules, Teo spends considerable time with Rosa Pérez Núñez and, on weekends, with Carmen Rodríguez Pérez. The family reports strong extended-family support and frequent gatherings.

4. BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Blue Ridge Women's Hospital via scheduled cesarean section due to breech presentation. Birth weight was 6 lbs 4 oz. Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Lucía Rodríguez Pérez reported an otherwise unremarkable pregnancy, with routine prenatal care beginning on 9 de agosto de 2020.

Developmental milestones were reported as follows: sat independently at 7 months, walked independently at 14 months, and said his first words (in Spanish) around 16 months. Lucía noted that word combinations did not emerge until closer to 3;0, considerably later than observed in Isabella at a comparable age.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with 6 documented episodes between 12 months and 30 months of age. Teo underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on November 18, 2023, performed by Dr. Samuel Price, pediatric ENT. A follow-up audiological evaluation on 02/14/2024 documented normal hearing bilaterally following tube placement, with no further episodes of middle ear infection reported since that date. No history of seizures, significant head injury, or hospitalization aside from the ear tube procedure. Teo is not currently prescribed any medications. He is up to date on immunizations per Dr. Whitfield's records.

Family medical and developmental history is notable for a paternal cousin with a diagnosed speech sound disorder who received services through the local school system; no other family history of language, learning, or genetic disorders was reported.

5. EDUCATIONAL AND DAYCARE HISTORY

Teo has attended Mariposa Azul Early Learning Village since August 2022, currently in the Pre-K classroom under the supervision of lead teacher Ms. Jennifer Lopez and assistant teacher Ms. Dana Whitmore. Ms. Lopez reported that Teo is social and well-liked by peers, frequently seeking out classmates such as Juan "Juanito" Flores and Sofia Martinez for play, but that his attempts at verbal communication are "about half understandable" to classroom staff and largely unintelligible to peers outside his close friend group.

Ms. Lopez further reported that Teo follows one-step directions reliably but requires repetition or gestural cues for two-step directions, particularly in English. He has not exhibited significant behavioral concerns, though he becomes visibly frustrated when peers or staff cannot understand his requests, at times resorting to pointing or pulling an adult toward a desired item.

Isabella "Lupita" Hernández Rodríguez attends Hamilton Elementary School and has no history of speech-language services. José "Pepe" Hernández Rodríguez is not yet enrolled in any childcare program outside the home.

6. CLINICAL OBSERVATIONS

Teo presented on el martes 4 de junio de 2026 accompanied by his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Pérez, and interpreter Gabriela Soto. He separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the evaluator, Patricia Delgado, across both structured and play-based tasks. Eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during interactive play were age-appropriate. Teo demonstrated a positive affect throughout the session and required only occasional redirection to remain on task.

Oral-motor examination revealed symmetrical facial musculature, adequate labial and lingual range of motion, and no overt structural abnormalities. Diadochokinetic rate was mildly reduced for age but within functional limits for connected speech. No concerns regarding feeding or swallowing were reported or observed.

Hearing was screened informally through observation and parent report; given the history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement, a formal audiological re-screening is recommended as noted in Section 9.

7. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND RESULTS

The following standardized and informal measures were administered across two languages, with results interpreted in light of Teo's simultaneous bilingual language exposure. Spanish-language forms were administered by Patricia Delgado directly; English forms were administered with support from interpreter Gabriela Soto for parent-report components.

7.1 Standardized Test Results

Test and Subtest / Standard Score / Percentile / Age Equivalent / Confidence Interval

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English Form
  Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 76, 5th percentile, age equivalent 3;4, 95% CI (70-82)
  Expressive Communication: Standard Score 72, 3rd percentile, age equivalent 3;1, 95% CI (66-78)
  Total Language Score: 73, 4th percentile

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Preschool-3 Spanish (CELF-5 Spanish)
  Receptive Language Index: Standard Score 81, 10th percentile
  Expressive Language Index: Standard Score 79, 8th percentile

Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax Subtest
  Spanish: Scaled Score 7, within normal limits for bilingual exposure
  English: Scaled Score 5, below average

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
  Sounds-in-Words: Standard Score 70, 2nd percentile

7.2 Speech Sound Production

Spontaneous and imitated speech samples were collected in both Spanish and English. Teo substituted /k/ and /g/ with [t] and [d] respectively in word-initial position (e.g., "tat" for "cat," "dato" for "gato"), consistent with velar fronting. The Spanish tap /ɾ/ was produced inconsistently, often distorted or omitted in words such as "pero" and "para." Final consonant deletion was observed in 8/10 opportunities in connected speech (e.g., "ca" for "cat," "do" for "dog"). Cluster reduction was noted in 3 of 5 attempted consonant clusters.

Overall intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at 40% for unfamiliar listeners and 65% for familiar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

7.3 Language Sampling

A conversational language sample was collected and transcribed using SALT conventions. Mean length of utterance was 2.8 morphemes in Spanish and 2.3 morphemes in English, both below age expectations. Instances of code-mixing within utterances were marked with the code [EW] where an English word was embedded in an otherwise Spanish utterance (e.g., "quiero el [EW] truck"). This pattern is typical and expected in simultaneous bilingual development and was not interpreted as a language-specific deficit in isolation.

7.4 Diagnostic Coding

Based on today's findings, the following codes apply for billing and eligibility purposes: ICD-10 F80.1 (Expressive Language Disorder) and ICD-10 F80.0 (Phonological Disorder). Procedure code CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) was used for today's visit, with modifier -59 applied per agency billing guidance.

8. CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Results of today's bilingual evaluation indicate that Teo presents with a Speech Sound Disorder and a Language Disorder affecting both Spanish and English, with deficits present across both languages that cannot be attributed solely to typical second-language acquisition or reduced exposure. Scores on the PLS-5 and CELF-5 Spanish fall more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in both languages, and speech sound production deficits (velar fronting, final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, inconsistent tap production) are present across both Spanish and English phonological systems.

Teo's strong nonverbal communication, social engagement, and relatively intact receptive vocabulary are considered relative strengths. His frustration with communication breakdowns, while currently manageable, is a risk factor for future behavioral concerns if left unaddressed.

Given the combined pattern of findings, Teo meets criteria for Early Intervention services through Piedmont Regional CDSA under the category of Established Condition / Developmental Delay in Communication, and is recommended for an updated IFSP with speech-language goals as Outcome #2 and Outcome #3.

9. RECOMMENDATIONS

9.1 It is recommended that Teo receive individual bilingual speech-language therapy services two times weekly, 30 minutes per session, focusing on expressive language structure, speech sound production, and functional communication strategies in both Spanish and English.

9.2 A formal audiological re-screening is recommended given the history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement, to rule out any residual hearing loss contributing to current language and speech sound delays. This can be coordinated through Dr. Samuel Price's office or through Piedmont Regional CDSA.

9.3 Therapy should incorporate principles of PROMPT for motor-based speech sound intervention and the Cycles approach for phonological pattern remediation, with cueing hierarchies progressing from maximum cues to moderate cues (mod cues) to minimal cues as Teo demonstrates mastery at each level.

9.4 Given Teo's strong nonverbal communication and occasional frustration, introduction of a visual support system modeled on PECS principles is recommended as a bridge strategy during periods of reduced intelligibility, to be phased out as verbal intelligibility improves.

9.5 Caregiver coaching using Hanen-based strategies ("OWL": Observe, Wait, Listen) is recommended for Lucía Rodríguez Pérez, Jesús Hernández Morales, and Rosa Pérez Núñez, given their central roles in Teo's daily language environment. Materials will be provided in Spanish.

9.6 It is recommended that Teo continue bilingual exposure at home and at Mariposa Azul Early Learning Village; no reduction of either language is indicated, as continued dual-language exposure supports, rather than impedes, his overall communication development.

9.7 Coordination between Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC, Mariposa Azul Early Learning Village, and Piedmont Regional CDSA is recommended to ensure consistency of strategies across settings. A classroom consultation with Ms. Lopez is recommended within the next 30 days.

9.8 Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately 6 months, or sooner if significant changes in communication skills are observed, with the next IFSP review currently scheduled for 15 de enero de 2027 (numerically, 01/15/2027).

10. SUMMARY

Mateo "Teo" Alejandro Hernández Rodríguez, age 5;3, presents with a bilingual Speech Sound Disorder and Language Disorder affecting both Spanish and English, in the context of a supportive, Spanish-dominant home environment with extensive extended-family involvement. He demonstrates relative strengths in social engagement and nonverbal communication alongside significant deficits in expressive and receptive language and speech sound production across both languages. He meets eligibility criteria for continued Early Intervention services through Piedmont Regional CDSA, and individualized bilingual speech-language therapy, caregiver coaching, and interdisciplinary coordination are recommended as outlined above.

Expressive Language	PLS-5 Expressive Communication	71	3rd percentile	13 months

The PLS-5 Expressive Communication score of 71 falls within a 95% confidence interval of 65–77, confirming a significant delay. Teo used a 12-word expressive vocabulary at the time of testing and combined two words inconsistently, producing "más agua" and "no quiero." His phonetic inventory is limited to /m/, /p/, /n/, /b/, and /a/; he produced [ba] for "ball" and [ti] for "teta" (bottle). He required moderate cues to imitate single words and maximal cues for two-word combinations. Language sample analysis (SALT code [EW] marked for word-final omissions) showed 4 of 10 utterances were intelligible to an unfamiliar listener.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

Maria Elena Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP conducted this portion of the visit directly in Spanish; no outside interpreter was required for the speech discussion, though Jennifer Boyd supported the overall meeting in English for Héctor's workplace documents.

Lucía said, "Quiero que Teo pueda decirme lo que necesita sin llorar tanto. A veces grita y yo no sé qué quiere" ("I want Teo to tell me what he needs without crying so much. Sometimes he screams and I don't know what he wants").

Héctor added that he wants Teo ready for preschool "para que no se quede atrás como su prima" (so he isn't behind like his cousin). He works in estimating for Palmetto Construction Group and asked that sessions be scheduled before 4:00 p.m. so he can attend after his shift ends.

The family is also concerned about Teo's transition into Tadpole Trail Children's Center, where he attends the toddler room two mornings a week. His lead teacher there, Ms. Danielle Ferris, and assistant teacher M.P., report that Teo often pulls his friend Sofia Whitaker's hair when he wants a toy instead of asking. Lucía worries this will affect his place in the room when the center's fall waitlist opens.

Priorities, in the family's words:
1. "That he can tell us what he wants with words, not screaming."
2. "That he can go to school with his sister someday without extra help."
3. "That the people at Tadpole Trail understand him and don't think he's behind in everything."

DAILY ROUTINES

Mornings: Teo wakes around 7:00 a.m., eats breakfast with Valentina before she leaves for kindergarten, and is dropped at Tadpole Trail Children's Center by Héctor on Tuesdays and Thursdays before he drives to Garner for work.

Afternoons: Rosa Ibarra Ramos picks Teo up and supervises outdoor play at a neighborhood park, where he plays near Sofia Whitaker and another child, Diego Martínez, though he mostly plays alone with trucks rather than interacting.

Mealtimes: Teo eats independently with a spoon but refuses most vegetables; mealtime requests are almost entirely gestural (reaching, pulling the caregiver's hand).

Bath and bedtime: Bath is around 7:30 p.m., followed by two books read in Spanish by Lucía; Teo points to pictures but rarely labels them. Bedtime is consistently 8:15 p.m..

Sibling routine: Valentina Flores Ibarra attends kindergarten in the Wake County Public School System at Pine Hollow Elementary School, in the classroom of Ms. Carmen Delgado. Lucía reports that Valentina often "translates" for Teo at home, which the team flagged as a pattern to monitor so Teo is not relying on his sister instead of using his own words.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

- Wake County DSS: the family receives food and housing support; caseworker R. Alvarez coordinates eligibility renewals.
- WIC: Lucía attends monthly nutrition appointments at the Garner office.
- Smart Start of Wake County: provided the family's initial referral to Tadpole Trail Children's Center and funds a partial subsidy.
- Early Head Start: the family is on the waitlist; Jennifer Boyd will follow up before the next review.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Teo will use 2-word combinations to request and comment across home and daycare settings.
Strategy: Caregivers will use a "say it, sign it" model during routines; the SLP will use milieu teaching and Hanen-based strategies (It Takes Two to Talk) during biweekly sessions. Target cueing level: minimal cues by the next review.

Outcome 2: Teo will reduce physical grabbing/hitting at Tadpole Trail Children's Center by using a picture or gesture to request a turn in 8 of 10 observed opportunities.
Strategy: Introduce a simplified PECS exchange system with Ms. Danielle Ferris and M.P.; coach caregivers on "wait and signal" during home play. Sarah Whitfield, OTR/L will co-treat monthly to address grasp and pointing precision needed for the exchange.

Outcome 3: Teo will produce initial consonants /m/, /b/, and /p/ in single words with no more than moderate cues in 3 of 5 trials.
Strategy: Direct articulation drill using a Cycles approach, targeting early-developing sounds in both English and Spanish lexicons; home practice list sent in Spanish.

Outcome 4: The family will have a shared routine for bedtime reading that increases Teo's labeling of familiar pictures from current baseline (near 0%) to 50% of prompted opportunities.
Strategy: Coaching session embedded in a home visit; Maria Elena Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP will model PROMPT-informed cueing for jaw and lip shaping during book-sharing, in Spanish.

SERVICE DELIVERY SCHEDULE

Session fee is billed under CPT 92507 for individual treatment and CPT 92523 for re-evaluation, both with modifier GN for speech-language pathology services.

CONSENT AND TRANSITION PLANNING

Both parents consented to continued services and to the transition planning discussion for Teo's third birthday on March 3, 2027. The team discussed referral to the Wake County Public School System Preschool Exceptional Children's Program as a possible next step, pending further evaluation closer to that date. Héctor specifically asked whether Valentina's school, Pine Hollow Elementary School, has a preschool program; Jennifer Boyd will research this and report back by November 15, 2026.

The family also asked that all written materials continue to be provided in Spanish and that Maria Elena Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP remain the primary therapist given the rapport she has built, noting in the visit that "ella es la única que Teo deja que le toque la boca" (she is the only one he lets touch his mouth).

- "Queremos que hable los dos idiomas, español en casa e inglés en la escuela, para que no se confunda." ("We want her to speak both languages, Spanish at home and English at school, so she doesn't get confused.")
- Marcos Hernández Ortiz added that he wants Majo to be able to tell him what hurts or what she needs before she starts preschool.
- Lucía Castillo Reyes shared that because she works nights at Cardinal Glass Industries, most of the daytime caregiving and therapy carryover falls to Rosa Castillo and to Marcos Hernández Ortiz, and the family wants strategies that both caregivers can use consistently.

DAILY ROUTINES
- 6:30 a.m.: Majo wakes and has breakfast with Rosa Castillo or Marcos Hernández Ortiz, depending on who is home.

- 4:00 p.m.: pickup, usually by Rosa Castillo or Marcos Hernández Ortiz.
- Afternoons: free play at home with Sol, who likes to "teach" Majo words from her own homework; family reports this is a favorite routine.
- 6:00 p.m.: family dinner together when both parents are home; Spanish is the primary language used at the table.
- Bath and bedtime routine around 7:30 p.m., led by whichever parent is not working that night; includes a consistent song and two books read in Spanish.
- On nights Lucía Castillo Reyes works at Cardinal Glass Industries, Marcos Hernández Ortiz handles the bedtime routine alone.
- Saturday mornings: family attends a toddler playgroup hosted by Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza, where Majo interacts with other bilingual toddlers and the group leader, Mirna Osorio.
- Sunday afternoons: extended family gathering at Rosa Castillo's house, including cousins; family notes Majo is more vocal in this familiar setting.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED
- WIC — Wake County Human Services: family receives nutrition support; most recent recertification March 3, 2026.
- Smart Start of Wake County: provided a childcare subsidy that helps cover Majo's tuition at Honeybee Hollow Early Learning.
- Wake County Department of Social Services: no open case; family was referred for food assistance screening in January 2026 and determined ineligible at that time.
- Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza: weekly bilingual playgroup, described above, also provides occasional transportation assistance for therapy appointments.
- Southeast Regional Library: family attends the Saturday "Cuentos y Cantos" bilingual storytime when schedules allow, led by librarian Teresa Whitfield.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT — COMMUNICATION
- Most recent standardized assessment: Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish, administered April 6, 2026 by Alicia Meadows.
- Auditory Comprehension: standard score 76, 5th percentile, age equivalent 18 months.
- Expressive Communication: standard score 71, 3rd percentile, age equivalent 16 months.
- Total Language Score: 73, 95% confidence interval 68-78.
- Majo produces an estimated 30 single words across both languages, primarily nouns (agua, more, mamá, perro) and no two-word combinations observed during testing.
- During play-based sampling, Majo produced "aba" for agua and " te" for leche, with final consonant deletion noted on words ending in /s/ and /n/.
- Oral mechanism exam within normal limits; no concerns for feeding or swallowing.
- Receptively, Majo followed 8 of 10 one-step directions in Spanish and 6 of 10 in English during structured sampling.
- Joint attention and gesture use are relative strengths; Majo points, waves, and brings objects to adults to show them, consistent with typical 18-24 month milestones rather than her chronological age of 2;6.
- Daycare report from Ms. Patrice Albright echoes the pattern: Majo uses gestures and a few English words ("more," "up," "done") but does not combine words or use short phrases like her classroom peers.

OUTCOMES WITH STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Majo will use two-word combinations (e.g., "más agua," "mommy up") in Spanish and English across home, Honeybee Hollow Early Learning, and community settings, increasing from a baseline of 0 spontaneous two-word combinations to 10 different combinations observed across three consecutive sessions.
- Strategy: use expansion and modeling in both languages; caregivers repeat Majo's single-word utterance and add one word ("agua" becomes "más agua").
- Strategy: Alicia Meadows will coach Lucía Castillo Reyes, Marcos Hernández Ortiz, and Rosa Castillo on a home program using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, specifically following Majo's lead and commenting rather than questioning.
- Strategy: Ms. Patrice Albright and Yolanda Benítez will model two-word phrases during snack and play at Honeybee Hollow Early Learning and log attempts weekly.
- Strategy: during Saturday playgroup at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza, Mirna Osorio will prompt peer-directed requests ("quiero pelota") during group games.

Outcome 2: Majo will request desired items and actions using a word or approximation instead of only pointing or pulling, in at least 8 of 10 opportunities across three consecutive home and daycare observations.
- Baseline: Majo currently requests verbally in approximately 2 of 10 opportunities, relying on gesture the remainder of the time.
- Strategy: caregivers will use a brief communication temptation routine, withholding a preferred item briefly and modeling the target word with minimal cues before providing it.
- Strategy: Rosa Castillo, who provides most daytime care, will be given a simple picture list of five target words/approximations to model consistently, informed by principles from PECS without requiring a full exchange protocol.
- Strategy: Hannah Okafor, the developmental therapist, will co-treat with Alicia Meadows monthly to embed requesting opportunities into motor and play-based activities.

Outcome 3: Majo will imitate and spontaneously produce early consonant sounds /m/, /p/, /b/, and /t/ in word-initial position, increasing intelligibility of attempted words from an estimated 40% to 70% as rated by familiar and unfamiliar listeners.
- Baseline production sample: Majo produced "mamá" clearly, "apa" for "papá" (initial consonant deletion), and "o" for "no."
- Strategy: use PROMPT-informed tactile-kinesthetic cueing for bilabial sounds during snack time, when Majo is motivated by real food items.
- Strategy: target words selected jointly with the family to be meaningful in both Spanish and English (mamá, papá, más, pan, bebé).
- Strategy: Alicia Meadows will model with moderate cues fading to minimal cues across sessions and track progress using session data sheets shared with the family through Wake County CDSA's family portal.

Outcome 4: The family will feel confident supporting Majo's bilingual language development at home, as measured by a family-report rating of at least 4 out of 5 on a confidence survey administered at the next review.
- Current baseline rating: 2 out of 5, per Lucía Castillo Reyes and Marcos Hernández Ortiz.
- Strategy: provide the family with bilingual handouts in Spanish summarizing each outcome's strategies.
- Strategy: schedule at least one session every six weeks with Rosa Castillo present, since she provides the majority of daytime care and transportation.
- Strategy: connect the family with the bilingual toddler storytime at Southeast Regional Library as a low-cost, community-based language opportunity.
- Strategy: service coordinator Denise Falwell will check in monthly by phone to troubleshoot scheduling around Lucía Castillo Reyes's night shifts at Cardinal Glass Industries.

SERVICE DELIVERY AND DATES

  - Location: primarily the home at 118 Willow Creek Lane; one session per month at Honeybee Hollow Early Learning for consultation with Ms. Patrice Albright.

text:
Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro Flores Ramírez  Apodo: Teo  Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de marzo de 2022  Edad cronológica: 4;7
Número de expediente: MRN-0042187  Número de Medicaid: 987654321A  Número de autorización: AUTH-55218
Fecha de evaluación: 2 de octubre de 2026  Fecha del informe: 9 de octubre de 2026
Evaluadora: Diana Castillo Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP  Empresa: Terapias Integrales Carolina del Este, PLLC
Pediatra remitente: Dr. Samuel Ibáñez  Coordinadora de servicios (CDSA): Andrea Pérez
Agencia CDSA: Agencia de Desarrollo Infantil del Este, oficina de Goldsboro  Condado: Wayne
Dirección del hogar: 215 Cherry Street, Mount Olive, NC 28365  Teléfono: (919) 555-0148
Correo electrónico de la madre: lucia.rodriguezf@gmail.com

MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA

Mateo, conocido en casa como Teo, es un niño de 4;7 años referido por Dr. Samuel Ibáñez para una evaluación completa de habla y lenguaje debido a preocupaciones persistentes de su madre, Lucía Rodríguez Flores, y su coordinadora de servicios del CDSA, Andrea Pérez, sobre su inteligibilidad del habla y su desarrollo de lenguaje expresivo en español y en inglés. Mateo fue referido inicialmente a los Servicios de Intervención Temprana del Condado de Wayne a los 26 meses de edad después de que su niñera, Rosa Elena Martínez, notara que el niño producía muy pocas palabras inteligibles en comparación con su hermana mayor, Camila Flores Rodríguez. La familia fue conectada con el CDSA de Goldsboro a través de una referencia hecha por el Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Wayne durante una visita de recertificación de beneficios.

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO MÉDICO

Según el reporte de Lucía Rodríguez Flores, el embarazo de Mateo fue de alto riesgo por preeclampsia materna, y el parto ocurrió por cesárea de emergencia en el WakeMed, campus Raleigh a las 34 semanas de gestación. Mateo nació con un peso de 2,150 gramos y un puntaje de Apgar de 6 al minuto y 8 a los cinco minutos. Permaneció en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos Neonatales del WakeMed, campus Raleigh durante 19 días por dificultad respiratoria e ictericia. Durante su estancia, fue evaluado por el equipo de terapia de alimentación del hospital debido a succión débil y coordinación inmadura de succión-deglución-respiración. Fue dado de alta con seguimiento ambulatorio en la clínica pediátrica de seguimiento de alto riesgo de WakeMed.

A los 8 meses de edad, Mateo presentó varios episodios de otitis media aguda y fue remitido a la práctica de Otorrinolaringología y Audiología Pediátrica de Duke Health, campus Durham, donde el Dr. Marcus Whitfield colocó tubos de ventilación bilaterales (CPT 69436) a los 14 meses de edad. Las evaluaciones audiológicas posteriores en esa misma clínica mostraron audición dentro de límites normales bilateralmente, documentadas mediante timpanometría y audiometría conductual. La madre reporta que, desde la colocación de los tubos, las infecciones de oído han disminuido notablemente, aunque Mateo continúa con seguimiento anual con audiología en Duke Health, campus Durham.

El historial médico adicional incluye un diagnóstico de reflujo gastroesofágico (ICD-10 K21.9) tratado con omeprazol durante el primer año de vida, y un diagnóstico reciente de trastorno fonológico (ICD-10 F80.0) y trastorno del lenguaje expresivo (ICD-10 F80.1) documentados por el Dr. Samuel Ibáñez en la visita de los 4 años. Mateo no tiene antecedentes de convulsiones, pérdida auditiva permanente, ni diagnóstico de trastorno del espectro autista, aunque la familia reporta que un primo paterno, Joel Castillo Nuñez, recibe servicios de intervención por retraso en el desarrollo.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo vive con su madre, Lucía Rodríguez Flores; su padre, Henry Flores Castillo; su hermana mayor, Camila Flores Rodríguez, de 6 años; y su abuela materna, Rosa Elena Martínez, quien cuida a los niños durante el día. La familia reside en una casa alquilada en 215 Cherry Street, Mount Olive, a unos quince minutos de la oficina del CDSA de Goldsboro. Lucía Rodríguez Flores trabaja de noche en la línea de empaque de Mount Olive Pickle Company, y Henry Flores Castillo trabaja en el turno diurno en la planta de procesamiento de Butterball, planta de Mount Olive. Debido a estos horarios, Rosa Elena Martínez es la cuidadora principal de Mateo durante la mayor parte del día.

La familia emigró de la aldea de Las Flores, en el departamento de Yoro, hace aproximadamente seis años, antes del nacimiento de Mateo. En casa se habla principalmente español; Lucía Rodríguez Flores reporta que ella y Henry Flores Castillo hablan español entre ellos y con los niños, mientras que Camila Flores Rodríguez mezcla español e inglés desde que comenzó el kínder en la Escuela Primaria Carver Heights. Mateo asiste de forma parcial al programa Early Head Start del Condado de Wayne, en el centro ubicado cerca de Mount Olive, donde su maestra, Marisol Jiménez, reporta que Mateo se comunica principalmente con gestos y palabras sueltas, y que sus compañeros, incluyendo a Ángel y Destiny, a menudo hablan por él cuando no es comprendido.

La familia también ha recibido apoyo del Programa WIC del Condado de Wayne desde el nacimiento de Mateo, y participó en un programa de alfabetización familiar ofrecido por Smart Start del Condado de Wayne el año pasado. Lucía Rodríguez Flores expresa que está muy motivada para ayudar a Mateo en casa, pero que su horario nocturno limita el tiempo que puede dedicarle directamente, por lo que gran parte de la estimulación diaria recae en Rosa Elena Martínez, quien habla únicamente español.

La mascota de la familia es un perro llamado Rocky, al que Mateo llama frecuentemente con una aproximación de la palabra, lo cual la madre considera uno de los pocos intentos verbales espontáneos y consistentes del niño.

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES

Durante la sesión de evaluación, realizada en la oficina satélite del CDSA de Goldsboro, Mateo se mostró inicialmente tímido pero se adaptó rápidamente al entorno con el apoyo de su madre. Mantuvo contacto visual apropiado, respondió a su nombre de manera consistente, y demostró juego simbólico apropiado para su edad con figuras de animales. Su atención a las tareas estructuradas fue variable, requiriendo redirección frecuente y refuerzo con pegatinas. Mateo utilizó principalmente gestos, señalización y aproximaciones vocálicas para comunicarse, con producción verbal espontánea limitada a aproximadamente 15 a 20 palabras reconocibles, la mayoría en español.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Se administraron los siguientes instrumentos estandarizados, complementados con observación clínica, muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, y entrevista a los padres:

Instrumento: Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), versión en español  Puntaje estándar Comunicación Auditiva: 76  Percentil: 5
Puntaje estándar Comunicación Expresiva: 71  Percentil: 3  Puntaje Total de Lenguaje: 72  Intervalo de confianza 95%: 65-79

Instrumento: Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)  Puntaje estándar: 68  Percentil: 2  Edad equivalente: 2;4

Instrumento: Evaluación de inteligibilidad en contexto conectado  Inteligibilidad para oyentes familiares: 60%  Inteligibilidad para oyentes no familiares: 30%

Instrumento: Muestra de habla espontánea, 50 enunciados  Procesos fonológicos observados: reducción de grupos consonánticos, frontalización velar, omisión de consonante final

RESULTADOS: HABLA

El análisis fonológico reveló patrones consistentes de simplificación del habla. Mateo produjo "tetota" para "pelota", omitiendo el fonema /p/ inicial y sustituyendo /l/ por /t/. También produjo "dao" para "gato", con frontalización del sonido velar /g/ y omisión de la consonante final /t/. En inglés, produjo "[EW] tat" para "cat", reflejando patrones similares de frontalización. Los grupos consonánticos como /tr/ y /bl/ fueron consistentemente reducidos a un solo elemento, por ejemplo "toque" para "tren" y "azul" producido como "azú". Con claves de articulación de nivel moderado (mod cues), Mateo logró producir correctamente el sonido /k/ en posición inicial en 6 de 10 intentos, sugiriendo capacidad de estimulación. Sin claves, su precisión consonántica global se estimó en 45%, marcadamente por debajo de lo esperado para su edad.

RESULTADOS: LENGUAJE RECEPTIVO Y EXPRESIVO

En el PLS-5, el desempeño de Mateo en comunicación auditiva reflejó dificultades para seguir instrucciones de dos pasos no relacionados y para identificar conceptos cuantitativos básicos como "más" y "menos". En comunicación expresiva, su vocabulario funcional fue limitado principalmente a sustantivos de alta frecuencia, con uso mínimo de verbos conjugados, pronombres, y estructuras de dos a tres palabras. La longitud media de enunciado en la muestra espontánea fue de 1.8 morfemas, consistente con un nivel de desarrollo lingüístico de aproximadamente 18 a 24 meses. Mateo mostró habilidades pragmáticas relativamente fuertes, incluyendo toma de turnos, uso de gestos comunicativos intencionales, y protodeclarativas consistentes, lo cual es un factor positivo pronóstico.

RESULTADOS: VOZ Y FLUIDEZ

No se observaron características de disfluencia atípica durante la muestra de habla espontánea. La calidad vocal fue dentro de límites normales, sin evidencia de ronquera, tensión, o resonancia anormal.

IMPRESIONES DIAGNÓSTICAS

Con base en los hallazgos de esta evaluación, Mateo presenta un trastorno fonológico de severidad moderada a severa (ICD-10 F80.0), caracterizado por procesos de simplificación inconsistentes con su edad cronológica, e inteligibilidad reducida tanto en español como en inglés. Adicionalmente, Mateo cumple criterios para un trastorno del lenguaje expresivo (ICD-10 F80.1), con relativa preservación de habilidades pragmáticas y de comunicación social. Dada la exposición bilingüe consistente del niño desde el nacimiento, y el desempeño reducido en ambos idiomas, se descarta que las dificultades observadas se deban únicamente a adquisición típica de un segundo idioma; más bien, los patrones son consistentes con un trastorno primario del lenguaje que afecta ambos sistemas lingüísticos.

Mateo continúa siendo elegible para servicios de intervención temprana coordinados por el CDSA de Goldsboro, y su coordinadora de servicios, Andrea Pérez, deberá actualizar el Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) para incluir los nuevos resultados de esta evaluación, bajo el Resultado IFSP #3 relacionado con comunicación funcional.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda terapia de habla y lenguaje bilingüe (español-inglés) individual, dos veces por semana, con sesiones de 30 minutos, utilizando un enfoque combinado de terapia fonológica basada en procesos (Enfoque de Ciclos) y estrategias de estimulación de lenguaje basadas en el modelo Hanen.

2. Continuar seguimiento audiológico anual en Duke Health, campus Durham para monitorear cualquier recurrencia de otitis media y su posible impacto en el desarrollo del habla.

3. Coordinar con la maestra del programa Early Head Start del Condado de Wayne, Marisol Jiménez, para implementar estrategias de lenguaje en el aula, incluyendo expansión de enunciados y modelado en ambos idiomas.

4. Proveer a la familia, incluyendo a Lucía Rodríguez Flores, Henry Flores Castillo, y Rosa Elena Martínez, materiales de estimulación de lenguaje en español para uso en el hogar, dado que Rosa Elena Martínez es la cuidadora principal durante el día.

5. Reevaluar en 6 meses para medir progreso en inteligibilidad y longitud media de enunciado, y determinar necesidad de ajuste en la frecuencia de servicios.

6. Notificar a la coordinadora de servicios, Andrea Pérez, y al CDSA de Goldsboro, para actualizar el IFSP con los resultados de esta evaluación antes de la próxima reunión de revisión programada para el 15 de enero de 2027.

7. Mantener comunicación con el pediatra, Dr. Samuel Ibáñez, sobre el progreso del niño y cualquier cambio en su historial médico relevante para el tratamiento del habla y lenguaje.

Esta evaluación fue realizada y este informe fue redactado por Diana Castillo Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe certificada, en nombre de Terapias Integrales Carolina del Este, PLLC. Para preguntas sobre este informe, favor comunicarse al (919) 555-0148 o al correo dcastillo@terapiascarolinaeste.com.

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Robert Kim at Mateo's 4-year well-child visit on September 11, 2026, due to parental and teacher concerns about limited intelligibility and short sentence length in both Spanish and English. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez Hernández, reported, "No le entendemos a veces ni nosotros, y eso me preocupa mucho" ("Sometimes even we don't understand him, and that worries me a lot"). Lucía Rodríguez Hernández further stated that Mateo "se frustra y empieza a llorar cuando no lo entendemos" (becomes frustrated and cries when he is not understood). His father, Javier Hernández Cruz, added that Mateo's older sister, Sol, frequently "translates" for Mateo at home and at family gatherings, which the family worries may be masking the extent of his difficulties.

Mateo currently attends Little Learners Bilingual Academy four days per week, where his lead teacher, Maestra Ana Flores, also expressed concern, noting that Mateo is "much quieter than his classmates" and often points or gestures rather than using words during circle time. Maestra Ana Flores reported that classmates Liam and Emma sometimes speak for Mateo when he is not understood, and that Mateo has started to withdraw from group activities. The family was also referred for an initial eligibility evaluation through Guilford County CDSA given concerns raised at a routine developmental screening administered through Smart Start of Guilford County.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestational age at Triad Regional Health – University Campus on August 9, 2022, following a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia. Birth weight was 4 lbs 11 oz (2,126 grams). Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. Mateo was admitted to the Triad Regional Health NICU for 19 days for respiratory support and feeding difficulties, including documented poor coordination of suck-swallow-breathe noted by the NICU speech-language pathologist, Hannah Weiss. He was discharged home on August 28, 2022 without supplemental oxygen.

Mother reports an unremarkable toddler medical history aside from recurrent otitis media. Mateo had six documented episodes of acute otitis media between 8 months and 24 months of age, treated with antibiotics, with persistent middle ear effusion noted on exam at 22 months. He underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement (CPT 69436) on June 14, 2024 at Carolina Hearing & Balance Associates at Triad Regional Health – University Campus, performed by Dr. Patricia Owens, otolaryngologist. Tubes extruded spontaneously by February 2025 without recurrence of effusion. His most recent audiological evaluation, completed March 18, 2026 by audiologist Dr. Samantha Lee at the same campus, documented bilateral hearing within normal limits via visual reinforcement audiometry, with normal tympanograms bilaterally.

Mateo has no history of seizure, head injury, or hospitalization beyond the NICU stay and tube placement. He is not currently on any medications. Vision was last screened at within normal limits at his 4-year well-child visit. Diagnosis under consideration for this evaluation includes expressive language disorder (ICD-10 F80.1) and possible speech sound disorder (ICD-10 F80.0); evaluation billed under CPT 92523.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo lives at home with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Hernández; his father, Javier Hernández Cruz; and his older sister, Sol, age 7. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández was born in Guanajuato, Mexico, and moved to the United States at age 19. Javier Hernández Cruz was born in Greensboro to parents who emigrated from Jalisco. Both parents report that Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home, estimating approximately 80% Spanish and 20% English input, with English increasing since Mateo began attending Little Learners Bilingual Academy.

Lucía Rodríguez Hernández reported, "En casa hablamos español casi todo el tiempo, pero su papá a veces le habla en inglés cuando mira dibujos animados" ("At home we speak Spanish almost all the time, but his dad sometimes speaks English with him when he watches cartoons"). Javier Hernández Cruz works at Carolina Fresh Foods Distribution Center on second shift, which the family noted affects how much time he has to engage in extended play and language routines with Mateo during the week.

Sol is described by both parents as verbally advanced for her age and bilingual with strong skills in both languages. The family reports that Sol often "speaks for" Mateo when he struggles to be understood, both at home and during visits with extended family, including his cousins Diego and Valentina, the children of Javier Hernández Cruz's sister. Family gatherings occur frequently at the home of paternal grandparents and at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, where the family attends services weekly and where Mateo participates in a toddler Sunday school class alongside several cousins and family friends.

Mateo's regular caregiver on weekday evenings when both parents work late is a family friend, Marisela Pérez, who speaks primarily Spanish with Mateo and reports similar concerns about his intelligibility, noting that she sometimes has to ask him to repeat himself "cuatro o cinco veces" (four or five times) before understanding him. The family's dog, Max, is frequently mentioned by Mateo in play narratives and was present during the home observation portion of this evaluation.

Developmental milestones in other domains were reported as within normal limits: Mateo walked independently at 14 months and is fully toilet trained. Mother denies concerns regarding fine or gross motor skills, feeding, or social-emotional development aside from frustration related to communication breakdowns.

EDUCATIONAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY

Mateo has attended Little Learners Bilingual Academy since January 2024, currently in the Pre-K 3 classroom under lead teacher Maestra Ana Flores and assistant teacher Ms. Johnson. Classroom instruction is delivered bilingually, with approximately equal time in Spanish and English. Maestra Ana Flores completed a classroom observation form prior to this evaluation, noting that Mateo "entiende todo pero habla muy poco" (understands everything but speaks very little) and tends to play alongside rather than with peers such as Liam, Emma, and Camila during free play.

The family also participates in a bilingual storytime program, "Cuentos y Canciones," held weekly at the Greensboro Public Library – Glenwood Branch, which Lucía Rodríguez Hernández reports Mateo enjoys but in which he rarely participates verbally compared to other children his age. The family additionally receives nutrition support through WIC and was connected to Guilford County CDSA for developmental services following a screening referral from Smart Start of Guilford County completed at a community health fair on July 19, 2026.

An Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) review is scheduled for November 5, 2026, at which this evaluation's findings will be presented to the team, including service coordinator Brenda Walsh.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted bilingually in both English and Spanish by Katherine Diaz, M.S., CCC-SLP, over two sessions on October 2, 2026 and October 6, 2026, at the Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates clinic. Procedures included formal standardized testing, parent interview, language sample analysis, and a brief home-based play observation attended by Lucía Rodríguez Hernández and Sol.

Standardized measures administered included the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), administered in both English and Spanish forms; the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3); and the Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Semantics subtests. Nonstandardized procedures included a 50-utterance spontaneous language sample collected in Spanish during play with toy animals and a separate 30-utterance sample in English during a picture-book task, both coded using SALT conventions including codes such as [EW] for word-final errors and [FP] for filled pauses.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and testing materials across both sessions. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks but required frequent redirection during less structured play, particularly when frustrated by word-finding or articulation breakdowns. When unable to produce a target word, Mateo frequently resorted to gesture, pointing, or looked to his mother or sister for support, consistent with reports from home and Little Learners Bilingual Academy.

Rapport was easily established, aided by the evaluator's use of both English and Spanish throughout testing. Mateo appeared more spontaneous and verbal during the Spanish-language portions of testing, consistent with the home language environment, though errors in intelligibility were noted in both languages.

TEST RESULTS

Standardized Test Scores

Test	Language	Standard Score	Percentile Rank	Age Equivalent
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension	Spanish	82	12th percentile	3;1
PLS-5 Expressive Communication	Spanish	74	4th percentile	2;7
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension	English	85	16th percentile	3;3
PLS-5 Expressive Communication	English	71	3rd percentile	2;5
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words	English	78	7th percentile	3;4
BESA Morphosyntax	Bilingual composite	70	2nd percentile	n/a
BESA Semantics	Bilingual composite	81	10th percentile	n/a

On the PLS-5, administered in both languages with best-performance scoring reflecting Mateo's stronger responses across languages, composite Auditory Comprehension fell within the below average range and Expressive Communication fell within the significantly below average range relative to monolingual norms, with bilingual norm-referenced interpretation considered given BESA results.

Articulation and Phonology

On the GFTA-3, Mateo produced 18 sound errors across 53 test items, including consistent substitution of [t] for /k/ and [d] for /g/ in word-initial position, consistent with a phonological process of fronting. He also demonstrated gliding of liquids, producing [w] for /l/ and /ɾ/ in both English and Spanish contexts, notably in his production of the target word "carro" as "kawo" and "ball" as "baw". Final consonant deletion was observed in approximately 30% of eligible words, for example "pan" produced as "pa" and "cat" produced as "ca".

Stimulability testing indicated that Mateo could produce /k/ correctly in isolation with moderate (mod) cueing and tactile support, and could approximate /ɾ/ in Spanish with maximum (max) cues, suggesting motor planning difficulty rather than a fixed phonological pattern alone. Overall speech intelligibility was estimated at 40% in context for unfamiliar listeners and 65% in context for familiar listeners across both languages.

Language Sample Analysis

In the Spanish language sample, Mateo's mean length of utterance (MLU) was 2.3 morphemes, and he used primarily two- and three-word combinations such as "mas agua" and "perro come." Grammatical morphemes frequently omitted included verb tense marking and plural -s/-n endings. In the English sample, MLU was 2.1 morphemes, with omission of copula "is," regular past tense -ed, and third person singular -s noted across 8 of 10 obligatory contexts.

Vocabulary and semantic skills, assessed informally and via the BESA Semantics subtest, were a relative strength, with Mateo correctly labeling 17 of 20 common objects and demonstrating appropriate categorization skills (for example, sorting "frutas" versus "animales" with 9/10 accuracy).

Oral-Motor and Hearing Status

Oral-motor examination was within normal limits for structure and function, with adequate lip rounding, tongue lateralization, and diadochokinetic rates for age. As noted above, Mateo's most recent audiological evaluation on March 18, 2026 documented hearing within normal limits bilaterally; however, given his extensive history of recurrent otitis media during the critical period for speech sound acquisition (ages 8 to 24 months), fluctuating conductive hearing loss during that window is considered a likely contributing factor to his current speech and language profile.

IMPRESSIONS

Mateo Hernández Cruz is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish-English) male presenting with a moderate-to-severe mixed expressive-receptive language disorder affecting both of his languages, alongside a moderate speech sound disorder characterized by fronting, gliding, and final consonant deletion patterns consistent with, but more persistent than, typical phonological development for his age. Importantly, Mateo's difficulties are present across both Spanish and English, which, per bilingual assessment best practice and corroborated by the BESA bilingual composite scores, supports a true language disorder rather than a language difference attributable to typical second-language acquisition or sequential bilingual exposure.

Mateo's history of chronic otitis media with effusion during a developmentally sensitive period, combined with his 34-week prematurity and NICU stay, are considered likely contributing risk factors to his current profile, though his language and speech difficulties appear to extend beyond what would be expected from hearing history alone, particularly given his currently normal hearing sensitivity.

Reduced intelligibility, combined with family members such as Sol frequently interpreting on his behalf, appears to be contributing to Mateo's growing frustration and withdrawal from peer interactions at Little Learners Bilingual Academy and during community activities such as the library storytime program. Continued compensatory "translation" by family members, while well-intentioned, may reduce Mateo's opportunities to practice independent communication and should be addressed through family coaching.

Mateo meets eligibility criteria for Early Intervention services under the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program based on standardized scores at least 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in both receptive and expressive language domains across both of his languages, as well as moderate impairment in speech sound production affecting intelligibility and social participation.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo is recommended for bilingual (Spanish-English) speech-language therapy services through the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program, to be coordinated with service coordinator Brenda Walsh of Guilford County CDSA at the upcoming IFSP review scheduled for November 5, 2026.

2. Treatment approach should emphasize a hybrid model combining principles of Cycles phonological approach for speech sound intervention, targeting fronting and final consonant deletion patterns first, and a focused language stimulation approach informed by Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies to support expressive morphosyntax and increase independent verbal output across both languages.

3. Services should be delivered primarily in Spanish, Mateo's dominant home language, with English incorporated given his dual-language educational environment at Little Learners Bilingual Academy.

4. Parent coaching is strongly recommended to reduce sibling and caregiver "interpreting" for Mateo and to increase opportunities for him to practice communication repair strategies independently. Specific coaching should be offered to Lucía Rodríguez Hernández, Javier Hernández Cruz, and, as appropriate, caregiver Marisela Pérez, who provides regular evening childcare.

5. Continued audiological monitoring is recommended given Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media, with follow-up evaluation recommended if any signs of recurrent effusion or hearing fluctuation are observed; referral back to Dr. Patricia Owens at Carolina Hearing & Balance Associates at Triad Regional Health – University Campus should occur promptly if symptoms recur.

6. Collaboration with classroom staff, including Maestra Ana Flores and Ms. Johnson at Little Learners Bilingual Academy, is recommended to support generalization of therapy targets into the classroom setting and to encourage structured peer interaction opportunities with classmates such as Liam, Emma, and Camila.

7. The family may benefit from continued connection to community language-rich activities such as the "Cuentos y Canciones" program at the Greensboro Public Library – Glenwood Branch and could also benefit from exploring additional bilingual family support programming through El Centro Hispano of the Triad, which offers parent workshops and developmental support groups in Spanish.

8. Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan accordingly.

SUMMARY OF ELIGIBILITY AND NEXT STEPS

Based on the results of this comprehensive bilingual evaluation, Mateo Hernández Cruz presents with a bilingual language disorder and a moderate speech sound disorder impacting intelligibility and social-emotional functioning. He meets criteria for Early Intervention services through the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program and would benefit from the services outlined above. This report will be shared with the family, Guilford County CDSA, and Little Learners Bilingual Academy with written parental consent, and findings will be reviewed at the IFSP meeting on November 5, 2026.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Mateo. Please contact the undersigned with any questions regarding this report or the recommendations outlined above.

MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA

Mateo (de aquí en adelante "pt") fue referido al servicio de patología del habla-lenguaje de CPSLT por su pediatra, Dr. Álvarez, debido a preocupación continua de la familia y del personal de daycare sobre su desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo, inteligibilidad del habla, y dificultad para seguir instrucciones de 2 pasos. La mamá, Lucía Rodríguez Méndez, y el papá, Andrés Cruz Paredes, refieren que pt usa aprox 40-50 palabras combinadas entre inglés y español, principalmente en español, y que CG frecuentemente tiene que "traducir" lo que dice pt para que otros adultos y niños lo entiendan. Esta es la primera evaluación formal de habla-lenguaje para pt a esta edad; recibió seguimiento del programa de intervención temprana del CDSA del Piedmont entre los 18 meses y los 30 meses de edad b/c retraso motor leve, pero fue dado de alta de ese servicio en March 2024 sin seguimiento de lenguaje.

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO MÉDICO

Según reporta CG, el embarazo de Mateo fue de término completo, edad gestacional de 39 semanas, sin complicaciones prenatales significativas más allá de diabetes gestacional controlada con dieta. Parto vaginal en el Duke Regional Hospital; peso al nacer 7 lbs 4 oz; Apgar 8/9. No hubo estancia en NICU. Hitos motores gruesos levemente retrasados (caminó independiente aprox 16 meses), lo cual motivó la referencia inicial al CDSA. Hitos de lenguaje también retrasados: primeras palabras aprox 20 meses, combinaciones de 2 palabras aprox 34 meses.

Historia médica: pt tuvo 4 episodios de otitis media entre los 12 y los 24 meses de edad, tratados con antibiótico oral; no requirió tubos de ventilación. Audiología reporta audición dentro de límites normales bilateral por timpanometría y screening conductual en February 2025 (ver reporte de Hannah Weiss, audióloga, Duke Health Pediatric Audiology). No historia de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones significativas, ni cirugías. Visión no evaluada formalmente pero CG no reporta preocupación. Pt toma actualmente solo vitaminas, sin medicamentos relacionados a conducta o desarrollo. Diagnóstico médico actual según pediatra: Z13.42 (screening de desarrollo) pendiente de confirmación tras esta eval.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo vive en casa con su mamá, su papá, su hermana mayor Luz (de 9 años), y su abuela materna Paz Méndez, quien vive con la familia y provee cuidado de CG aprox 3 días por semana mientras los padres trabajan. Lucía trabaja en Blue Ridge Textiles como supervisora de turno, y Andrés trabaja en construcción con una compañía local. El idioma primario del hogar es español; CG reporta que ambos padres hablan inglés conversacional pero prefieren español en casa, y que Luz es bilingüe dominante en inglés por la escuela. Paz habla únicamente español con pt.

Exposición al inglés: pt asiste de lunes a viernes, de 7:30 a.m. a 5:00 p.m., al Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos, un programa bilingüe donde la maestra principal, Srta. Jennifer Davis, reporta que pt interactúa con compañeros como Emily y Noah mayormente de forma no verbal o con gestos, y que su inteligibilidad en el salón es aprox 30% para oyentes no familiares. La familia también participa activamente en el programa de cuentos bilingües de la Biblioteca Regional del Condado de Durham los sábados por la mañana, y recibe apoyo de transporte de la Fundación Manos Unidas, una organización sin fines de lucro local que ayuda a familias de bajos ingresos a llegar a citas médicas.

No hay historia familiar reportada de trastornos del habla o lenguaje en primer grado, aunque CG menciona que un tío paterno tuvo "problema para hablar" de niño sin diagnóstico formal. Historia de desarrollo bilingüe: la familia reporta exposición simultánea a ambos idiomas desde el nacimiento, con predominancia de español en casa (aprox 80%) e inglés en daycare (aprox 100% del tiempo escolar).

OBSERVACIÓN CONDUCTUAL Y MÉTODOS DE EVALUACIÓN

La evaluación se llevó a cabo en 2 sesiones en las oficinas de Carolina Pediatric Speech Therapy, con la mamá presente en ambas sesiones. Pt se presentó cooperativo pero tímido al inicio, con calentamiento gradual durante los primeros 10 minutos. Rapport se estableció con juguetes preferidos (carritos, bloques) y reforzadores sociales. Atención sostenida aprox 8-10 minutos por actividad con descansos breves. Pt mostró juego simbólico apropiado para la edad (alimentar muñeco, construir torre y "chocar" carritos con sonidos vocales). No se observaron conductas repetitivas atípicas, contacto visual apropiado, y reciprocidad social presente aunque con iniciación verbal limitada.

Se administraron pruebas estandarizadas en español e inglés según protocolo bilingüe, complementadas con muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, observación de juego, y entrevista con CG. Se revisó también reporte previo de Bayley-4 (Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition) administrado por el CDSA en January 2024 cuando pt tenía 30 meses, y reporte de Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale de esa misma evaluación, los cuales mostraron retraso leve-moderado en lenguaje receptivo y expresivo en ese momento.

| PLS-5 (Preschool Language Scale-5), Spanish Edition — Auditory Comprehension | Lenguaje receptivo | 78 | 7mo percentil | 2 años 11 meses |
| PLS-5 — Expressive Communication | Lenguaje expresivo | 72 | 3er percentil | 2 años 6 meses |
| PLS-5 — Total Language Score | Lenguaje total | 73 | 4to percentil | — |
| Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5) | Vocabulario receptivo (inglés) | 81 | 10mo percentil | — |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | Articulación | 65 | 1er percentil | — |

Nota sobre interpretación: dado el perfil bilingüe de pt, los puntajes del PPVT-5 (administrado en inglés) deben interpretarse con cautela, ya que no reflejan vocabulario total combinado entre los dos idiomas. Se calculó un conteo de vocabulario conceptual combinado informal (CG report + muestra directa) de aprox 180 palabras entre ambos idiomas, lo cual sigue por debajo de lo esperado para la edad.

ANÁLISIS DE HABLA Y LENGUAJE ESPONTÁNEO

Se obtuvo muestra de lenguaje espontáneo de 50 enunciados durante juego libre w/ CG y w/ clínica. Longitud media de enunciado (LME) en morfemas: 2.1, aprox 1.5 desviaciones estándar por debajo de la media para la edad. Pt combina 2 palabras consistentemente ("más agua", "no quiero") y ocasionalmente 3 palabras ("mamá dame eso"). Uso de morfología gramatical limitado; omite artículos y preposiciones frecuentemente ("quiero pelota" en vez de "quiero la pelota"). Vocabulario funcional presente para ítems de alta frecuencia (comida, animales, familia) pero limitado para categorías abstractas (colores, números más allá de "uno", "dos").

En el análisis fonológico (GFTA-3 y muestra espontánea), pt presenta los siguientes procesos fonológicos persistentes más allá de la edad esperada: sustitución de /r/ por [l] (ej. "lata" por "rata"), simplificación de grupos consonánticos (ej. "pato" por "plato", "tes" por "tres"), y posteriorización ocasional de /t/ a [k] en posición inicial. Inteligibilidad para oyente familiar estimada en 70%; para oyente no familiar, aprox 35-40%, consistente con reporte de daycare. Con mod cues (modelo + repetición), pt logró producir correctamente 6/10 palabras objetivo de 2 sílabas; con min cues, su exactitud bajó a 2/10. Praxia oral motora dentro de límites normales; no hay evidencia de apraxia infantil del habla.

Pt siguió instrucciones de 1 paso de forma consistente (9/10 intentos) y de 2 pasos no relacionados de forma inconsistente (4/10 intentos), con mejora notable cuando las instrucciones incluían gestos o contexto visual de apoyo. Comprensión de conceptos básicos (adentro/afuera, grande/pequeño) presente aprox 70% de las veces en ambos idiomas.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados estandarizados, el análisis de muestra de lenguaje, la historia del desarrollo, y la observación directa, pt presenta un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo de moderado a severo, con compromiso fonológico-articulatorio concomitante, en el contexto de desarrollo bilingüe típico de exposición simultánea. Los retrasos observados son consistentes a través de ambos idiomas (español e inglés) y no se explican únicamente por el bilingüismo, lo cual apoya un diagnóstico primario de trastorno de la comunicación más que una diferencia lingüística esperada.

Código ICD-10 sugerido: F80.2 (trastorno mixto receptivo-expresivo del lenguaje) con F80.0 (trastorno fonológico) como diagnóstico secundario. Códigos CPT recomendados para servicio continuo: 92523 (evaluación de habla y lenguaje) ya facturado para esta sesión, y 92507 para terapia individual continua.

El perfil de pt es consistente con, aunque más severo que, lo documentado en la evaluación previa del Rossetti y Bayley-4 a los 30 meses, sugiriendo que el retraso no se ha resuelto espontáneamente y que, de hecho, la brecha entre pt y sus pares se ha ampliado desde el alta del CDSA en March 2024.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda terapia de habla-lenguaje individual, 2 veces por semana, 45 minutos por sesión, con enfoque bilingüe español-inglés según preferencia de la familia, a través de CPSLT.
2. Enfoque de tratamiento: se recomienda el enfoque Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk") para entrenamiento de CG, combinado con el abordaje de Cycles para los procesos fonológicos identificados (/r/, grupos consonánticos, posteriorización).
3. Se sugiere re-evaluación de audición formal con audiograma conductual completo dado historia de otitis media recurrente, aunque screening reciente fue normal.
4. Se recomienda consulta con el CDSA del Piedmont para determinar elegibilidad de reingreso a servicios de intervención temprana dado el deterioro relativo desde el alta, contactando a la coordinadora M.R..
5. Se anima a la familia a continuar participando en el programa de cuentos bilingües de la Biblioteca Regional del Condado de Durham y a mantener comunicación con Srta. Davis en el Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos para apoyar generalización de metas en el ambiente escolar.
6. Se recomienda monitoreo de progreso cada 6 meses con re-administración de PLS-5 y GFTA-3.
7. Se proveerán materiales de estimulación del lenguaje en español e inglés para uso en casa w/ CG, Lucía, Andrés, y Paz, dado que todos participan activamente en el cuidado diario de pt.

Se discutieron estos hallazgos y recomendaciones con Lucía Rodríguez Méndez el August 18, 2025. CG reporta estar de acuerdo con el plan e interesada en comenzar terapia lo antes posible. Se envió copia de este informe a Dr. Kevin Álvarez y al CDSA del Piedmont con consentimiento firmado de la familia en archivo.
