Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC
Informe de Evaluación de Habla y Lenguaje — Bilingüe (Español/Inglés)

Niño/a: Mateo Hernández Cruz (apodo "Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de marzo de 2022
Edad cronológica al momento de evaluación: 4;7
Sexo: masculino
Fecha de evaluación: 2 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del informe: 9 de octubre de 2026
ID de expediente clínico: CPT-2206-0451
ID de Medicaid: 987654321A
Evaluadora: Dra. Ana Martínez, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingüe español/inglés
Coordinadora de servicios (Parte C): Carla Jiménez, CDSA de Durham
Pediatra de cabecera: Dr. Rajesh Patel
Dirección de la clínica: 4215 Page Road, Suite 220, Durham, NC 27703
Tel. clínica: (919) 555-0148 | Correo: amartinez@carolinapedstherapy.com
Consentimiento informado firmado por Lucía Rodríguez el 28 de septiembre de 2026.

S: (Subjetivo)

Hx de referencia. Evaluación solicitada por Lucía Rodríguez (madre) y Javier Hernández (padre), motivados por preocupación persistente sobre inteligibilidad y lenguaje expresivo de Teo, 4;7. Refieren cita: "habla como con la boca llena" y que personas fuera de casa "no le entienden casi nada". Preocupación inicial surgió a los 18 meses, cuando Mateo aún no combinaba dos palabras y tenía vocabulario expresivo limitado (<20 palabras). Evaluado por Early Intervention a través de CDSA de Durham a los 20 meses; IFSP activo desde 5 de enero de 2023. Revisión semestral más reciente: 12 de agosto de 2026. Resultado/meta #2 (lenguaje expresivo, combinar 3+ palabras) y Resultado #3 (inteligibilidad fonológica) siguen activos y parcialmente alcanzados por reporte de proveedor anterior.

Hx de embarazo y parto. Embarazo a término (39 semanas), sin complicaciones, madre niega uso de sustancias, tabaco o alcohol durante embarazo. Parto vaginal espontáneo en Duke University Hospital. Apgar 8/9. Peso al nacer 3,200 gramos (7 lb 1 oz). Sin ingreso a UCIN, alta a las 48 horas de vida, junto con Lucía Rodríguez.

Hx médica. Hitos motores dentro de límites esperados (caminó a los 13 meses). Hx de 4 episodios de otitis media aguda entre 12 y 26 meses, tratados con antibióticos; colocación de tubos de ventilación bilateral el 7 de junio de 2024 por Dra. Susan Kim, otorrinolaringóloga. Madre reporta mejoría de audición aparente tras tubos, aunque retraso de lenguaje persistió. Visión evaluada por pediatra, WNL. Sin hx de convulsiones, sin hospitalizaciones adicionales. Dx actuales en expediente, confirmados por pediatra Dr. Rajesh Patel: F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo) y F80.0 (trastorno fonológico), ambos pendientes de reconfirmación en esta evaluación (ver A:). Sin dx de autismo, aunque seguimiento de desarrollo general continúa abierto por pediatra como precaución.

Hx familiar. Madre refiere hx personal de "terapia de habla" en la niñez, sin detalles de dx. Hermana mayor, Luz Hernández (7 años), desarrollo típico, sin hx de retraso de habla/lenguaje, actualmente en 2do grado. Primo materno, Sol Cruz (6 años), con dx de trastorno del espectro autista, seguido por otro proveedor fuera de esta clínica; familia reporta cierta preocupación de que Teo "se parezca" a Sol en algunos aspectos sociales, aunque niega conductas repetitivas marcadas o intereses restringidos en Teo. Abuela materna, Rosa Cruz, cuida a Mateo dos días por semana (martes y jueves) mientras ambos padres trabajan; habla únicamente español con el niño y refuerza vocabulario de rutinas diarias (comida, baño). Niñera ocasional de fin de semana: Patricia Gómez, vecina de la familia.

Hx de lenguaje y exposición bilingüe. Hogar bilingüe; madre estima que el español representa aproximadamente 80% del input lingüístico en el hogar, inglés 20% (principalmente a través de televisión y hermana mayor, quien es dominante en inglés por la escuela). Teo asiste de lunes a viernes, 7:30 a.m. a 5:00 p.m., al centro de cuido infantil El Jardín de Mariposas, ubicado en Durham, NC, donde el ambiente del aula es mayormente en inglés con apoyo bilingüe parcial. Maestra principal del salón, Srta. Patricia Gutiérrez, reporta por correo electrónico y llamada telefónica previa a esta evaluación que Teo participa con gusto en actividades grupales, busca a sus compañeros para jugar, pero se frustra visiblemente cuando sus pares no comprenden lo que dice; compañero cercano, Diego, frecuentemente "traduce" las intenciones de Teo a otros niños del salón. Otra compañera mencionada por la maestra, Valentina, evita jugar con Mateo en actividades de conversación dirigida, aunque sí participa en juego físico/motor grueso con él.

Familia participa activamente en actividades comunitarias de apoyo al lenguaje: programa semanal "Cuentos Bilingües" los sábados en la sucursal North Regional de la Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Durham; asistencia dominical a clase de niños en español en Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, en Durham. Familia recibió apoyo nutricional de WIC desde el nacimiento de Teo hasta los 3 años; actualmente en lista de espera para beca de cuido infantil a través de Smart Start del condado. Familia fue referida previamente a Early Head Start pero no obtuvo cupo disponible en su zona. Trabajadora social de caso en DSS asignada para seguimiento de beneficios es Yolanda Pérez.

Hx ocupacional de los padres. Madre, Lucía Rodríguez, trabaja como auxiliar de enfermería en Duke Regional Hospital, turnos rotativos de 12 horas. Padre, Javier Hernández, trabaja en construcción con horario variable y frecuentes viajes cortos fuera del condado, lo cual limita su disponibilidad para sesiones de terapia programadas en horario diurno.

Hx de mascotas/contexto doméstico. Familia tiene un perro, Max, descrito por madre como "parte de la familia"; Teo usa frecuentemente el nombre de Max en juego simbólico y como motivador en actividades de lenguaje en casa.

Hx de terapia previa. Mateo recibió terapia de habla-lenguaje en el hogar a través de Early Intervention, una vez por semana, desde marzo de 2024 hasta su transición al preescolar actual en agosto de 2026. Proveedora anterior: Mónica Suárez, CCC-SLP. Reporte de progreso más reciente disponible (recibido por fax de proveedora anterior) documenta mejoría de longitud media de enunciado (LME/MLU) de 2.1 a 3.4 morfemas en el curso de 18 meses de tx, y aumento de vocabulario expresivo estimado de 50 a más de 300 palabras.

O: (Objetivo)

Sesión de evaluación realizada el 2 de octubre de 2026, de 9:00 a.m. a 11:15 a.m., en consultorio de la clínica, con madre presente en sala durante la mayor parte de la sesión. Evaluación conducida completamente en español por evaluadora bilingüe nativa; no se requirió intérprete. Niño cooperador durante toda la sesión, afecto positivo, buen contacto visual, atención sostenida con descansos breves cada 15 minutos aproximadamente; sin conductas disruptivas.

Pruebas estandarizadas administradas (normas en español cuando disponibles):

Prueba / Subprueba — Puntaje — Interpretación
CELF-5 Español — Comprensión Auditiva — SS 76 (percentil 5) — por debajo de lo esperado
CELF-5 Español — Estructura de Oraciones — SS 71 (percentil 3) — significativamente por debajo
CELF-5 Español — Recordando Oraciones — SS 68 (percentil 2) — significativamente por debajo
Índice de Lenguaje Receptivo — 74 (IC 95%: 70–78) — rango deficiente
Índice de Lenguaje Expresivo — 69 (IC 95%: 65–73) — rango deficiente
GFTA-3 (adaptado p/análisis fonológico) — SS 72, edad equiv. 3;0 — retraso fonológico moderado-severo
PLS-5 Spanish Auditory Comprehension — edad equiv. 3;2
PLS-5 Spanish Expressive Communication — edad equiv. 2;10

Facturación de hoy: 92523 (evaluación de habla y lenguaje), 92507 modificador de prueba de tx trial.

Muestra de habla espontánea (50 enunciados, contexto de juego libre en español). LME 3.4 morfemas, consistente con reporte previo. Inventario fonético: produce consonantes bilabiales, nasales y oclusivas de forma consistente; procesos fonológicos persistentes observados:
- Reducción de grupos consonánticos: "["pato"]" por "plato" (/pl/ → /p/).
- Omisión de sílaba inicial: "["apato"]" por "zapato".
- Sustitución /ɾ/ por /l/: "["calo"]" por "carro".
- Fronting inconsistente de /k/ a /t/: "["tasa"]" por "casa" (en 4 de 10 oportunidades).
- Posteriorización ocasional de [s] a [ʃ] en posición final de sílaba.

Precisión de producción de consonantes (PCC) estimada en 65%. Inteligibilidad en contexto conocido (con familia) 75%; con desconocidos, sin contexto, 40%.

Comprensión de instrucciones de 2 pasos sin apoyo contextual: 6/10 (60%) correctas. Repetición de oraciones de complejidad creciente: 5/10 correctas, con errores principalmente en estructuras subordinadas y orden de palabras.

Prueba de narrativa (secuencia de 4 láminas): produjo 3 de 5 elementos clave de la historia (personaje, problema, acción, resolución), sin incluir marco temporal; nivel considerado por debajo de lo esperado para la edad.

Tx trial dentro de la sesión (vocabulario de acción con apoyo visual y modelado): 8/10 (80%) de respuestas correctas con mod cues (modelo verbal + apoyo visual); sin apoyo, desempeño cayó a 3/10 (30%). Respondió favorablemente a estrategias de expansión y modelado tipo Hanen.

Prueba de praxias orales no verbales y verbales: sin hallazgos sugestivos de apraxia infantil del habla; diadococinesia (DDK) dentro de límites normales para la edad en tareas de repetición silábica alternante. Examen oral-motor: estructura y función dentro de límites normales, sin hallazgos de fisura submucosa ni frenillo lingual restrictivo. Cribado auditivo: pasó cribado conductual en consultorio; madre reporta tubos de ventilación en buen estado por chequeo reciente.

Observación pragmática y juego simbólico: iniciativa social adecuada para la edad, contacto visual recíproco apropiado, respuesta consistente a nombre, juego simbólico de nivel esperado (tema de "rescate" con figuras de acción, incluyó diálogo entre personajes aunque con inteligibilidad reducida). Sin conductas repetitivas ni intereses restringidos observados durante la sesión; sin banderas rojas adicionales de espectro autista identificadas en esta evaluación puntual.

A: (Análisis)

Resultados de esta evaluación son consistentes con trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo, F80.2, de severidad moderada a severa en ambos dominios, junto con trastorno fonológico, F80.0, de severidad moderada-severa, en el contexto de desarrollo bilingüe típico español-inglés. Los déficits observados en español (idioma dominante y de mayor exposición) no se explican únicamente por la exposición bilingüe, dado que el desempeño está significativamente por debajo de lo esperado en comprensión y expresión en el idioma de mayor dominio. El patrón de errores fonológicos (reducción de grupos consonánticos, sustitución /ɾ/ por /l/, fronting inconsistente) es consistente con un trastorno fonológico primario y no representa transferencia dialectal regional esperada ni interferencia típica entre español e inglés en desarrollo bilingüe simultáneo.

Factores contribuyentes probables: hx de otitis media recurrente entre los 12 y 26 meses pudo haber contribuido al retraso inicial de adquisición fonológica por reducción intermitente de input auditivo claro durante periodo crítico. Hx familiar materna de dificultades de habla en la niñez sugiere posible componente hereditario, aunque sin diagnóstico formal documentado de la madre. Primo con dx de TEA no constituye, por evidencia de esta evaluación, indicador de riesgo compartido de espectro autista en Teo; sin embargo, dado hx familiar, se recomienda monitoreo continuo de hitos sociales por parte de pediatra.

Impacto funcional significativo: inteligibilidad reducida (40% con desconocidos) limita participación social plena en el aula de El Jardín de Mariposas y en actividades comunitarias como el programa de biblioteca. Maestra Srta. Gutiérrez documenta frustración observable y dependencia de intermediación de pares (p. ej. Diego) para comunicarse, lo cual representa riesgo de evitación verbal progresiva si no se interviene.

Mateo continúa siendo elegible para servicios de patología del habla-lenguaje bajo IDEA Parte C hasta su transición a Parte B. Reunión de transición con distrito escolar y CDSA de Durham está programada para 20 de enero de 2027; se recomienda que resultados de esta evaluación formen parte del expediente de elegibilidad para servicios preescolares especiales.

P: (Plan)

1. Continuar terapia de habla-lenguaje individual, 2 veces por semana, sesiones de 30 minutos, bajo CPT 92507, con enfoque combinado: abordaje fonológico basado en Ciclos (Cycles) dirigido a procesos de reducción de grupos consonánticos y sustitución /ɾ/-/l/, junto con intervención de lenguaje expresivo usando modelado, expansión y técnicas del enfoque Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" adaptadas al español.

2. Meta a corto plazo (6-8 semanas): producción de grupos consonánticos /pl/, /kl/, /bl/ en palabras aisladas con mod cues a 80% de precisión en 3 sesiones consecutivas.

3. Meta a corto plazo paralela: combinar 3-4 palabras en enunciados espontáneos describiendo acciones, con apoyo visual, 80% de oportunidades en contexto estructurado.

4. Capacitación a padres una vez al mes, presencial o por telesalud, enfocada en estrategias de modelado, tiempo de espera y expansión en el hogar; coordinar calendario con disponibilidad laboral de Javier Hernández cuando sea posible, dado horario variable.

Patricia Gutiérrez en El Jardín de Mariposas: modelar enunciados cortos y claros, ofrecer tiempo de espera de al menos 5 segundos antes de repetir o reformular, usar apoyo visual durante instrucciones de grupo, y fomentar interacción directa entre Teo y pares como Valentina en actividades estructuradas de baja demanda verbal para construir confianza antes de aumentar demanda comunicativa.

9. Enviar copia de este informe, con consentimiento firmado, a pediatra Dr. Rajesh Patel y a trabajadora social de DSS, Yolanda Pérez, para expediente de servicios sociales y seguimiento de beneficios.

+ Name: María José Fuentes Almonte
+ CA: 3;4
+ Context: Annual IFSP Review, Cumberland County CDSA (Children's Developmental Services Agency), conducted at the family's home in Hope Mills, Cumberland County
+ Date: October 6, 2026
+ Examiner/Author: Dr. Carolina Vega-Martínez, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist, Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Therapy, PLLC (also known as Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Therapy or CBPT)

Summary:

María José is a 3;4-year-old girl who receives speech-language therapy through CBPT under her active IFSP managed by Cumberland County CDSA. This annual review was completed on October 6, 2026 with her mother, Lucía Fuentes Almonte, her father, Henry Almonte, her service coordinator, Mr. Derek Sanders, and the undersigned clinician present. The family's older daughter, Esperanza "Hope" Almonte, age 7 years, was also home during the visit and briefly joined the session to model turn-taking games with her sister.

FAMILY INFORMATION

María José lives with her parents, Lucía Fuentes Almonte and Henry Almonte, and her sister Hope, at 214 Rosewood Court, Hope Mills, NC 28348. The family also receives regular support from María José's maternal grandmother, Rosa Fuentes, who provides childcare two afternoons a week while Mrs. Almonte attends English classes through Cumberland County Partnership for Children. Home phone: (910) 483-2217. Mother's email: lucia.almonte28@gmail.com. Medicaid ID: 784302165B. CDSA record number: CFV-20193.

The family's primary language at home is Spanish, with Mr. Almonte communicating primarily in English at work. Both parents report feeling comfortable asking questions during sessions when the clinician, Dr. Vega-Martínez, provides bilingual support, and they have also worked with an interpreter, Ms. Patricia Owusu, during medical appointments.

SERVICE COORDINATION AND AGENCY INVOLVEMENT

Service coordination is provided through Cumberland County CDSA, located in Fayetteville, by Mr. Derek Sanders. The family is also enrolled with Cumberland County DSS for food assistance, and Mrs. Almonte receives nutrition support through WIC at the Fayetteville clinic. María José's pediatrician, Dr. Samuel Okafor, at Cape Fear Valley Pediatrics, referred the family to Cumberland County CDSA after noting delayed expressive language at the 18-month well-child visit. María José previously attended a parent-child playgroup through Early Head Start in Hope Mills but was not enrolled in a classroom placement at this review.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES (in the family's own words)

Mrs. Almonte shared, translated with permission: "Nos preocupa que no pueda decir frases completas todavía. Ella entiende mucho, pero cuando quiere algo solo señala o hace sonidos." ("We are worried she still cannot say full sentences. She understands a lot, but when she wants something she only points or makes sounds.")

Mr. Almonte added, "At daycare pickup, I notice other kids her age talking in sentences and she's still mostly using single words. We want her to be ready for pre-k."

The family's priorities for this IFSP period are:
1. María José will use two-to-three-word combinations in both Spanish and English during daily routines.
2. María José will increase her sound repertoire so unfamiliar listeners, including her grandmother Rosa, can understand her requests.
3. The family wants strategies for supporting bilingual language development without "confusing" her, a concern Mrs. Almonte voiced directly: "Mi suegra piensa que deberíamos hablarle solo en inglés."

DAILY ROUTINES

María José's typical day begins around 7:00 AM with breakfast at home with her family. Rosa arrives around 1:00 PM on Tuesdays and Thursdays to care for María José while her parents are at work and class. Bath time occurs nightly around 7:30 PM, followed by a bedtime routine with books read in both languages by Mrs. Almonte. María José enjoys playing with her stuffed rabbit, which the family calls Conejo, and frequently brings him to therapy sessions.

Hope helps care for her sister by narrating play and modeling words during shared activities, which the family identified as a strength to build on.

OTHER AGENCIES AND SUPPORTS

In addition to Cumberland County CDSA and Cumberland County DSS, the family is connected with Smart Start of Cumberland County, which provided a car seat safety class the family attended in September 2026. Mr. Almonte works at Fayetteville Metal Fabricators, and his employer has approved flexible scheduling for him to attend therapy sessions monthly.

DEVELOPMENTAL SUMMARY

Administration of the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) on September 29, 2026 yielded an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), with a Total Language score of 72 (3rd percentile). These scores reflect moderate delay relative to same-age peers in both English and Spanish administration, consistent with prior findings. Bilingual administration included both languages per PLS-5 Spanish norms, with the examiner selecting the higher score per item per standard bilingual scoring procedure.

Articulation screening revealed stimulable productions of /k/ and /g/ in isolation, though María José continues to substitute [t] for /k/ in connected speech (e.g., "tasa" for "casa"). She produced the target word "agua" correctly in 6 of 10 trials with minimal cues, and "more" in English with moderate cues in 4 of 10 trials.

María José's birth history is unremarkable: she was born at 39 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 7 lbs 2 oz and Apgar scores of 8 and 9. No significant medical history is reported. ICD-10 code F80.1 (Expressive Language Disorder) is used for billing purposes under CPT code 92523.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: María José will combine two to three words to request desired items and actions during daily routines (snack, bath, play) in both Spanish and English, as measured by caregiver report and direct observation, with 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive sessions.
- Strategies: Use of expansion and parallel talk during routines; family coached to model two-word combinations such as "más agua" and "more milk"; visual supports introduced using a modified PECS-style choice board.

Outcome 2: María José will increase intelligibility of target words containing velar sounds to 70% accuracy with minimal cues across unfamiliar listeners, including extended family.
- Strategies: Cycles approach targeting velar fronting; home practice list sent weekly to family and to Rosa with picture cards; clinician models correct production with exaggerated articulatory placement, cueing level reduced from moderate to minimal over the review period.

Outcome 3: The family will receive bilingual language strategies and written materials addressing the benefits of dual-language exposure, with satisfaction rated by caregiver report at the next review.
- Strategies: Clinician provided research summary (in Spanish and English) on bilingual first-language acquisition; discussed with extended family present during a joint visit that included Rosa; recommended continued use of both languages at home per family preference.

PROGRESS SINCE LAST REVIEW

Since the previous IFSP review on April 14, 2026, María José has progressed from primarily single-word utterances to occasional two-word combinations, most consistently in Spanish ("más leche," "no quiero"). Her Expressive Communication standard score improved from 65 to 71 on repeat PLS-5 administration, though she remains below the 10th percentile in this domain. Her Auditory Comprehension score remained relatively stable.

María José was observed interacting with peers during a community playdate organized by a family friend; her peer, Daniela, was noted to understand approximately half of María José's spontaneous utterances without context.

SERVICE DELIVERY

María José currently receives speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, in the home setting, provided by Dr. Carolina Vega-Martínez of Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Therapy, PLLC. Services began on January 12, 2026 under authorization number AUTH-55920-CF. The team recommends continuing at the current frequency and intensity through the next annual review, scheduled for October 2027, with a six-month progress check scheduled for April 2027.

Mr. Sanders confirmed that transportation assistance remains available through Cumberland County CDSA if needed for future evaluations at Cape Fear Valley Pediatrics or other specialty appointments.

TEAM SIGNATURES AND CONTACT INFORMATION

Service Coordinator: Derek Sanders, Cumberland County CDSA, phone (910) 677-4420, email d.sanders@cumberlandcdsa.nc.gov

Speech-Language Pathologist: Carolina Vega-Martínez, M.S., CCC-SLP, CBPT, phone (910) 555-0192, email cvega@carolinabilingualpt.com

Parent signatures obtained from Lucía Fuentes Almonte and Henry Almonte on October 6, 2026, indicating agreement with the outcomes and services outlined above. The family was provided a written copy of this review in both English and Spanish, along with contact information for Cumberland County CDSA and Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Therapy, PLLC for questions prior to the next scheduled visit.

1920 Tate Boulevard SE, Hickory, NC 28602

October 2, 2026

Dear Lucía Rodríguez and Carlos Flores,

Thank you for meeting with us last week to review Mateo's Individualized Family Service Plan, or IFSP. It was wonderful to see Mateo Alejandro again and to hear how much he has grown since his last review on April 14, 2026. This letter sums up what we talked about. Please keep it for your records, and feel free to share it with anyone else who helps care for Mateo.

My name is María Elena Santos, MS, CCC-SLP. I am Mateo's speech-language pathologist through Carolina Bridges Therapy Services. I am bilingual in English and Spanish, so we can talk together in whichever language feels most comfortable for your family. Mateo's service coordinator at Western Piedmont CDSA, Jasmine Carter, joined the meeting too, along with our interpreter, Ana Beltrán, who made sure everyone understood each other clearly.

**Family and Child Information**

Mateo Alejandro Flores Ramírez was born on January 18, 2024, at Atrium Health Hickory, Hickory Campus. He arrived early, at 34 weeks gestation, weighing 4 pounds, 2 ounces, with Apgar scores of 6 and 8. He spent three weeks in the NICU at Atrium Health Hickory, Hickory Campus before coming home. Mateo is now 2;8 years old. He lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Carlos Flores; and his older sister, Camila, who is in kindergarten this year. His grandmother and regular babysitter, Rosa Martínez, helps with childcare most weekday mornings. His cousin Diego often comes over on weekends to play trucks with him. The family's dog, Canela, follows Mateo everywhere around the house, and he laughs every time she barks at the mail carrier.

Mateo attends Little Steps Early Learning Center three days a week. His teacher, Debbie Watts, says he is affectionate, curious, and quick to show other children his favorite toys. His closest classmate there is Emma, who he follows everywhere during free play, and he also enjoys sitting next to Jonah at snack time. Carlos works at CommScope, and Lucía stays home with Mateo on the days he is not at daycare.

**Family Concerns and Priorities**

During our visit, Lucía shared, in her own words, "I just want him to be able to tell me what he needs without getting so frustrated." Carlos added, "We want him ready for prekindergarten, and we want his sister to understand him too, not just us." You both told us that family gatherings are hard right now, because relatives sometimes cannot understand Mateo, and that this upsets him and makes him want to leave the room. You asked us to keep working on words he can use at home in both English and Spanish, and to help Camila learn simple ways to support her brother when he gets stuck trying to communicate. Lucía also mentioned that Rosa has started using some of the same strategies we modeled, and that this has made mornings calmer for everyone.

**Daily Routines**

Mateo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Camila before Rosa arrives at 7:15 a.m.. On daycare days, Carlos drops him off at 8:00 a.m. on his way to work and picks him up around 4:30 p.m.. At home, Mateo loves bath time, reading books with Lucía, and chasing Canela in the backyard. Dinner is shared family time, usually around 6:00 p.m., and Lucía told us this is when Mateo's frustration shows up most, because he wants to tell everyone about his day and does not yet have the words. Weekends often include visits from Diego and trips to the park, where Mateo likes to point out dogs that remind him of Canela.

**Other Agencies Involved**

Your family continues to work with Catawba County Department of Social Services for ongoing family support services. Lucía mentioned you recently applied for nutrition assistance through Catawba County WIC Program. Mateo is also on the waiting list for a Catawba County Partnership for Children-funded playgroup through Smart Start, and Jasmine is helping your family get a spot there. Mateo sees Dr. Nadia Osei for pediatric care at Atrium Health Pediatrics, Hickory Campus, and he was referred to Atrium Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology, Hickory Campus after a routine hearing screening flagged follow-up concerns. His audiologist there, Dr. Samuel Kwan, confirmed hearing within normal limits bilaterally on August 19, 2026. Dr. Osei also referred Mateo to Dr. Rebecca Lin, ENT, at the same Hickory Campus, to rule out chronic middle-ear fluid before our next review.

**Evaluation Results**

On September 3, 2026, I administered the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5). Mateo earned a standard score of 76 on the Auditory Comprehension subtest (5th percentile) and a standard score of 72 on the Expressive Communication subtest (3rd percentile), with an age equivalent of 18 months for expressive language. On the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition, he produced initial and final consonants with moderate cues, substituting /t/ for /k/ and [w] for /l/, which is consistent with phonological patterns typical before age 3;0. During play, he said "wa wa" for water and "ba" for ball, each with moderate cues. He imitated two-word phrases on 4 of 10 trials and used single words spontaneously on 7 of 10 trials, or about 70% of opportunities offered.

**Outcomes, Strategies, and Progress**

*Outcome 1: Mateo will use two-word combinations in English and Spanish to request and comment during daily routines.*
Strategy: We are using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, including following Mateo's lead, expanding his single words into two-word phrases, and pausing to give him time to respond. Lucía and Rosa are practicing this during snack time and bath time, in whichever language Mateo starts in. He has progressed from using two-word combinations on 0 of 10 opportunities at intake to 4 of 10 at this review.

*Outcome 2: Mateo will increase intelligibility of target sounds in single words with moderate to minimal cues.*
Strategy: We are using PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cues to support jaw and lip placement for /b/, /p/, and /m/, paired with repetition of target words during shared book reading at home. Mateo's intelligibility in known contexts has improved from 40% at intake to 65% at this review, based on the Intelligibility in Context Scale.

*Outcome 3: The family will have strategies to reduce Mateo's frustration when he is not understood.*
Strategy: We modeled a simple "show me" gesture system for Camila and Rosa to use when Mateo is upset, paired with offering two real-object choices instead of asking open-ended questions. Carlos reported this has already reduced tantrums at dinner, and he would like to try the same approach when Diego visits on weekends.

**Service Dates and Billing**

Mateo receives speech-language therapy twice weekly, on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 10:00 a.m., for 30-minute sessions billed under CPT code 92507. His current authorization runs from July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, under Medicaid ID 638204751B and CDSA record number WP-2024-00318. Our next IFSP review is scheduled for January 15, 2027, at 9:30 a.m., at the Western Piedmont CDSA office.

If you need to reach me between sessions, you can call or text my direct line at 828-555-0199, or email me at maria.santos@carolinabridgestherapy.com. Jasmine can be reached at (828) 555-0173. Rosa also asked us to note her sister's number, Mateo's great-aunt in Guatemala, who often calls to ask about his progress: +502 2234-5678.

Thank you for being such dedicated partners in Mateo's progress. He is working hard, and so is your whole family. Please let us know if anything in this letter needs correction, or if your priorities have changed since we last talked.

Warmly,

María Elena Santos, MS, CCC-SLP
Speech-Language Pathologist, Carolina Bridges Therapy Services
Office: (828) 555-0188 | Fax: 828.555.0120

Nota de sesión – Terapia del habla y lenguaje

October 6, 2026, 3:15 PM, Carolina Pines Health Pediatric Rehab – Siler City Campus. Camilo Andrés Ventura (fecha de nacimiento 04/11/2023, edad 3;5) llegó con su mamá, Rosa Ventura, y su hermana mayor Yareli para su sesión semanal de 30 minutos. La familia llegó un poco tarde porque salieron directo de la Little Blessings Daycare, donde Camilo está en el salón de Ms. Ortiz ("the Bumblebee Room"). Rosa comentó, "está diciendo más palabras en la casa, pero en la escuela se queda callado," lo cual coincide con lo reportado por Ms. Ortiz por correo la semana pasada.

Subjective: Rosa reporta que Camilo ha estado produciendo aproximaciones de "agua" y "más" espontáneamente en casa, aunque con su abuela, Carmen, quien lo cuida los jueves, se mantiene mayormente en silencio. También mencionó que su esposo, Héctor Ventura, trabaja turnos largos en Siler City Poultry Processing y no pudo asistir hoy. La familia sigue conectada con su coordinadora de servicios, Denise Alvarado, de la oficina del CDSA de Piedmont Triad, y está pendiente la revisión del IFSP para November 18, 2026 (Outcome #2).

Objective: Se trabajaron metas de vocabulario funcional usando PECS en combinación con modelado verbal. Camilo produjo /m/ inicial en "más" con mod cues en 6 of 10 ensayos (60%), mejora comparado con la sesión anterior. También intentó "agua" → "aba", con sustitución de /g/ por omisión, consistente con patrón fonológico esperado para su edad. Se usó el protocolo Hanen para facilitar turnos comunicativos durante juego con burbujas. Comprensión auditiva evaluada informalmente: siguió 2 of 3 instrucciones de dos pasos.

Assessment: Camilo continúa mostrando progreso lento pero consistente en producción de vocabulario funcional temprano, con mayor generalización necesaria entre ambientes (casa vs. daycare). El contraste entre producción en casa y silencio en el salón podría reflejar ansiedad social o diferencias de exposición lingüística; se recomienda observación en Little Blessings Daycare antes de la próxima revisión.

Plan: Continuar sesiones semanales. Se enviará solicitud de observación escolar y se coordinará con Denise Alvarado para alinear con la visita trimestral de WIC programada para October 22, 2026. La familia también participa en el programa de lectura bilingüe en la Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Chatham los sábados, lo cual se anima a continuar como exposición adicional de lenguaje. Rosa preguntó sobre referir a audiología; se documentó nota para el Dr. Marcus Webb en UNC Health Chatham Ear, Nose & Throat – Pittsboro Campus para descartar pérdida auditiva leve, dado historial de otitis recurrente.

Próxima cita: October 13, 2026 a las 3:15 PM. Contacto de la familia: (919) 555-0148, rosa.ventura88@example.com. ID de Medicaid: 998271345B. Nota firmada electrónicamente por Alejandra Mejía, M.S., CCC-SLP, bajo contrato con Carolina Pines Pediatric Therapy Associates.

FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES

En las palabras de la familia / In the family's own words:

Lucía del Río shared, "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Teo no nos dice lo que quiere. Señala, pero no usa palabras. En la casa le entendemos un poco, pero en Rinconcito de Luz las maestras dicen que se frustra y a veces pega a los otros niños porque no puede decir lo que necesita."

Andrés Flores-Castillo added, in English, "He's a happy kid otherwise — he loves puzzles, he loves his hermano Sol — but we want him to be able to tell us 'quiero agua' or 'más, por favor' instead of just crying. Right now it's mostly crying o jalándonos de la mano."

Family priorities identified:
1. Increase Mateo's functional communication at home and at Rinconcito de Luz (bilingual vocabulary, requesting).
2. Reduce frustration-related behaviors (hitting, throwing) linked to communication breakdown.
3. Support the family in talking to Teo's pediatrician, Dr. Patricia Whitfield, about a hearing re-check, since colds this fall have caused some ear fluid.
4. Connect with Spanish-speaking playgroups through Smart Start of Wake County.

Resources: Extended family nearby (abuela Carmen Flores and tía Rosa Castillo both help with childcare); stable housing; both parents employed — mother at Cardinal Linens Services, father at Triangle Auto Glass; reliable transportation.

DAILY ROUTINES

Wake / Morning: [X] Home  [ ] Daycare  [ ] Other — Mateo wakes around 6:45 AM, eats breakfast with Sol and abuela Carmen Flores before being dropped at Rinconcito de Luz by 7:30 AM.
Daycare day: [ ] Home  [X] Daycare  [ ] Other — At Rinconcito de Luz, Teo is in the "Mariposas" room with lead teacher Sra. Yolanda Pacheco and assistant Sra. Dana Eberhardt; peer Jayden is his closest friend in the room, though staff report conflict over toys most days.
Pickup / Evening: [X] Home  [ ] Daycare  [ ] Other — Picked up by Lucía del Río or abuela Carmen Flores around 5:00 PM; family eats dinner together, then bath and books before bed around 8:30 PM.
Weekends: [X] Home  [ ] Community  [ ] Other — Family attends misa at Garner on Sundays; Mateo enjoys the playground behind the church with Sol.

OTHER AGENCIES / PROGRAMS INVOLVED

[X] WIC — Wake County WIC Program, office contact handles nutrition follow-up.
[X] DSS — open supportive-services case, not protective, coordinated by Wake County Department of Social Services for childcare subsidy.
[X] Early intervention community playgroup through Smart Start of Wake County (family placed on waitlist September 15, 2026).
[ ] Part C to Part B transition planning — to begin at next review per team discussion.
School district of residence (for future Part B referral): Wake County Public School System; home school expected to be Forest Pines Elementary once eligible, per district boundary lookup done by service coordinator.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT (Speech-Language, summarized from September 22, 2026 assessment)

Receptive language, per PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension subtest: standard score 76 (5th percentile), age equivalent 18 months. Expressive language, PLS-5 Expressive Communication subtest: standard score 71 (3rd percentile), age equivalent 16 months.

Mateo produced 8 intelligible words in English and 11 in Spanish during a 20-minute structured sample ([EW] codes applied for word-approximations), for a combined vocabulary estimate below the 10th percentile bilingually. He used single-word requests ("agua," "más," "arriba") with moderate cues and imitated two-word combinations ("más agua") 3 of 5 trials with minimal cues. Target sound /t/ was stimulable in isolation; /k/ was produced as [t] in word-initial position (""tasa"" for ""casa""), consistent with a phonological process rather than a structural concern.

Oral-motor exam unremarkable. Hearing: last screened March 10, 2026, passed, but family and daycare both report frequent congestion; re-check recommended with Dr. Patricia Whitfield.

Occupational Therapy summary (Marisol Ibáñez, OT, eval September 24, 2026): fine motor skills within normal limits per Bayley-4 Fine Motor subscale, scaled score 9. Behavioral regulation noted as an area to monitor jointly with speech goals.

Physical Therapy summary (Grant Olufemi, PT): gross motor age-appropriate; no PT services recommended at this time per Bayley-4 Gross Motor scaled score 11.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Mateo will request preferred items and actions using two-word combinations in Spanish and/or English (e.g., "más agua," "quiero arriba") across home and Rinconcito de Luz, in 4 of 5 opportunities across three consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Use PROMPT-informed cueing during snack and play routines; model bilingually, honoring whichever language Teo attempts first; coach Lucía del Río, Andrés Flores-Castillo, abuela Carmen Flores, and daycare staff Sra. Yolanda Pacheco on consistent wait-time and expectant pausing.

Outcome 2: Mateo will use a word or gesture instead of hitting or crying to communicate frustration, in 8 of 10 observed opportunities at Rinconcito de Luz.
Strategies: Introduce a small picture-based choice board (informed by PECS principles) for "more," "all done," "help"; Rinconcito de Luz staff to use the board during transitions; family to use a matching board at home.

Outcome 3: The family will report increased confidence supporting bilingual language development at home, measured by parent-report checklist at next review.
Strategies: Rachel Owens, SLP, will share Hanen-based strategies (self-talk, parallel talk) in both English and Spanish handouts; interpreter Héctor Jiménez to assist with any clarifying questions between visits as needed via service coordinator.

Outcome 4: Family will attend at least one Spanish-speaking caregiver playgroup session through Smart Start of Wake County prior to next review, to build peer support and community connection.
Strategies: Service coordinator Brenda Suárez to share playgroup schedule and assist with transportation questions if needed.

**Coordinadora de servicios y oficina del CDSA**

Su coordinadora de servicios sigue siendo Karen Phillips, del CDSA Foothills. Pueden comunicarse con ella al (828) 555-0142 o por correo electrónico a kphillips@cdsafoothills.org. También estuvo presente en la reunión la interprete de español, Ana Beatriz Reyes, quien nos ayudó a traducir durante toda la sesión.

**Lo que ustedes nos compartieron**

Durante la reunión, Lucía nos dijo: "Mateo entiende casi todo lo que le decimos en español y en inglés, pero cuando quiere algo solo señala o grita, y eso lo frustra mucho. Queremos que pueda decirnos 'quiero agua' o 'ayúdame' con palabras." Esteban agregó: "También nos preocupa que en la guardería no lo entiendan cuando intenta hablar, y que se quede callado todo el día."

Estas preocupaciones guiaron las prioridades que la familia estableció para este periodo:
1. Que Mateo use al menos diez palabras funcionales en español e inglés para pedir cosas.
2. Que la familia aprenda señas sencillas de apoyo para usar en casa mientras se desarrolla el lenguaje hablado.
3. Que el personal de su preescolar reciba estrategias para animarlo a comunicarse durante el juego.

**Rutinas diarias**

Mateo se levanta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con su hermano Joaquín antes de que Esteban lo lleve al preescolar El Arca de Noé Preschool a las 8:30 a.m.. Allí pasa el día con su maestra, la señora Dolores Camacho, y comparte salón con su amigo Benjamín, con quien juega en el área de bloques. doña Rosario lo recoge a las 3:30 p.m. casi todos los días, y en ocasiones su vecina y amiga de la familia, Griselda Montoya, ayuda con el transporte cuando doña Rosario no puede. Las noches son más tranquilas: cena en familia, baño, y un cuento antes de dormir alrededor de las 8:00 p.m..

**Otras agencias que apoyan a la familia**

La familia también recibe apoyo del programa WIC del condado de Catawba y participa en actividades de Smart Start de Catawba County. Lucía mencionó que están en lista de espera para recibir ayuda de Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Catawba (DSS) con el cuidado infantil.

**Resumen de la evaluación**

Administré partes de la prueba Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), versión en español. Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 72 en Comprensión Auditiva (percentil 3) y una puntuación estándar de 68 en Expresión Verbal (percentil 2), lo cual indica un retraso significativo en ambas áreas del lenguaje. También administré la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, donde mostró fortalezas en interacción y juego, pero limitaciones claras en vocabulario expresivo.

Durante la sesión, Mateo produjo de forma espontánea las palabras "agua" y "mamá", y logró imitar "más" con apoyo mínimo. En 4 de 10 intentos logró combinar un gesto con una aproximación verbal, por ejemplo "ba" para "pelota". Su pediatra, el Dr. Samuel Whitfield, confirmó que no hay preocupaciones auditivas ni médicas adicionales en este momento, y el código diagnóstico registrado es ICD-10 F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo). El servicio se facturó bajo el código CPT 92523.

**Resultados (Outcomes) y estrategias**

**Resultado 1:** Mateo usará al menos 15 palabras o aproximaciones verbales funcionales en español y/o inglés para pedir objetos, acciones o ayuda en el 80% de las oportunidades (8/10 ensayos), observado en dos entornos naturales.
*Estrategias:* usar modelado de lenguaje aumentado, ofrecer opciones ("¿quieres agua o jugo?"), y reforzar cualquier intento verbal, siguiendo principios de Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk".

**Resultado 2:** La familia usará al menos seis señas o gestos de apoyo (sistema tipo PECS adaptado en casa) para reducir la frustración de Mateo durante las comidas y el juego.
*Estrategias:* entrenamiento familiar en sesión, tarjetas visuales bilingües para usar en casa, y práctica guiada con doña Rosario durante las tardes.

**Resultado 3:** El personal de El Arca de Noé Preschool implementará al menos tres estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje durante el juego dirigido, con apoyo de consulta trimestral.
*Estrategias:* visita de consulta en el aula, modelado para la maestra Dolores Camacho, y seguimiento con llamadas mensuales.

**Fechas y horario de servicio**

Los servicios de patología del habla y lenguaje continuarán dos veces por semana, los martes y jueves a las 10:00 a.m., con sesiones de 45 minutos en el hogar de la familia. La fecha de la próxima revisión del IFSP será el 3 de marzo de 2027, y la evaluación anual completa está programada para el 14 de enero de 2027, coincidiendo con el cumpleaños de Mateo.

**Mi información de contacto**

Seguiré siendo la patóloga del habla y lenguaje de Mateo durante este periodo. Trabajo para Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC (también conocida como Carolina Bilingual Therapy, o simplemente CBTS), bajo contrato con el CDSA Foothills. Si tienen preguntas, pueden llamarme al (828) 555-0179 o escribirme a mvelasquez@carolinabilingualtherapy.com. También pueden encontrar información general sobre nuestros servicios en www.carolinabilingualtherapy.com.

Fue muy valioso escuchar directamente de ustedes sobre lo que más les preocupa, y espero que trabajemos juntos como equipo para apoyar a Mateo en su comunicación. ¡Está haciendo un progreso hermoso, y con el apoyo de toda la familia, incluyendo a Joaquín y a doña Rosario, sé que seguirá avanzando!

Con cariño y respeto,

Mariana Velásquez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje Bilingüe
Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC

Jesús Emmanuel de la Cruz-Fernández — Informe de Evaluación de Habla y Lenguaje / Speech-Language Evaluation Report

**Pt. Name:** Jesús Emmanuel de la Cruz-Fernández ("Chuy")
**DOB:** April 9, 2022
**CA:** 4;2
**Date of Eval:** June 12, 2026 and June 19, 2026
**Examiner:** Carmen Álvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (Eng/Span)
**Employer:** Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
**Interpreter:** not needed; CG is bilingual
**Referral Source:** Mecklenburg CDSA, case mgr. T. Singh
**Medicaid #:** 998271345K
**Record ID:** LD-04471
**Address on file:** 2217 Rozzelles Ferry Rd, Charlotte, 28208
**Phone:** (704) 555-0198
**Email:** lucia.fernandez99@gmail.com

**Razón de Referido / Reason for Referral**

Chuy was referred by Mecklenburg CDSA 2/2 parental and teacher concern for expressive language delay and ~unintelligible speech, esp. in Spanish. Su mamá, Lucía Fernández Ramírez, reports "no le entendemos casi nada cuando habla rápido" — CG states he is understood approx 50% of the time by familiar listeners and much less by unfamiliar listeners. Teacher at Pequeños Pasos Early Learning Center, Ms. Patricia López, noted pt. "mezcla" / mixes EN-SP within utterances and omits final consonants, w/ limited MLU for age.

**Antecedentes del Nacimiento / Birth & Medical History**

Pt. born at 35 weeks gestation at Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital, Myers Park Campus, c/s delivery 2/2 maternal preeclampsia. Birth weight 4 lbs 11 oz, Apgar 7/9. Admitted to NICU x18 days at same campus for respiratory support (CPAP) and feeding difficulty; d/c'd home w/ no supplemental O2. No reported hearing screen failure at birth (passed bilat.). Hx of 3 episodes of AOM (ages 11 months, 16 months, 22 months), tx'd w/ amoxicillin; no PE tubes placed. Pediatrician Dr. Sandra Kim at Novant Health Pediatrics – Steele Creek referred to audiology b/c of parental concern re: hearing. Audiogram completed March 3, 2026 at Novant Health Ear, Nose & Throat – Ballantyne by Dr. Walter Osei, AuD: results WNL bilat., no conductive loss at time of testing. No current ENT concerns; tympanograms type A bilat. No seizure hx, no genetic testing completed to date. Gross/fine motor milestones reportedly WNL per CG report (sat 6 months, walked 13 months).

**Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje / Family & Language History**

Chuy lives with mamá Lucía Fernández Ramírez and papá Rafael de la Cruz in a home shared at times w/ abuela Rosa Fernández ("abuela Rosa"), who provides childcare 3 days/wk while parents work. Rafael de la Cruz works 2nd shift at Compass Furniture Gallery; Lucía works part-time as a home health aide. Older sister Guadalupe de la Cruz Fernández ("Lupita"), age 7, attends Hornets Nest Elementary and is reportedly typically developing in both languages, often serving as "translator" for her brother per CG report — "ella le dice a la maestra lo que él quiere" per mamá. Paternal uncle Mateo de la Cruz ("Teo"), who lives nearby, is frequently present and described as pt.'s primary male role model given father's work schedule.

Language exposure: home is reported ~70% Spanish / 30% English, w/ mamá and abuela speaking primarily Spanish, papá and Lupita code-switching freely. Pt. attends Pequeños Pasos Early Learning Center M–F, 8:30 AM–3:30 PM, English-dominant classroom instruction w/ some bilingual staff support. Teacher Ms. López and asst. teacher Ms. Dawn Phillips both report concern re: intelligibility and peer interaction — pt. reportedly plays alongside peers but limited verbal exchange; classmate José Hernández ("Pepe") described as pt.'s closest friend at daycare, and neighbor child Juan Pablo Ortiz ("Juanito") is pt.'s frequent playmate at home, per report mostly nonverbal play (chasing, trucks). Family dog, "Canela," is reportedly a motivator during play-based sampling.

Prior records (reviewed, not generated at this visit) include a 2024 CDSA intake note co-signed by SLP initials "M.R." indicating "emerging bilingual, monitor"; no formal tx initiated at that time per CDSA case mgr. T. Singh.

**Procedimientos / Procedures**

Eval conducted over 2 sessions totaling approx 110 minutes in a combo of English and Spanish, following family's lead w/ code-switching matched to pt.'s own language use. Standardized testing was supplemented w/ dynamic assessment and language sample analysis given pt.'s bilingual status, per best-practice guidelines for emerging bilinguals (SPEC-aligned, non-biased approach). CG report (Lucía) and classroom report (Ms. López) obtained via checklist and interview. Behavior during testing: cooperative, mod cues needed to maintain attention across both sessions, occasional off-task behavior redirected w/ min cues.

**Resultados de las Pruebas / Test Results**

| Measure | Domain | Standard Score | %ile | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 (English) | Auditory Comprehension | 78 | 7th | below avg |
| PLS-5 (English) | Expressive Communication | 71 | 3rd | below avg |
| Preescolar de Lenguaje (Spanish, informal) | Comprensión | — | — | mod-sev delay est. |
| GFTA-3 | Articulation | 65 | 1st | sev delay |
| CELF Preschool-2 | Core Language | 74 | 4th | below avg |
| MLU (Spanish sample, 50-utterance) | — | — | — | 2.4 morphemes, below age exp. |
| MLU (English sample) | — | — | — | 2.1 morphemes, below age exp. |

Articulation/phonology (combined EN/SP sample): pt. demonstrated final consonant deletion (e.g., target "pato" → [pa]; target "cat" → [kæ]), stopping of fricatives (target "/s/" → [t]), and cluster reduction. Intelligibility rated approx 40% to unfamiliar listener, approx 60% to familiar listener w/ context. Stimulability fair w/ mod cues; pt. produced target /k/ correctly in isolation 7/10 trials w/ mod verbal cues.

Receptive/expressive sampling across both languages suggests delay present in both Spanish and English (i.e., not solely attributable to typical bilingual acquisition pattern or "silent period"), consistent w/ primary language impairment. Pt. followed 2-step directions 6/10 trials (mod cues), used mostly 2-word combos ("mas agua," "no quiero"), limited use of grammatical morphology in either language (e.g., plural -s, Spanish gender agreement errors noted: "la perro" for "el perro").

Oral mech exam: structure/function WFL, no overt feeding/swallowing concerns reported by CG at this time. Hearing: per most recent audiogram (March 3, 2026), WNL — recommend re-screen given hx of recurrent AOM.

**Impresiones / Impressions**

Chuy presents w/ a Developmental Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.9) affecting both Spanish and English, w/ a concomitant moderate-severe Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0). Delay is present across both languages per parent and teacher report and direct testing, which supports a primary language disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition variability. Hx of recurrent AOM and NICU stay are noted as risk factors but current audiologic findings do not explain the magnitude of delay observed. Family provides a rich, affectionate bilingual environment; Lupita's "interpreting" role for her brother, while loving, may be reducing Chuy's own communicative attempts and should be addressed in tx planning and caregiver coaching.

**Recomendaciones / Recommendations**

1. Individual speech-language tx, 2x/week, 30 min sessions, targeting both languages (not English-only), per bilingual service delivery model.
2. CPT 92523 (eval, speech/language w/ articulation) and 92507 (individual tx) recommended for authorization through Mecklenburg CDSA; case mgr. T. Singh to process referral.
3. Parent coaching (bilingual) 1x/month focused on expanding Chuy's independent communication attempts rather than relying on Lupita or Teo to interpret for him; brief written strategies to be provided in Spanish for home use by mamá Lucía and abuela Rosa.
4. Classroom consult w/ Ms. López and Ms. Phillips at Pequeños Pasos Early Learning Center re: visual supports and simplified directions; encourage continued peer interaction w/ Pepe using modeled language rather than gesture-only exchanges.
5. Re-screen hearing given hx of recurrent AOM; CG to follow up w/ Dr. Osei at Novant Health Ear, Nose & Throat – Ballantyne if additional ear infections occur.
6. Re-evaluate in approx 6 months to monitor progress across both languages; consider formal Spanish standardized battery if available at next review.
7. IFSP Outcome #2 to be updated to reflect bilingual expressive language goals; team review scheduled December 4, 2026, 10:00 AM, at family's home.

Report prepared by Carmen Álvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC, June 22, 2026. Copy to Mecklenburg CDSA, case mgr. T. Singh; copy to Dr. Sandra Kim, Novant Health Pediatrics – Steele Creek.
